A bright red flower ornament that symbolizes blazing glory.

Miss Guillotin sits in Snezhnograd 's central square, enjoying borscht outdoors and hot coffee spiked with liquor, just like a local. The coffee has barely been served before the frigid wind turns it cold, yet each sip still burns all the way from her throat to her stomach. Exceptionally perceptive as ever, Miss Guillotin immediately understands why the pointy-eared waiter recommended a double Fire-water. Getting from Fontaine to Snezhnaya takes Miss Guillotin no small amount of effort, with most of the journey spent crossing the snowfields. The weather is colder than she expects, though the roads themselves prove surprisingly manageable. It is this strange place that keeps slowing her down instead. She sees people leap bare-chested from trees over ten meters tall into snowdrifts, and children race across frozen lakes to see who can break through the ice and fall into the water first. Whoever suffers the worst luck wins, and is therefore the happiest of them all. She finds it even harder to understand than Alain's little stories about heroes slaying dragons. None of it seems to serve any purpose, yet everything feels wonderfully new. A few months earlier, she sat on a bench in the Court of Fontaine with a teacup in hand, watching through the damp, misty air as the building across the street was being renovated. She passed the time by pointing out flaws in the construction crew's work. Rather than taking offense, the man overseeing the project thanked her, leaving her with a favorable impression of him. She therefore allowed him to carry on with his unsolicited conversation. The man, who introduced himself as the president of some association branch, spoke in such a mild, measured tone that made her drowsy listening to him. Normally, it would have been a fine opportunity to rest. Unfortunately, since Alain 's departure, she always had far too much time to sit idle and doze, and had grown accustomed to handling trivial matters unrelated to her research while only half awake. For instance, the Palais Mermonia granted her an enormous sum in compensation following the death of Duke Alain Guillotin. She had no intention of sitting on the Mora like some miser until she died of old age. For one thing, she obviously never would. Nor did she wish to become the subject of some horror story centuries later about a haunted doll lurking in a basement. She heard that the bank nearby offered some attractive investment plans, but a bank from a foreign nation seemed like a trap in and of itself. No matter how highly the branch president beside her praised the bank for its generous support, it was not enough to convince the ever-astute Miss Guillotin. Then there was the question of how bread could possibly be as bitter as black coffee, or how a drink could taste like bread. Alain had carefully equipped her with taste and thermal perception systems indistinguishable from a human's, so how was she supposed to test whether they could continue operating reliably under prolonged exposure to low temperatures? The overly friendly branch president continues to entertain her with tales of adventures in other nations, occasionally slipping in a compliment or two. He claims that even the most well-traveled adventurers would rarely encounter a lady of such insight, and that merely helping to correct flaws in a building's design is hardly a worthy use of her talents. And so, Miss Guillotin sets down her empty teacup and decides to go try the drink that tastes like bread. At a table amid the ice and snow, she met the Director of the Fatui . At the time, she was wondering just how old the Podvorye truly was as she watched a Volkodlak, clumsier even than Pulonia , struggle to keep an entire tray of overflowing glasses level. Against this precariously balanced backdrop, the masked man spoke to her of an ideal that sought to save the world. He said that a fate devoid of reason was a shackle meant to be broken, and that to destroy the old world was to save it. Fate and salvation were both familiar subjects to her, yet now they felt somewhat pointed. Oh, Alain... she thought. You gave me a free and exceptional soul, but did you ever wonder what I might choose to do with it? Then again, she immediately reflected, that was never Alain's question to answer. It was hers, a question she would have to confront in her own life. The hero who wielded the holy sword and the dragon he was meant to slay, whether it deserved to be slain or not, it was a story of the past. And yet, the world was still waiting to be saved. Not long after, she came to be known as Marionette, or Sandrone, and took on the responsibilities that came with the name. In her spare moments, she returned to that familiar seat and gazed across at the Adventurers' Guild window. Behind it stood a receptionist named Katheryne , poised and graceful, seemingly untouched by even the fiercest winter winds and snow. Someone pinned a theater program to the nearby noticeboard, followed by a Fatui recruitment poster. The latter bore a scarlet flower, brighter than the actresses' skirts. It was a medal promised to those who would devote themselves to the cause. Ever since Sandrone learned of the Adventurers' Guild's deeper purpose in Snezhnaya, none of this strikes her as unusual. The Fatui's grand ideal is a voracious beast, and both talent and intelligence are vital to its nourishment. Sometimes, she feels as though she too is part of it.
A bright red quill pen, granted to the youngest blood.

In theory, aside from the Belyi Tsar who accepted divine authority bestowed from on high , no other fae bears any responsibility to care for humans. Evidently, however, that has never stopped some among them from longing for human life. As though roaming freely across the tundra offered them no pleasure, and only bundling up in heavy coats and struggling to kindle a fire were truly worth enjoying. In truth, Mirko was indeed one of those who chose to enter the human world. But he would never claim to love or admire humanity. He would only say that it was a remarkably farsighted decision. He was fond of observing the world and drawing conclusions from what he saw. For instance, examining a group member by member could be a complicated affair, but generally speaking, they could be divided into three categories: the youngest, the oldest, and the hopeless lot in between. Young fae, or young creatures of any other kind, tend to be very adaptable. They are often molded by their surroundings, then call it discovering themselves and finding purpose. Full of youthful fervor, they enlist in the military or devote themselves to research, doing their part to magnify the glory of Her Majesty the Tsaritsa . Once they pass an absurdly high threshold of age, however, they tend to adopt a different sort of noncommittal, go-with-the-flow attitude. When the Tsaritsa ascended the throne, for example, one of the first letters of congratulations she received came from the uninhabited reaches of the far north. Had it not borne the name of one of the princes, one might well have wondered whether its sender was still among the living. As for those in between, perhaps they refused to believe that His Majesty had truly perished in the calamity , or perhaps they could not accept that the crown had passed beyond the hands of their own kind. Either way, their stubborn fury did manage to blaze rather fiercely, if only for a little while. Mocking one's own kin would generally be condemned as despicable, but Mirko simply could not help himself. There was little point denying it. After all, among the qualities by which politicians are judged, despicable is a remarkably mild one. Combine it with foresight, and it instead becomes the virtue known as knowing which way the wind is blowing. After giving it some thought, Mirko decided to apply to join the Fatui . In fact, he would be disappointed if the Tsaritsa failed to see through his intentions. Assuming, for the moment, that the witch still counted as human, this organization of self-proclaimed fools had yet to make room for a fae. Mirko had no intention of dressing up his motives as a struggle for the rights of all fae. He merely reasoned that, if a new world was soon to be born, he had no wish to find that it held no place for him. The Fatui's response to his application was rather concise. "Mr. Mirko Radovidovich Veleshek," he read, "Please report to the Mayor." Mayor Ioanna Ivanovna also served as Speaker of the Snezhnograd Veche , and different observers naturally drew different conclusions from the arrangement. To outsiders, compelling a fae to bow his head and become the pupil of a human was Her Majesty's warning to the old order. As for "The Rooster," his willingness to endure such an indignity for a seat among the Fatui could be taken as either naked ambition or an admirable ability to swallow his pride. A far-sighted politician wouldn't rush to deny these interpretation. Ambition he certainly had, as evidenced by Speaker Ivanovna's high opinion of him making him a likely successor to her position. Indignities, meanwhile, he had suffered in no small measure. Ioanna Ivanovna was exceptionally skilled at weaving elaborate conspiracies while erasing every trace of her own involvement, and Pulcinella, perhaps on account of his short legs, initially struggled to keep up the pace. All things considered, Pulcinella had learned all manner of things from humans, useful and otherwise: loyalty and the sowing of discord, strategic mastery and the appearance of it, a foul temper and how best to conceal it. Thus was he able to preside calmly over the Veche while wishing he could drive a spear straight through Pantalone 's calf. Admittedly, he had been outmaneuvered when it came to lobbying the Adventurers' Guild . That was only to be expected when most of his own work was confined to Snezhnaya . Just you wait, he thought. That grinning madman might be the Guild's nominal president, but Pulcinella would not allow all its wealth and influence to fall into his hands. Humans had also left their mark on some of the Domovoy gentleman's habits. After Ioanna Ivanovna's death, Pulcinella found himself considering who might one day succeed him. The thought was rather absurd, since with sufficient caution, he could probably live until the end of time. Perhaps one day he would grow weary of it all, weary of devising new ways to deal with his oddly assorted colleagues. Yet the ideal the Tsaritsa had once laid before them aligned with the greater vision he held in his own heart. He would have to endure at least until the day that ideal was fulfilled, would he not? Of course, putting the matter of a successor out of his mind did not prevent Pulcinella from taking notice of a certain young man many years later. Ajax plainly lacked every quality required of a politician. For one thing, he had already chosen his master and had no desire to become anyone else's pupil. And if someone had to guide him, The Captain was clearly far better suited to the role. And so, just as Ioanna Ivanovna had once watched him, Pulcinella watched "Childe" grow. After one morning meeting, he discreetly broached the subject with Capitano, who was preparing to depart for Natlan . The very next day, Pulcinella spotted Tartaglia's beaming smile from afar. "Look! I just went to see The Captain off, and he gave me this..." Pulcinella recognized the object in the box at once. It was one of the quill pens issued to soldiers during the Fatui's earliest recruitment. Its color had not faded even after several centuries, proof that it had been carefully preserved all this time. Pulcinella nodded with a kindly smile. Like the future, passed onward from one hand to the next, this too was part of his foresight.
A bright red pocket watch marking the time allotted for a conversation.

Almost as soon as recruitment posters began appearing on noticeboards across Snezhnaya , Pulcinella had several quiet, comfortable rooms prepared for use as counseling rooms. "Counseling rooms" was what they call them internally. To everyone else, they were usually known as "meeting rooms" or simply "the little rooms," as though needing counseling were some shameful affliction best kept hidden. Then there was "the dark room," a nickname of uncertain origin that Capitano categorically rejected. At first, the Fatui trained properly qualified counselors to deal with all manners of problems. In practice, however, many soldiers were reluctant to open up to strangers. They preferred to turn to someone they trusted and, somewhere they would not be disturbed, speak of things they didn't want brought into the light. Or simply break down and cry. So the considerate Pulcinella relaxed the rules to some degree. Once a booking was approved, anyone could spend a few hours inside talking with a companion of their choice. The Harbingers were naturally no exception. Capitano once saw Lohefalter coming out from one of the rooms, dabbing at her face with a powder puff, with Pulcinella close behind, holding up her handbag. He had no intention of prying into a lady's private affairs, and the Mayor was a man who knew how to keep a secret. Neither of them ever mentioned it again. On another occasion, Capitano saw Dottore and Pantalone leaving that floor together late one evening, both grinning from ear to ear. As expected, Pulcinella soon gave them a furious scolding ("Those two could talk anywhere they wanted to! Did they really have to take up a shared facility?!"). He then announced that measures would be taken to put a stop to such behavior ("Tell whoever's in charge to reject those bastards' applications outright next time!"). Unfortunately, neither of them ever booked a counseling room again. With no chance to deliver the punishment he had prepared, Pulcinella was left to stew in frustration all over again. Capitano didn't know what to say, either. Later, he bought Pulcinella a bottle of good wine, though he never asked whether he ever opened it. When it came to private lives, Capitano was practically invisible. Whether he was present or not made little difference to others' casual chatter, unless the conversation became too outrageous. Everyone agreed that The Captain would never tell on anyone. At times, he felt like a walking counseling room, silently taking in every whispered secret. The chatter didn't bother him. After all his years of training, his own heart could sometimes be louder than any of his colleagues. Sitting in the counseling room, he felt as though he were a little room enclosed within another, and then another still... until his soul was squeezed into the very center, hemmed in from above and below, front and back, left and right. The meeting room was small, with heavy curtains drawn across the windows. This was not because Pulcinella had been stingy, but because of a theory that people found it easier to trust one another in close, warm surroundings. Capitano had no idea where the theory came from. After giving it some thought, he removed his helmet and gently set it aside. At the time, his face was not yet so horrific. It looked merely marked by more scars than most, wounds that stubbornly refused to heal, and in the dim light, the sight was not quite horrifying. The man who invited him to talk was a former student of his who had joined a special operations unit after completing his training. Capitano knew what happened to the man's squad and therefore had some idea of what he wished to talk about. They were sent to a remote region to quell a disturbance. It should have been a relatively straightforward mission, yet every survivor who returned was left deeply shaken. In the end, with no other options remaining, they were forced to call in Dottore. Only then was the situation finally brought under control. Capitano was present at the time and, feeling responsible for the men, asked, "What did you give them?" "This?" Dottore produced another unopened glass vial on the spot and generously handed it to him. "A potent sedative." The vial was still in his pocket. Hopefully, he would have no need for it today. The soldier across from him looked utterly exhausted. With his only remaining hand, he opened his pocket watch, closed it, then opened it again, as though checking that time was still passing. "I know many still don't believe it, but I swear, everything in the report is true," the soldier said with a bitter smile. "Those people never even heard of Her Majesty the Tsaritsa . They thought it's still the age of the Belyi Tsar . At first, they called us lackeys of the fae and four-eyed monsters. They threw water over us, claiming they would wash away our sins of apostasy and our false faith..." "Yeah, that was how absurd it all seemed at first! They didn't even have any proper weapons. Someone beside me were even laughing. Our squad leader approached them slowly and tried to reason with them. He told them that now is the age of humanity, that we no longer needed to..." "And then... then..." Capitano read the report. It consisted of accounts recorded after the survivors regained consciousness, followed by several notes Dottore had added after examining them. The locals had long been suffering from a virus-induced form of mass hysteria brought on by cannibalism. That, at least, was how Dottore had summarized it. The soldiers sent to suppress the unrest developed the same symptoms after coming into contact with the contaminated water. Their infections were less severe, however, and they could still be saved. Dottore later produced a new course of treatment. As he stood with his hands clasped behind his back, observing its effects, he looked almost like a real doctor. Perfectly reasonable. The doctor adjusted his glasses. The way he narrowed his eyes made him look strangely like someone else. They lived in a place so isolated and inhospitable that one could hardly expect them to have anything else to eat. Capitano sighed. He had no desire to waste time arguing with reasoning so cold, yet so correct. But whose throat had been torn open? Whose arm had ended up in whose stomach? Was that really something the word "reasonable" could explain? "Never mind." The soldier abruptly broke off, pulling Capitano from his memories as well. "The counselor told me that if I could one day recount everything that happened without getting upset, it would mean I was recovering. What a load of bullocks... Forgive me." He immediately lowered his head in apology, then glanced at his pocket watch again. "I only booked an hour. I don't want to take up too much of your time. The truth is... I came to say goodbye." After the soldier left, Capitano looked over the things he had left behind: a red flower medal, a quill and a bottle of liquor he had carried with him, a patched helmet that looked almost new, and a pocket watch that might have been left deliberately or simply forgotten. Capitano suspected that they weren't all belonged to the same person. They merely happened to be reunited here. "I'd like you to keep these, my lord," the soldier, having already decided to retire, said. "Or you could pass them on to those who come after me. I hope they'll be luckier than we were. Or perhaps... a little stronger." You shouldn't think that way, Capitano thought, though he never spoke the words aloud. In fact, those who can survive are already strong enough.

blocks.text: On the first night, he stood with his hands behind his back in a birch forest swept by biting winds. Flecks of snow clinging to his glasses were slightly more of a nuisance than those landing on his face, so he took them off and slipped them into his coat pocket. Contrary to what others might have thought, Zandik understood humans very well. First, the typical human being has two hundred and six bones. Most use their brains to think and usually feel fear when startled or threatened. Second, to be precise, he carefully included qualifiers such as "complete," "most," and "usually" in his description, thereby avoiding any potential objections based on individual outliers. Ultimately, his deepest understanding of humanity lay in knowing that its possibilities were limitless. On the second night, he sat beside a feeble campfire, sharing a meal of plants mixed with scraps of animal flesh with several villagers. A black-haired woman with a deeply lined face prodded at the firewood, trying to coax the flames higher. Zandik was certain she had no idea why doing so made the flames suddenly leap higher. She did it only because those before her had done the same and got the result they wanted, and so this unwritten method had been passed down from generation to generation. Zandik further concluded that she must be younger than her appearance suggested, and that the same was true of the others. Harsh living conditions invariably caused premature aging and bred resentment. This time, their resentment was directed at the cold, hunger, the fae, the higher-ranking fae, and the debased humans who submitted to them. Zandik had already been warned that this place held an exceedingly antiquated view of the world, which spared him the step of being surprised. Curiously, neither illness nor death figured among the villagers' grievances. Perhaps people instinctively struggled for as long as they lived, whereas in death, they spared everyone the trouble. Under such circumstances, a stranger appearing out of nowhere would naturally be perceived as a threat and frighten the locals. Fortunately, well-versed in human nature, Zandik came prepared: the animal scraps were his contribution. What a perfect place. Ice and snow sealed away all outside interference, forming a world within a world, each enclosed in its own shell. Human behavior remained primitive, while history itself had ground to a halt. This place should have given rise to even more possibilities. And when Zandik spoke of humanity's possibilities, he by no means intended the word as praise. Setting aside its connections to the outside world, a human brain placed in a water tank is no different from one housed within a skull. So long as the appropriate signals can be simulated, it will produce the predetermined response. As Dottore poured the experimental materials into the tank, a child's voice came up nearby. He asked, "Is that a butterfly on your bottle?" This child must be very curious to venture out on a night cold enough to freeze a person to death just to watch him conduct his experiment. If he had been a little more curious and ventured a little farther, beyond the birch forest, perhaps he could have gone on to live a much better life. To reward the child's curiosity, Dottore tossed him the empty bottle and said, "That isn't a butterfly. It's a four-eyed monster!" The child took a frightened step back, and the bright red bottle fell into the snow. The boy's fear was entirely as expected, so Dottore quickly lost interest and went back to what he had been doing. On the tenth night, the food and water in his pack had noticeably dwindled, replaced by detailed records of his psychotropic drug trials. The results were exactly as he anticipated, drug-induced mental control could work in either direction. Stimulation and sedation each had their uses, and whether applied to interrogation or therapy, both appeared to offer considerable profit potential. The experiments yielded fantastic results, but that also meant Zandik's time as himself was drawing to a close. Soon, he would return to the castle of Fatuus , become Dottore once more, and attend to matters of a somewhat more humane nature. "So far away," he thought with regret as he gazed in the direction of Snezhnograd . If only he could perform surgery on his own brain, then he could sit back and travel in comfort like everyone else.
A bright red helmet. Hopefully it has, once upon a time, protected someone.

Pantalone sits in the theater like a statue, with only his index finger showing any sign of life as it occasionally taps along to the music. Today's performance features neither a celebrated artist nor a renowned play, and plenty of seats below remain empty. Still, he comes and he sits alone. His doctor prefers him to spend his leisure time in public, where he has no opportunity to engage in anything detrimental to his health. Besides, in the private box reserved for the Fatui, he is unlikely to be attacked by anyone other than his colleagues. All things considered, it's nearly the best place he could be. The performers onstage sing of love and acceptance, but heartwarming tales rarely find much favor with audiences here. Not that the people of Snezhnaya dislike happy endings. Rather, before such an ending can be earned, the characters must endure trial after trial, giving voice to all that lies pent up in the hearts of those who inhabit these frozen lands. You must shatter the shackles of a decaying world and struggle onward, through forests and cold wind, before you can hope to glimpse the rooftops of a warmer world from afar. But that is not the end. This seemingly warm world is no home of yours, either. If you have no value and can do nothing but beg for compassion never meant for you, nothing will change. Even so, there is no turning back. That is the lesson he has learned: once the shackles seize you again, the chains only tighten. To break free a second time, all you can do is wait for an opening, even if it may lead you somewhere worse. He once touched on the subject in casual conversation. His birthplace sought to tame those who refused to comply through violence and confinement, while his friend's homeland chose exile instead. Even the same narrow-minded thinking could take different forms and give rise to different possibilities. At that, they both laughed, as though each took pleasure in the other's suffering. For the first twenty years of his life, happiness came only in fleeting moments, such as the day his mother sold him to debt collectors, or those times when he made a fortune off powerful officials and nobles and mistakenly believed he might have a chance to join their ranks. Make no mistake: he wasn't pleased with the price he fetched, nor with the fortune he made later. Rather, somewhere in his subconscious, he sensed his potential to appreciate in value (After all, how many people get sold twice in one lifetime? Ha). That woman finally found the chance to rid herself of the disobedient freak, but in doing so, she also gave him the chance to escape that frozen wasteland, a place even wild beasts wanted nothing to do with. From the makeshift life of his "foster father," he learned money could be made to multiply. The nobles in league with the criminal underworld lured him into a trap with the illusion of profit, but at the bottom of that trap lay a path to powers greater than the nobility themselves. And since every one of these bizarre turns of fortune came only after he stopped praying to the heavens, he began to question the established rules of this world all the more. It was only after he abandoned his reverence for the gods and cast his lot with the world's outcasts that he became eligible to be recruited by those very gods. Whether audiences would condemn such a horror story is anyone’s guess. Fortunately, he has no intention of sharing it. As the final song of the performance rings out, someone pushes open the door without warning. Only one person would be inconsiderate enough to interrupt someone enjoying the ending. If the newest Harbinger were here, the ensuing barrage of curses would make the disturbance twice as bad. Speaking of his new colleague, Pantalone finds her very interesting. She begins voicing her displeasure with every manner of procedure the moment she arrives, perfectly embodying the rebellious spirit expected of a Harbinger . Pulcinella 's attempt to use her to secure a share of the Adventurers' Guild 's profits has plainly failed. The girl would never heed the honeyed words of that hypocritical politician. Besides, her creations have taken on the burden of all that tedious reception work. Though he cannot appear too willing, Pantalone has nevertheless ceded to Sandrone the share that is rightfully hers, and done so in complete sincerity. It is only fair exchange, a principle he fully approves. Pantalone has spent much of the performance lost in thought, so naturally, he has little interest in its ending. He rises and turns to Dottore , who has evidently only just returned to Snezhnograd , and reads from his expression that all has gone smoothly. Some time ago, Dottore proposed a new idea for an experiment, and Pantalone happened to know the perfect place for it. This, too, is part of a fair exchange, and he fully approves.

That was a time when the gentle frost-light still lingered, a silver mirror unbroken, even as the golden realm had already fallen. In a single night, the glorious golden tower fell like a fig tree. Across the frozen northern plain, From the holy citadel to the ancient capital, dark blue crystal nails annihilated every last city with even the most minuscule sign of life. The once-praised apostle and the gods ' first messenger both vanished in the catastrophe. Those who survived by grace of being nowhere near the cities at the time could only cling to life amidst the freezing wind and snow. With no refuge left to them, they simply waited for destruction to find them in the hollow dark. This is the great extinction spoken of in later prayers. Halcyon prosperity turned to dust, And the gods remained silent, unmoved by cries, curses, or reproach. In the despair of that long night, only one celestial ruler shed tears for the mortals' pain. She was the mistress of the Frost Moon , queen of the celestial chariot and of light, a heavenly agent whose origin was one with that of the world. Moved by pity, and a deeper, unspoken wish, she heeded the survivors' prayers. According to legend, she spun gleaming threads from the silver glow to lead the displaced across the frozen plains. And where her tears, full of longing, fell upon the frost-covered soil of the far north, they blossomed into lilies that would stand eternal in the icy winds. The proud descendants of Hyperborea call themselves the " Frostmoon Scions " for this reason, To honor the divinity who, whatever her original intent, gave them a new lease on life.
An immaculate feathered accessory said to have been forged by the first Moonchanter herself.

That was a time when frost's gentle light had long shattered like a silver mirror, but when the new moon had yet to rise. This is the story of two sisters who, born defective products, were never meant to be blessed. In the moonlight, an undisturbed sanctuary for strangers, the fragile souls shared a single breath. In the brief moments between agonies, moments that should have been filled with joy, they huddled together, drawing what little warmth they could from each another. They had never seen their parents, and nor had they ever heard the wind whispering through the groves. The two of them had only their grandmother , and the only way they'd seen the world was through the pages of a faded storybook. Its brittle, yellowed pages, torn and tattered, revealed to them a world they'd never seen: There it was, a single white bird, a streak of grace, gliding beneath a perfect moon. As they admired the free creatures of the fairy tales, the two children made a promise to each other... One day, the two of them would fly together like the white birds in the vast sky. "Since the day we were born, it's always been just the two of us." "When the day comes for us to leave, let's live the rest of our lives together." Many years later, one of them broke their promise, leaving for a faraway place alone. But alas, this was no flight toward a brighter future, but a fall into a much darker night. With her went half the dream, and half the pain meant for them both. Aila , later to become the first Moonchanter, began to endure twice the torment from that day on. "So you lied to me all along as well... My older sister, the only one I ever truly trusted." "But I won't resent you... I have long lost hope for the sky beyond."
An immaculate timepiece that long ago ceased turning, along with the delusions of its former owner.

That was a time when frost's gentle light had long shattered like a silver mirror, but when the new moon had yet to rise. It was then that the great plan, carried through countless generations since the time of extinction, was on the verge of culmination. The bloodline, purified for over a thousand years, would at last give birth to the chosen one destined to reign over Elysium. The false sevenfold radiance of the high heavens would fall at her feet, and the bones of the earth would rise to follow her. For from her would spring union with the world, and from her would the first great cause be rebuilt. That was the sacrosanct duty that had been passed down to the daughters of the far north. So it should have been. So it should have been... But on a moonless, snowbound night, the girl chosen to bear the sacred heir met the boy from the northern realm , And in his eyes, as clear as a winter's day, she beheld a reflection of a self she had never known. This unfamiliar stirring was enough to make the holy woman turn her back on destiny for that young officer from afar. For this new feeling, this foolishness called love, she cut off her bloodstained antler-crown and cast it down upon the snowy earth. The fallen one, who had betrayed her own people, ultimately failed to fulfill her destined duty. She was captured by a spy sent by the mad monk and was soon to be returned to the homeland she was meant to love. But as she looked down at the officer by her feet, crimson pooling beneath him, she drew the dagger to her throat in one final, fatal kiss. And so, the woman who failed to bear the sacred heir was buried in haste, her death forestalling the prophecy. Fortunately, the leaders of every generation had long prepared for premature end of such a blessed lady. Lovia , the then-Archpriestess, swiftly turned to a lesser branch of the bloodline for spares. But the twin sisters born of this lineage were a pale shadow of the one they were meant to replace. Hundreds of years might now have to pass before another child of sufficient purity was born. Seeing the glory of the great endeavor slip from her grasp like dissipating dew, The antler-crowned Archpriestess, maddened by anguish and obsession, hatched a terrible scheme. Why wait for the thousand winds to sweep through several generations? If they were too impure, Their flesh and blood too weak to bear the radiance of true moonlight... Did the Frost Moon 's boon not linger faintly in all ███? Then let ███ purify their ███! Thus, in the name of flawless moonlight, the priestess committed an act so profane, That even the mistress of the Frost Moon would recoil in horror at the blasphemy...
An immaculate silver cup said to have been used in the bygone rituals of the Frostmoon Scions . Their modern rites have no need for such a vessel.

That was a time when frost's gentle light had long shattered like a silver mirror, but when the new moon had yet to rise. The descendants of the far north could no longer hear the divine teachings of the high heavens, and they were consumed by burning wrath, just like in the days of old. No one knew how to forge anew the marvel the apostle of the Golden City had revealed to their ancestors. Yet the ambitions of the exiled — the ambitions of mortals — were more unyielding than even those of the gods. Should one lose the reliquary that can overnight till ten thousand acres of fertile land upon the dark, misty sea of ice, Then pen wild oxen into the furrows so that one may conquer the tundra inch by inch with fire, hoe, and sickle. Should one lose the arrow that can strike down the gods and pierce even that false sky, Then forge the plowshare into sword and blade, and the sickle and hoe into spear and halberd, then let blood be the lantern that dispels the darkness. And should the authority of creation , gifted by the highest of angels , be broken, Then one must govern the proliferation of the countless generations that follow by the crudest, primordial means remaining, that is, through law. So it must remain, until blood thinned by disaster and exile is purified into holy seed, And mortal descendants are born as perfect beings, fully one with the world. The perseverance and determination of all living creatures would eventually overcome all calamity — or at least that is what they firmly believed. After all, those who have planned the future of their people rarely have to suffer the slings and arrows of their contempt. "Here, drink this pure moonlight, my beloved child, my most cherished child!" "Let it weave into your flesh and blood, so that you too may be worthy of the gods' grace." "Look to the apostle of the Golden City. How he drank bitter wine and fought for the freedom of his compatriots!" "Like him, you must embrace this joyous pain, for from it, perfection will one day be born." The two could no longer tell what filled the ancient silver goblet. But if the kindly grandmother said so, then it must also be the will of the gods. Yes, yes. All to sculpting perfection, to fulfill a wish that had endured a thousand years. For the sake of the prophesied Elysium and the king destined to descend upon the world, impurity and trial had first to be transcended...
An immaculate adornment created in imitation of the envoy of the grove's antlers.

That was a time when frost's gentle light had long shattered like a silver mirror, but when the new moon had yet to rise. The gods ' ancient blessing, like a lone spark on the vast tundra, eventually flickered out. As the heavenly moon passed from the sky, the earth that could not become the moon began to wither. The great deeds miracle workers did in years past had faded into vaporous prayers, and those prayers were now the silent worries of the masses. In those crumbling, moonless nights, even a holy woman of the purest blood, Was hard-pressed to weave the flowing light into a song that could move the world, as her ancestors once did. No matter how fervently the ancestors of the far north once vowed to follow their departed gods, Their descendants , mortals in this sublunary sphere, lived lives as fleeting as a flickering flame. In days long gone, when one could still behold holy women and Archpriestesses channeling the grace of the gods, People yet believed the new moon would one day arise from the shattered light. And so, when the last glimmer of grace had faded and miracles were no longer witnessed, The line between so-called faith and so-called lies in turn grew as thin and fragile as the morning mist. Legend has it that the antler crown of Moonchanters today was a gift from the Frost Moon at the moment of its obliteration. The silver tree was splintered, and bereft of white branches they might find, the priesthood pleaded for new coronals. Out of pity, the mistress of the moon wove holy crowns for them out of flawless moonlight, ones innate to their birth. That was why the last Archpriestess chose to forge her circlet from cold, pure iron. The young Lovia was just a priestess then, one who had never once witnessed a moonlit blessing, And she dreamed that such lies, that deceived others and oneself alike, could still bind the unfaithful believers together. Decades later, when the false antlered crown sank into the foul, corrupt blood, That which reflected in her eyes was still not the flawless moonlight, but the frigid night swallowed whole by her own shadow.

Aino is a playable Hydro character in Genshin Impact .
She is a child prodigy and the founder of the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop who created Ineffa and many other intricate machinery. She is an orphan and sees her creations and screws as her "family."
After reaching Friendship Level 6 with Aino, a Krumkake Bolt may be obtained through the character menu.

rows: Alyosha is an Electro character with both off-field DPS and healing capabilities. After his Elemental Burst is unleashed, he can also summon his hound companion Tugarin to the field. Alyosha applies Hunter's Mark to opponents hit by the last strike of his Normal Attack or Elemental Skill. For some time after, should he then hit opponents affected by Hunter's Mark again with the last strike of his Normal Attack, Elemental Skill, or a Tugarin attack, nearby active party members will also have their on-field ATK increased. After the Passive Talent "Awakened by the Baying Hounds" is unlocked, whenever Tugarin attacks the opponent, nearby active party members will also regenerate HP.

When his Elemental Skill is unleashed, Alyosha applies Hunter's Mark to opponents hit. Should any of these marked opponents then be hit again by the final strike of Alyosha's Normal Attack or Elemental Skill, or take a hit from Tugarin, nearby party members will also have their on-field ATK increased for some time. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Alyosha Talent Demo 1.mp4

When holding the Elemental Skill , Alyosha will also enter aiming state and lock in on opponents inside a target zone in front of him. He then fires at these opponents when the hold is released. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Alyosha Talent Demo 2.mp4

With his Elemental Burst , Alyosha summons his hound companion Tugarin which then periodically attacks nearby opponents. The area in front will also become a hunting ground which continuously absorbs the opponent's attacks and then deal Electro DMG to opponents who find themselves inside periodically. This hunting ground lasts for a short time. After the Passive Talent "Awakened by the Baying Hounds" is unlocked, whenever Tugarin attacks the opponent, nearby party members will also regenerate HP. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Alyosha Talent Demo 3.mp4

rows: Description Gameplay Notes Advanced Properties Attribute Scaling Preview Normal Attack Performs up to 6 consecutive spear strikes. Charged Attack Consumes a fixed amount of Stamina, dashing toward a nearby opponent and cleaving once. Continuously holding this button will cause Arlecchino to consume Stamina and engage in up to 5s of high-speed movement. Plunging Attack Plunges from mid-air to strike the ground below, damaging opponents along the path and dealing AoE DMG upon impact. Masque of the Red Death When Arlecchino has a Bond of Life equal to or greater than 30% of her Max HP , she will enter the "Masque of the Red Death" state, where her Normal, Charged, and Plunging Attacks will be converted to deal Pyro DMG . This cannot be overridden. When in the "Masque of the Red Death" state, Arlecchino's Normal Attacks will deal extra DMG to opponents on hit that scales off her ATK multiplied by a certain ratio of her current Bond of Life percentage. This will consume 7.5% of said current Bond of Life. Her Bond of Life can be consumed this way every 0.03s. When her Bond of Life is consumed in this manner, All Is Ash 's CD will decrease by 0.8s. Unlike all other Polearm users, Arlecchino's Charged Attack is not preceded by a Normal Attack. The third hit of Arlecchino's Normal Attack will pull enemies towards her. If Arlecchino wields any other polearm other than Crimson Moon's Semblance , her polearm will have a yellow scythe blade starting from the second hit of her Normal Attack combo. While holding her Charged Attack and during her high speed movement, she will sprout a red wing and be able to fly over the surface of water . Her Normal Attack AoE is increased during her "Masque of the Red Death" state. Arlecchino remains in the "Masque of the Red Death" state even if she is swapped off field and swapped back in, so long as her Bond of Life is greater than 30% Max HP. During the "Masque of the Red Death" state, the base damage of Normal Attacks is calculated as: ATK × ( Talent Multiplier + Masque of the Red Death Increase × Bond of Life Max HP ) {\displaystyle {\text{ATK}}\times ({\text{Talent Multiplier}}+{\text{Masque of the Red Death Increase}}\times {\frac {\text{Bond of Life}}{\text{Max HP}}})} The on-hit 7.5% Bond of Life consumption during the "Masque of the Red Death" state is multiplicative. Constellation Effects Constellation Level 1, "All Reprisals and Arrears, Mine to Bear..." : "Masque of the Red Death is further enhanced, the value of the increase is 100%. Additionally, Arlecchino's interruption resistance is increased when she performs Normal or Charged Attacks while affected by the Masque of the Red Death." Description Gameplay Notes Advanced Properties Attribute Scaling Preview Summons forth Balemoon Bloodfire, dealing Pyro DMG to multiple nearby opponents and performing a dash-cleave against one of them, dealing AoE Pyro DMG . Opponents hit by the aforementioned attack will have a Blood-Debt Directive applied to them. Blood-Debt Directive Lasts 30s. Every 5s, it will deal 1 instance of Pyro DMG to the opponent. Max 2 instances. This DMG will be considered Elemental Skill DMG. When Arlecchino uses a Charged Attack or her Elemental Burst, Balemoon Rising , she will absorb and clear nearby Blood-Debt Directives. Each Directive absorbed grants her a Bond of Life worth 65% of her Max HP . The maximum value of the Bond of Life she can be granted through Blood-Debt Directives within 35s after using her Elemental Skill is 145% of her Max HP. Using the Elemental Skill again during this duration will restart the count on duration and the limit on the value of Bond of Life she may gain from Blood-Debt Directives. When this skill hits at least one enemy , it generates 5 Elemental Particles . Blood-Debt Directive DMG does not snapshot and will be affected by changes in Arlecchino's stats after the ability is cast. Arlecchino obtains Invincibility Frames during this skill for the duration that she disappears. To absorb nearby Blood-Debt Directives, Arlecchino only needs to initiate a Charged Attack. The Charged Attack does not need to hit and may be canceled, such as by dashing. Arlecchino cannot absorb Blood-Debt Directives from Stormterror Dvalin . When absorbed, it will instead grant Arlecchino a Bond of Life worth 130%. A Bond of Life created in the aforementioned ways cannot exceed the original limit on the value of Bonds of Life obtained through All Is Ash ." | Description Gameplay Notes Advanced Properties Attribute Scaling Preview Normal Attack Performs up to 6 consecutive spear strikes. Charged Attack Consumes a fixed amount of Stamina, dashing toward a nearby opponent and cleaving once. Continuously holding this button will cause Arlecchino to consume Stamina and engage in up to 5s of high-speed movement. Plunging Attack Plunges from mid-air to strike the ground below, damaging opponents along the path and dealing AoE DMG upon impact. Masque of the Red Death When Arlecchino has a Bond of Life equal to or greater than 30% of her Max HP , she will enter the "Masque of the Red Death" state, where her Normal, Charged, and Plunging Attacks will be converted to deal Pyro DMG . This cannot be overridden. When in the "Masque of the Red Death" state, Arlecchino's Normal Attacks will deal extra DMG to opponents on hit that scales off her ATK multiplied by a certain ratio of her current Bond of Life percentage. This will consume 7.5% of said current Bond of Life. Her Bond of Life can be consumed this way every 0.03s. When her Bond of Life is consumed in this manner, All Is Ash 's CD will decrease by 0.8s. Unlike all other Polearm users, Arlecchino's Charged Attack is not preceded by a Normal Attack. The third hit of Arlecchino's Normal Attack will pull enemies towards her. If Arlecchino wields any other polearm other than Crimson Moon's Semblance , her polearm will have a yellow scythe blade starting from the second hit of her Normal Attack combo. While holding her Charged Attack and during her high speed movement, she will sprout a red wing and be able to fly over the surface of water . Her Normal Attack AoE is increased during her "Masque of the Red Death" state. Arlecchino remains in the "Masque of the Red Death" state even if she is swapped off field and swapped back in, so long as her Bond of Life is greater than 30% Max HP. During the "Masque of the Red Death" state, the base damage of Normal Attacks is calculated as: ATK × ( Talent Multiplier + Masque of the Red Death Increase × Bond of Life Max HP ) {\displaystyle {\text{ATK}}\times ({\text{Talent Multiplier}}+{\text{Masque of the Red Death Increase}}\times {\frac {\text{Bond of Life}}{\text{Max HP}}})} The on-hit 7.5% Bond of Life consumption during the "Masque of the Red Death" state is multiplicative. Constellation Effects Constellation Level 1, "All Reprisals and Arrears, Mine to Bear..." : "Masque of the Red Death is further enhanced, the value of the increase is 100%. Additionally, Arlecchino's interruption resistance is increased when she performs Normal or Charged Attacks while affected by the Masque of the Red Death." Constellation Level 3, "You Shall Become a New Member of Our Family..." : Increases this talent's level by 3, up to a maximum of 15. Columbina Hyposelenia is a playable Hydro character in Genshin Impact .

Known as the Moon Goddess of Nod-Krai , Kuutar to the Frostmoon Scions , and formerly The Damselette , Third of the Fatui Harbingers , she was born into an unkind world and cast into solitude from the moment of her creation. Once a wanderer of looping paths and fading memories, she found her identity through the bonds she formed and the quiet hopes she claimed as her own. Though she bears many names, to those closest to her she is Columbina Hyposelenia—and she prefers it that way.

When triggering Gravity Interference , Columbina gains the Lunacy effect, increasing her CRIT Rate by 5% for 10s. This effect can be stacked up to 3 times.

When characters within the Lunar Domain trigger Lunar reactions, they will gain the following effects respectively: Lunar-Charged : When the Thundercloud performs lightning strike(s) against a valid target, it has a 33% chance to perform an additional lightning strike. Lunar-Bloom : When triggering Lunar-Bloom reactions, the party gains a special Moonridge Dew . Up to 3 Moonridge Dews can be gained every 18s. Lunar-Crystallize : When Moondrift Harmony is triggered, every Moondrift has a 33% chance to inflict an extra attack.

When a party member triggers an Electro-Charged , Bloom , or Hydro- Crystallize reaction, it will be converted into a Lunar-Charged , Lunar-Bloom , or Lunar-Crystallize reaction respectively. Lunar Reaction DMG inflicted by party members gain a Base DMG increase based on Columbina's Max HP . For every 1,000 points of Max HP, the Base DMG of Lunar reactions is increased by 0.2%, up to a maximum of 7%. Additionally, when Columbina is in the party, the party's Moonsign will increase by 1 level.

Description Gameplay Notes If one of your party members is incapacitated while in the Nod-Krai or Frost Moon regions, Columbina will revive this character. The amount of HP the character will have upon revival is based on Columbina's Friendship Level . This effect can occur once every 100s. This effect does not trigger in Domains, Trounce Domains, or the Spiral Abyss. Additionally, Columbina appears to have a special affinity for certain animals who are influenced by kuuvahki ... Columbina must be in the active party and alive for this passive's effects to work. This applies to both the revival effect and the wildlife -related effects. If Columbina is the active character and is incapacitated while this passive is not on cooldown, she will revive herself. If a party member is incapacitated while this passive is on cooldown or unavailable, the revival will not activate even after this passive is available again. Like with Lauma 's utility passive , certain wildlife will behave differently if Columbina is in the party. This only applies in Nod-Krai, and will not work on the same creatures in other regions . Some creatures will have special interactions. A glowing symbol will briefly appear above them when approached. Blunthorn Rhino - These mine and retrieve nearby Rainbowdrop Crystals . Chic Badger - These dig up Fowl and Raw Meat (amount varies). Puffin - These follow the party around. Rimehorn Deer - These heal the party and fully fill their Energy meters. Wildlife in the " Other " category will not startle when approached. Pale-Furred Wolves will not attack when approached. However, they will do so if the player enters combat or stays near them for more than a few minutes. Unlocks exclusive dialogue with certain animal NPCs , such as Pavlov at the Lucky Spin minigame, the finch beside Richeza at the Vesnici Proleca Greenhouse , and the guard animals near Lyylikki . The following Talents are similar to this talent: Other Wildlife: Prayers for the Forest ( Lauma ) Tailing on Tiptoes ( Yaoyao ) Thought and Intent, Like Silken Scent ( Lan Yan ) Yoohoo Art: Silencer's Secret ( Sayu )

rows: Columbina is an off-field DMG dealer who enables her teammates to trigger Lunar-Charged, Lunar-Bloom, and Lunar-Crystallize reactions, dealing various types of Lunar reaction damage. After casting her Elemental Skill , Columbina summons a Gravity Ripple. She can accumulate Gravity whenever nearby characters trigger Lunar reactions or deal Lunar reaction DMG. Once Gravity is accumulated to its limit, different types of Lunar reaction DMG will be dealt. After unleashing her Elemental Burst , Columbina will summon the Lunar Domain, granting different buffs for the Lunar reaction(s) triggered, and increasing the Lunar reaction damage dealt by all characters within the domain.

After casting her Elemental Skill , Columbina summons a Gravity Ripple that continuously deals AoE Hydro DMG to nearby opponents. Whenever nearby characters trigger Lunar reactions or deal Lunar reaction DMG, Columbina will accumulate Gravity. When Gravity reaches its maximum, different types of Lunar reaction DMG will be dealt. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Columbina Talent Demo 1.mp4

rows: Description Gameplay Notes Unleashing her Elemental Skill Eternal Tides will immediately trigger an effect equivalent to the effect of Gravity Interference . This effect can be triggered once every 15s. Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam When Gravity Interference is triggered, if the Lunar reaction type that has accumulated the most Gravity for Columbina is: Lunar-Charged : Your current active character will recover 6 Energy . Lunar-Bloom : Your active character's interruption resistance will be increased for 8s. Lunar-Crystallize : Summons a Rainsea Shield . The Rainsea Shield's DMG absorption is based on 12% of Columbina's Max HP , and it will absorb Hydro DMG with 250% effectiveness for 8s. All nearby party members' Lunar Reaction DMG is elevated by 1.5%. As the appropriate Lunar reaction type of the instant Gravity Interference effect is not guided by the gradual accumulation of Gravity through normal combat, it is instead determined directly based on the Elemental Types of characters in the party. When there is a majority of Electro , Dendro or Geo characters (with a fixed tie-breaker priority in this same order), the instant Gravity Interference will behave as if that respective element's Lunar reaction type had accumulated the most Gravity.

Rate of accumulating Gravity increases by 34%. When Gravity Interference is triggered, Columbina will receive the Lunar Brilliance effect, which increases her Max HP by 40% for 8s. Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam : When Lunar Brilliance is active, if, during the current trigger of Gravity Interference , the Lunar reaction type that has accumulated the most Gravity for Columbina is: Lunar-Charged : ATK of your current active character increases. Increase in ATK is equal to 1% of Columbina's Max HP. Lunar-Bloom : Elemental Mastery of your current active character increases. Increase in Elemental Mastery is equal to 0.35% of Columbina's Max HP. Lunar-Crystallize : DEF of your current active character increases. Increase in DEF is equal to 1% of Columbina's Max HP. All nearby party members' Lunar Reaction DMG is elevated by 7%.
Increases the Level of Elemental Skill Eternal Tides by 3. Maximum upgrade level is 15. All nearby party members' Lunar Reaction DMG is elevated by 1.5%.

This effect can be triggered at most once every 15s. All nearby party members' Lunar Reaction DMG is elevated by 1.5%.
Increases the Level of Elemental Burst Moonlit Melancholy by 3. Maximum upgrade level is 15. All nearby party members' Lunar Reaction DMG is elevated by 1.5%.

For 8s after characters in the Lunar Domain trigger a Lunar reaction, based on the elements involved in the reaction, the CRIT DMG of the corresponding Elemental DMG done by all party members is increased by 80%. The CRIT DMG-increasing effects for the same Elemental Type do not stack. All nearby party members' Lunar Reaction DMG is elevated by 7%.

Verdant Dew: When party members trigger Lunar-Bloom reactions, the party will receive such a resource. Your party will receive 1 Verdant Dew every 2.5s for 2.5s after triggering a Lunar-Bloom reaction. Your party can have up to 3 Verdant Dew. If you trigger another Lunar-Bloom reaction during this time, the duration of this effect will be reset.
Moonridge Dew: A special Verdant Dew resource provided by Columbina's Passive Talent, Law of the New Moon. Its maximum capacity and duration are calculated separately from Verdant Dew. When the party's Verdant Dew is expended, Moonridge Dew will be consumed instead. Your party can have up to 3 Moonridge Dew.
Gravity Ripple: After unleashing Elemental Skill Eternal Tides, Columbina will summon Gravity Ripple . Gravity Ripple will follow the current active character on the field, while continuously dealing AoE Hydro DMG to surrounding opponents. Additionally, while Gravity Ripple is on the field, and nearby party members trigger Lunar reactions or inflict Lunar Reaction DMG, Columbina will gain the New Moon's Omen effect for 2s, continuously accumulating Gravity. 20 Gravity can be accumulated every 2s. You can have up to 60 Gravity, and it will be removed when the duration of Gravity Ripple ends. Once Gravity is accumulated to its limit, a special Gravity Interference will be triggered. Different effects will be triggered depending on the Lunar reaction type that has accumulated the most Gravity for Columbina. If the Lunar reaction type that has accumulated the most Gravity for Columbina is: Lunar-Charged: Gravity Interference will deal a single instance of Electro AoE DMG . This DMG is considered Lunar-Charged DMG. Lunar-Bloom: Gravity Interference will fire 5 Moondew Sigils at surrounding opponents, dealing Dendro DMG . This DMG is considered Lunar-Bloom DMG. Lunar-Crystallize: Gravity Interference will deal a single instance of Geo AoE DMG . This DMG is considered Lunar-Crystallize DMG.
Elevation: Special DMG Boost effect. It is calculated independently of other DMG Boost effects.
Lunar Domain: The domain that Columbina summons after unleashing the Elemental Burst Moonlit Melancholy. When current active characters are within the Lunar Domain, Lunar Reaction DMG inflicted by all party members will increase.

rows: Flins is an Electro DMG dealer who enables his party members to trigger Lunar-Charged reactions and who deals Lunar-Charged DMG directly with his Talents.

When Flins is in the party, Electro-Charged reactions triggered by characters will be converted to Lunar-Charged reactions, which summon a thundercloud. This thundercloud will continuously release bursts of lightning at nearby targets who are affected by both Electro and Hydro, dealing Electro DMG. This DMG can trigger CRIT Hits, and the DMG dealt is based on all characters who have applied elements during the reaction. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Flins Talent Demo 1.mp4

After Flins uses his Elemental Skill , he enters the special Manifest Flame form, which converts his Normal and Charged Attacks to Electro DMG that cannot be overridden by other Elemental infusions. In this form, he can also use the enhanced Elemental Skill . Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Flins Talent Demo 2.mp4

While Flins is in the Manifest Flame form, for a period of time after using his enhanced Elemental Skill , he can use a special Elemental Burst . When the party's Moonsign Level is at Ascendant Gleam and there are thunderclouds generated from a Lunar-Charged reaction nearby, the special Elemental Burst will deal additional instance(s) of DMG. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Flins Talent Demo 3.mp4

Illuga is a playable Geo character in Genshin Impact .

Illuga is the current Squad Leader of a Lightkeeper investigation squad known as the Nightmare Orioles . His past experiences dealing with the Wild Hunt has driven him to care deeply for every squadmate under his command and ensure they never face the same tragedies he once endured.

Description Gameplay Notes Advanced Properties Attribute Scaling Preview Light the lamp, dealing AoE Geo DMG , and gain Haunted Night's Oriole-Song effect for 20s. When this effect is active, Illuga gains 21 stacks of Nightingale's Song . When Normal Attacks, Charged Attacks, Plunging Attacks, Elemental Skills, and Elemental Bursts of nearby active party members deal Geo DMG to opponents, 1 stack of Nightingale’s Song is consumed to increase the DMG dealt. Increase in DMG is based on Illuga’s Elemental Mastery. If DMG is inflicted by Lunar-Crystallize , DMG dealt will increase further. When Geo DMG dealt in this manner hits multiple opponents, multiple stacks of Nightingale's Song will be consumed, depending on how many opponents are hit. Additionally, if there are Geo Constructs created by nearby party members on the battlefield while Illuga unleashes his Elemental Burst, or when nearby party members create Geo Constructs while Haunted Night's Oriole-Song is active, every Geo Construct on the battlefield will allow Illuga to gain 5 additional stacks of Nightingale's Song. When Normal Attacks, Charged Attacks, Plunging Attacks, Elemental Skills, and Elemental Bursts of nearby active party members deal Geo DMG to opponents, 1 stack of Nightingale’s Song is consumed to increase the DMG dealt. Increase in DMG is based on Illuga’s Elemental Mastery. If DMG is inflicted by Lunar-Crystallize, DMG dealt will increase further. When Geo DMG dealt in this manner hits multiple opponents, multiple stacks of Nightingale's Song will be consumed, depending on how many opponents are hit. Additionally, if there are Geo Constructs created by nearby party members on the battlefield while Illuga unleashes his Elemental Burst, or when nearby party members create Geo Constructs while Haunted Night's Oriole-Song is active, every Geo Construct on the battlefield will allow Illuga to gain 5 additional stacks of Nightingale's Song. Within 20s after unleashing his Elemental Burst, Illuga can gain a maximum of 15 additional stacks of Nightingale’s Song this way. When all stacks of Nightingale's Song have been consumed, or when the state's duration ends, the Haunted Night's Oriole-Song effect will end.
Nightingale's Song: The effect gained after Illuga unleashes his Elemental Burst Shadowless Reflection . It can increase the Geo DMG inflicted by current active characters.
Torchforger's Covenant: After unleashing Elemental Skill Dawnbearing Songbird or Elemental Burst Shadowless Reflection , other nearby party members will gain the Lightkeeper's Oath effect for 20s: For Geo DMG dealt to opponents, CRIT Rate increases by 5% and CRIT DMG increases by 10%. Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam Party members affected by the Lightkeeper's Oath effect have their Elemental Mastery increased by 50.

Ineffa is a playable Electro character in Genshin Impact .

She is a creation of Aino , serving as an all-utility maid and battle automaton created from various scraps from across the nations. Her core originated from Ix Raq'lapuj Chue'q Buluk , the Eleventh of the Thirteen Sovereign Lords , as the part of her who wanted to abandon her vendetta against humanity and find a new place to belong.
After reaching Friendship Level 6 with Ineffa, a Krumkake Bolt may be obtained through the character menu.

rows: Ineffa is an Electro support character who provides protective Shields for her teammates and allows them to trigger Lunar-Charged reactions.

When Ineffa is in the party, when a party member triggers a Hydro–Electro reaction, it will be converted into the Lunar-Charged reaction, and a thundercloud will be created. While the thundercloud is active, when enemies are affected by Hydro and Electro, the thundercloud will release bursts of lightning at them, dealing Electro DMG. Jahoda is a playable Anemo character in Genshin Impact .

An employee of the Curatorium of Secrets , a self-proclaimed legendary bounty hunter. A former member of the Seahook Gang , she was taken in by Nefer to be the only front member, to cover up Nefer's informants and activities under the Northern Intelligence Network .

Description Gameplay Notes Advanced Properties Attribute Scaling Preview Jahoda dashes toward her opponent, entering the Shadow Pursuit state upon contact. While in this state, Jahoda moves continuously and swiftly: If nearby opponents are affected by Pyro , Hydro , Electro , or Cryo , she will quietly convert her Purr-loined Treasure Flask to that element, gradually filling it. When the duration ends or the skill is used again, Jahoda drains the Purr-loined Treasure Flask and deals a single instance of Anemo DMG to nearby opponents. When the Purr-loined Treasure Flask is full, Jahoda immediately drains it, exiting the Shadow Pursuit state and dealing a more powerful instance of Anemo DMG . If her dash fails to make contact with an opponent, Jahoda instead drops a Smoke Bomb at her location, dealing a single instance of Anemo DMG to nearby opponents. Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam : When the Purr-loined Treasure Flask becomes full, Jahoda will not immediately discharge it. Instead, for a short duration, she steadily consumes the stored element inside and periodically fires Fluffy Meowballs at nearby opponents, dealing DMG of the corresponding element stored in the Purr-loined Treasure Flask. When a Fluffy Meowball hits an opponent, Jahoda regenerates 2 Elemental Energy . This effect can be triggered once every 3.5s. When the filled or unfilled Purr-loined Treasure Flask hits at least one enemy , it generates 4 Elemental Particles . Jahoda needs to be at least 4m close to the element-affected enemy to be able to fill the Purr-loined Treasure Flask. The Purr-loined Treasure Flask is quarter-filled every 0.5s , and draining it takes another 0.5s . Therefore, Jahoda needs 2.5s to fill the flask. Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam: The full Purr-loined Treasure Flask has 10 charges of Fluffy Meowballs, periodically firing every 2 second. Fluffy Meowball DMG has no Internal Cooldown . Constellation Effects Constellation Level 1, One More Flask! : "When a Fluffy Meowball fired by the Purr-loined Treasure Flask from the Elemental Skill Savvy Strategy: Splitting the Spoils hits an enemy, there is a 50% chance for it to bounce, dealing the corresponding Elemental DMG to nearby opponents." Constellation Level 5, The Greatest Treasure : Increases this talent's level by 3, up to a maximum of 15. Constellation Level 6, The Littlest Luck : " Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam : After the Purr-loined Treasure Flask from the Elemental Skill Savvy Strategy: Splitting the Spoils is full, nearby Moonsign characters in your party have their CRIT Rate increased by 5% and CRIT DMG increased by 40% for 20s." This passive grants Jahoda access to the Intel Hunt feature, which is only available to members of the Curatorium of Secrets . When Jahoda is near certain NPCs , her Elemental Skill will be replaced with a special intel-gathering skill. | Description Gameplay Notes Advanced Properties Attribute Scaling Preview Jahoda dashes toward her opponent, entering the Shadow Pursuit state upon contact. While in this state, Jahoda moves continuously and swiftly: If nearby opponents are affected by Pyro , Hydro , Electro , or Cryo , she will quietly convert her Purr-loined Treasure Flask to that element, gradually filling it. When the duration ends or the skill is used again, Jahoda drains the Purr-loined Treasure Flask and deals a single instance of Anemo DMG to nearby opponents. When the Purr-loined Treasure Flask is full, Jahoda immediately drains it, exiting the Shadow Pursuit state and dealing a more powerful instance of Anemo DMG . If her dash fails to make contact with an opponent, Jahoda instead drops a Smoke Bomb at her location, dealing a single instance of Anemo DMG to nearby opponents. Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam : When the Purr-loined Treasure Flask becomes full, Jahoda will not immediately discharge it. Instead, for a short duration, she steadily consumes the stored element inside and periodically fires Fluffy Meowballs at nearby opponents, dealing DMG of the corresponding element stored in the Purr-loined Treasure Flask. When a Fluffy Meowball hits an opponent, Jahoda regenerates 2 Elemental Energy . This effect can be triggered once every 3.5s. When the filled or unfilled Purr-loined Treasure Flask hits at least one enemy , it generates 4 Elemental Particles . Jahoda needs to be at least 4m close to the element-affected enemy to be able to fill the Purr-loined Treasure Flask. The Purr-loined Treasure Flask is quarter-filled every 0.5s , and draining it takes another 0.5s . Therefore, Jahoda needs 2.5s to fill the flask. Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam: The full Purr-loined Treasure Flask has 10 charges of Fluffy Meowballs, periodically firing every 2 second. Fluffy Meowball DMG has no Internal Cooldown . rows: Jahoda is an Anemo character capable of both high-frequency Elemental DMG and continuous healing. In battle, she can adapt to various elemental environments to deal different types of Elemental DMG as the situation dictates.

When Jahoda uses her Elemental Skill , she enters the Shadow Pursuit state and charges at her target. While moving, she fills her Purr-loined Treasure Flask based on the elements applied to nearby opponents. When the state's duration ends, she deals a single instance of Anemo DMG to nearby opponents. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Jahoda Talent Demo 1.mp4

When the Purr-loined Treasure Flask is full, if the party's Moonsign is at least Ascendant Gleam, Jahoda will continuously consume the elements stored in her flask to periodically attack nearby opponents, dealing damage of the corresponding element. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Jahoda Talent Demo 2.mp4

When Jahoda uses her Elemental Burst , she deals a single instance of Anemo DMG to nearby opponents and deploys two Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots, which continuously restore HP to the party's current active character. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Jahoda Talent Demo 3.mp4

If the party's Moonsign is at least Ascendant Gleam, the robots will switch their attributes based on the elements applied to nearby opponents, while continuously dealing the corresponding Elemental DMG to surrounding opponents. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Jahoda Talent Demo 4.mp4

Purr-loined Treasure Flask: A small elemental vessel that Jahoda retrieves after casting her Elemental Skill Savvy Strategy: Splitting the Spoils. While Jahoda is in the Shadow Pursuit state, if nearby opponents are affected by Pyro , Hydro , Electro , or Cryo , the Purr-loined Treasure Flask will convert to that element and begin filling up. The order of priority that determines which element will be converted to is: Pyro , Hydro , Electro , then Cryo . After each use of her Elemental Skill, the Purr-loined Treasure Flask can undergo one such conversion. When the Purr-loined Treasure Flask is full, Jahoda immediately drains it, exiting the Shadow Pursuit state and dealing a single instance of Anemo DMG to nearby opponents. Each time the Elemental Skill is cast, Jahoda takes out a brand-new Purr-loined Treasure Flask. Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam : When the Purr-loined Treasure Flask becomes full, Jahoda will not immediately discharge it. Instead, for a short duration, she steadily consumes the stored element inside and periodically fires Fluffy Meowballs at nearby opponents, dealing DMG of the corresponding element stored in the Purr-loined Treasure Flask.
Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots: One of the gadgets that Jahoda — a former treasure hunter — carries around with her. It is deployed upon using her Elemental Burst Hidden Aces: Seven Tools of the Hunter. Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots continuously restore HP to your active character. If the healed character's HP is above 70%, they also restore HP to the nearby party member with the lowest HP. Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam : If nearby opponents are affected by Pyro , Hydro , Electro , or Cryo , Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots will convert to that element. The order of priority that determines which element will be converted to is: Pyro , Hydro , Electro , then Cryo . After each deployment, a Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robot can undergo one such conversion. After converting, the Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robot will periodically attack up to 3 nearby opponents, dealing damage of the corresponding element.

Lauma is a playable Dendro character in Genshin Impact .

As the Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions , Lauma is a well-respected and wise figure within the group, and trusted by all manners of wildlife. She is immeasurably kind and seeks to find a calm resolution to any conflict; though her steel will reveal itself should people mistake her benevolence for acquiescence.

Each point of Elemental Mastery Lauma has will give her the following bonuses: DMG dealt by her Elemental Skill is increased by 0.04%. The maximum increase obtainable this way is 32%. The cooldown of her Charged Attack Spirit Envoy Metamorphosis is reduced by 0.02%. The maximum reduction obtainable this way is 20%.

When a Bloom reaction is triggered by a party member, it will be converted into the Lunar-Bloom reaction, with every point of Elemental Mastery that Lauma has increasing Lunar-Bloom's Base DMG by 0.0175%, up to a maximum of 14%. Additionally, when Lauma is in the party, the party's Moonsign will increase by 1 level.

Description Gameplay Notes Preview Displays the location of nearby resources unique to Nod-Krai on the mini-map . Additionally, Lauma appears to have a special affinity with some small animals affected by kuuvahki ... Lauma must be in the active party for Prayers for the Forest to take effect. She does not need to be alive to locate local specialties, but does need to be alive to enable the passive's wildlife-related effects. Only one local specialty will be shown on the mini-map at a time. Certain wildlife will behave differently if Lauma is in the party. This only applies in Nod-Krai, and will not work on the same creatures in other regions . Some creatures will have special interactions. A glowing symbol will briefly appear above them when approached. Blunthorn Rhino - These mine and retrieve nearby Rainbowdrop Crystals . Chic Badger - These dig up Fowl and Raw Meat (amount varies). Puffin - These follow the party around. Rimehorn Deer - These heal the party and fully fill their Energy meters. Wildlife in the " Other " category will not startle when approached. Pale-Furred Wolves will not attack when approached. However, they will do so if the player enters combat or stays near them for more than a few minutes. Unlocks exclusive dialogue with certain animal NPCs , such as Pavlov at the Lucky Spin minigame, the finch beside Richeza at the Vesnici Proleca Greenhouse , and the guard animals near Lyylikki . The following Talents are similar to this talent: Nod-Krai Local Specialty: A Light in the Dark ( Flins ) Miniaturized Detection Sensor ( Aino ) Prayers for the Forest ( Lauma ) Other Wildlife: Prayers for the Forest ( Lauma ) Tailing on Tiptoes ( Yaoyao ) Thought and Intent, Like Silken Scent ( Lan Yan ) Yoohoo Art: Silencer's Secret ( Sayu )

Elevation: Special DMG Boost effect. It is calculated independently of other DMG Boost effects.
Frostgrove Sanctuary: A magical array that protects the Moonchanters and can be summoned by using the Elemental Skill Runo: Dawnless Rest of Karsikko. The Frostgrove Sanctuary will follow the active character, dealing a single instance of AoE Dendro DMG to opponents within the array every 2s. This DMG is considered Elemental Skill DMG.
Verdant Dew: When party members trigger Lunar-Bloom reactions, the party will receive such a resource. Your party will receive 1 Verdant Dew every 2.5s for 2.5s after triggering a Lunar-Bloom reaction. Your party can have up to 3 Verdant Dew. If you trigger another Lunar-Bloom reaction during this time, the duration of this effect will be reset.
Moon Song: A melody used to weave together hymns. When an Elemental Burst is used, or for a period of time after an Elemental Burst has been used, it can be converted into Pale Hymn stacks that increase the DMG from Bloom, Hyperbloom, Burgeon, and Lunar-Bloom reactions. When Lauma consumes Verdant Dew to perform the Hold version of her Elemental Skill Runo: Dawnless Rest of Karsikko, each Verdant Dew consumed will provide Lauma with 1 stack of Moon Song.
Pale Hymn: A hymn passed down by generations of Moonchanters that increases the DMG dealt by Bloom, Hyperbloom, Burgeon, and Lunar-Bloom reactions. Lauma can gain Pale Hymn stacks in the following ways: When using her Elemental Burst Runo: All Hearts Become the Beating Moon. When consuming Moon Song stacks due to using her Elemental Burst Runo: All Hearts Become the Beating Moon. When the Frostgrove Sanctuary triggers the effect of her Constellation "I Offer Blood and Tears to the Moonlight". When party members deal Bloom, Hyperbloom, Burgeon, or Lunar-Bloom DMG, 1 stack of Pale Hymn will be consumed and the DMG dealt will be increased based on Lauma's Elemental Mastery. If this DMG hits multiple opponents at once, then multiple stacks of Pale Hymn will be consumed, depending on how many opponents are hit. The duration for each stack of Pale Hymn is counted independently.

Linnea is a playable Geo character in Genshin Impact .

Raised among humans as one of the last Snowland Fae in Nod-Krai, as well as one of the last Augury Birds in existence, Linnea currently works as an advisor to the Adventurers' Guild and as a naturalist.
Upon obtaining Linnea, the Gadget Linnea's Naturalist Archive may be obtained through the character menu, which includes the badge Unadorned and companion Companion: Exclusive .
