Description Gameplay Notes Advanced Properties Attribute Scaling Preview Adventure with Lumi! Depending on how you Tap, Lumi attacks in different forms. Tap Lumi strikes in a Super Power Form , attacking nearby enemies continuously, dealing AoE Geo DMG . If there are Moondrifts nearby, Lumi will also deal AoE Geo DMG to nearby enemies, which will be considered Lunar-Crystallize Reaction DMG. Continuous Tapping Time to show what we're really capable of! After using her Elemental Skill, Linnea will feed Lumi sparkling gemstones when her Elemental Skill or Normal Attack is Tapped repeatedly. A full-bellied Lumi will strike in her Ultimate Power Form , dealing an especially powerful instance of AoE Geo DMG that is considered Lunar-Crystallize Reaction DMG, switching to Standard Power Form . Additionally, tapping the Elemental Skill increases Linnea's interruption resistance . Linnea's Elemental Skill must be tapped 5 times in quick succession to activate Lumi's Ultimate Power Form. Tapping 2-4 times is functionally identical to tapping one time. Using Linnea's Elemental Skill or Burst while Lumi is already on the field will refresh her duration (25 seconds). Lumi's attack frequency varies based on her form: In Super Power Form, she will use Pound-Pound Pummeler every ~2 seconds, and Heavy Overdrive Hammer every ~5 seconds (if there are Moondrifts nearby). Lumi will use Heavy Overdrive Hammer immediately after Moondrifts appear nearby. If Moondrifts are already on the field when Lumi is summoned in Super Power Form, her first attack will be Heavy Overdrive Hammer. In Standard Power Form, Lumi will use Pound-Pound Pummeler every ~5 seconds. Lumi will not immediately generate Elemental Particles when summoned. Instead, she will generate 3 particles occasionally when she hits an enemy with an attack. In Super Power Form, Lumi will generate particles on her first attack. Then: If her first attack was Pound-Pound Pummeler, she will generate particles on every 4th Pound-Pound Pummeler attack afterwards. If her first attack was Heavy Overdrive Hammer, she will generate particles on every 2nd Heavy Overdrive Hammer attack afterwards. In Ultimate Power Form, Lumi will generate particles upon using Million Ton Crush. Then, after switching to Standard Power Form, she will generate particles on her 3rd and 5th attack. In Co-Op Mode , only one instance of Lumi summoned by Linnea's Elemental Skill or Elemental Burst can exist at a time. The last player to summon Lumi will replace the already existing instance. Linnea will increase the Elemental Mastery of certain characters in your party according to your current active character. Increase in Elemental Mastery is based on 5% of Linnea's DEF . If your current active character: Is a Moonsign character: Increase this character's Elemental Mastery. Is not a Moonsign character: Increase Linnea's own Elemental Mastery.

When a party member triggers a Hydro Crystallize reaction, it will be converted into the Lunar-Crystallize reaction, with every 100 DEF that Linnea has increasing Lunar-Crystallize's Base DMG by 0.7%, up to a maximum of 14%. Additionally, when Linnea is in the party, the party's Moonsign will increase by 1 level.

Description Gameplay Notes When Linnea is not in combat, the charge time of her Aimed Shot is greatly decreased, and she will shoot an Ultra Convenient Quick Arrow instead. Different effects will occur depending on the targets hit: Specific animals: Ultra Convenient Quick Arrow will be transformed into a special "Net" that can capture the essence and form of these animals, using them as a medium to manifest the animal's physical form again. The "Net" can only be used for a limited number of times each week. Ore veins used in forging : Linnea will dispatch Lumi, who will quickly strike at the ore marked by the Ultra Convenient Quick Arrow, then collect the dislodged ore. If Lumi is not on the field, Linnea will summon her for a short duration to help obtain the ore. The DMG dealt to opponents by Linnea's Ultra Convenient Quick Arrow is reduced to 20% of her original Charged Arrow. Additionally, after firing a certain number of Ultra Convenient Quick Arrows within a short period of time, Linnea needs to take a temporary break before she can continue using them. The Ultra Convenient Quick Arrow has a charge time reduction of ? %. The Ultra Convenient Quick Arrow can go through and hit entities within Thunder Barriers . The Ultra Convenient Quick Arrow acts like an Omni-Ubiquity Net when it hits animals that can be captured by it. However, animals caught this way do not count toward the Zoo Tycoon achievements. The Ultra Convenient Quick Arrow can only be successfully used as such 5 times per week. Afterward, all would-be successful uses act as failed uses of the Omni-Ubiquity Net (creatures are startled but not killed) and will trigger the following dialogue: Media:vo linnea talents 01.ogg I'm all out of nets... Better call it a week! Upon successfully capturing an animal, the following text will appear on-screen: Come along, little one! Lumi will only be dispatched to mine ore if the Ultra Convenient Quick Arrow hits an ore used in forging (these ores are also the ones marked by other Utility Passives that they say mark ores used in forging). She will likewise only instantly mine such ores. Lumi will neither be dispatched for nor instantly mine any other Geo objects, such as Local Specialties or the rocks encasing Geograna . However, Lumi can still deal damage to them if they are near an ore that is marked with the Ultra Convenient Quick Arrow. Lumi will only be dispatched for an ore marked with the Ultra Convenient Quick Arrow if the player if within ? m of it. The Ultra Convenient Quick Arrow will only mark an ore for a maximum of 8 [ verification needed ] seconds. Only one ore can be marked at a time by the Ultra Convenient Quick Arrow. In Co-Op Mode , Lumi only collects ores for the player who dispatched her. Ores for other players are also not grouped, despite the animation. If the Ultra Convenient Quick Arrow hits a target that can be marked or captured (even if unsuccessful), then it will not deal damage. Ultra Convenient Quick Arrows are charged if Linnea begins charging her Charged Attack outside of combat. If Linnea begins charging while in combat and then leaves combat without having fired the arrow she was charging, then that arrow will be a normal Charged Attack when it is fired, even if it is fully charged, and even if it finished charging outside of combat. Likewise, if Linnea begins charging outside of combat and then fires that arrow after entering combat, the arrow will still be an Ultra Convenient Quick Arrow. Lumi collects the ores in real time, matching the animation. The player still has the option of collecting ores manually before Lumi collects them. If Linnea dies or is swapped out of the party before all ores are collected, Lumi is immediately despawned and the player must manually collect the remaining ores, including any ores that were on their way to Lumi when she despawned.

Lumi: Strike Forms: Lumi has three different Strike Forms. Super Power Form Lumi will use Pound-Pound Pummeler to attack nearby opponents continuously. Every attack will deal 2 instances of AoE Geo DMG . If there are Moondrifts nearby, Lumi will alternate between Pound-Pound Pummeler and Heavy Overdrive Hammer to continuously attack nearby opponents . Heavy Overdrive Hammer will deal AoE Geo DMG which will be considered Lunar-Crystallize Reaction DMG. Ultimate Power Form Lumi will use the ultimate Million Ton Crush, dealing an especially powerful instance of AoE Geo DMG that is considered Lunar-Crystallize Reaction DMG, switching to Standard Power Form. Standard Power Form It might not be as flashy as the other forms, but it still packs a serious punch. Lumi will use Pound-Pound Pummeler at longer intervals to attack nearby opponents continuously. Every attack will deal 2 instances of AoE Geo DMG .
Elevation: Special DMG Boost effect. It is calculated independently of other DMG Boost effects.

Description Gameplay Notes Gains 25% more rewards when dispatched on a Nod-Krai Expedition for 20 hours. Additionally, as the head of the Curatorium of Secrets , Nefer seemingly has the ability to obtain intelligence from a variety of sources — intelligence that certain factions in Nasha Town might find extremely interesting... This passive grants Nefer access to the Intel Hunt feature, which is only available to members of the Curatorium of Secrets . When Nefer is near certain NPCs , her Elemental Skill will be replaced with a special intel-gathering skill. Using it on these NPCs will reveal additional information about them and potentially unlock exclusive dialogue and/or quests . For each NPC, gathering intel from them for the first time will reward Recorded Intel ×1 . Recorded Intel can be exchanged with Katheryne to unlock Intel Quests . The intel-gathering skill has a fixed cooldown of 8.5 seconds, but uses Nefer's standard Elemental Skill animation. rows: Nefer is a Dendro DMG dealer who enables her party members to trigger Lunar-Bloom reactions and who can consume Verdant Dew created by Lunar-Bloom reactions to deal Lunar-Bloom DMG.

When Nefer is in the party, Bloom reactions triggered by party members are converted to Lunar-Bloom, which provides the party with valuable Verdant Dew on top of the standard reaction effects. Nefer herself and certain characters can utilize their Talents or consume Verdant Dew to deal Lunar-Bloom DMG to opponents. This DMG can trigger CRIT Hits. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Nefer Talent Demo 1.mp4

After Nefer uses her Elemental Skill , she will enter a special Shadow Dance state. While in this state, Nefer can consume Verdant Dew and Hold the attack button to initiate Phantasm Performance, dealing massive Lunar-Bloom DMG to opponents. After some time, or after initiating a maximum of 3 Phantasm Performances, Nefer will exit the Shadow Dance state. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Nefer Talent Demo 2.mp4

When the party's Moonsign Level is Ascendant Gleam, Nefer's Elemental Skill will cause nearby Dendro Cores to be converted into Seeds of Deceit. For a certain time thereafter, all nearby characters will instead generate Seeds of Deceit when triggering Lunar-Bloom reactions. When Nefer finishes charging her Charged Attacks, she will absorb nearby Seeds within a set AoE, which will grant her Veil of Falsehood effects, increasing Phantasm Performance DMG. The party's Moonsign is Ascendant Gleam by default during Nefer's character trial. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Nefer Talent Demo 3.mp4

Nefer's Elemental Burst deals AoE Dendro DMG and consumes all Veil of Falsehood effects to increase this Elemental Burst instance's DMG. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Nefer Talent Demo 4.mp4

Your party will receive 1 Verdant Dew every 2.5s for 2.5s after triggering a Lunar-Bloom reaction. Your party can have up to 3 Verdant Dew. If you trigger another Lunar-Bloom reaction during this time, the duration of this effect will be reset.
Phantasm Performance: When in the Shadow Dance state caused by her Elemental Skill Senet Strategy: Dance of a Thousand Nights, if you have at least 1 Verdant Dew, Nefer's Charged Attacks will be replaced with the special Charged Attack Phantasm Performance, which will not consume Stamina. Nefer summons shades of herself to perform Coordinated Attacks against enemies. Nefer and the shades will deal 2 and 3 stages of AoE Dendro DMG respectively. DMG dealt by the shades is considered Lunar-Bloom DMG. 1 Verdant Dew will be consumed the first time shades are summoned after every Phantasm Performance.
Veil of Falsehood: After absorbing Seeds of Deceit via the Ascension Talent A Wager of Moonlight, Nefer gains this effect, thereby increasing the DMG dealt by her Phantasm Performance. Each stack of Veil of Falsehood increases the DMG dealt by Nefer's Phantasm Performance by 8%. The initial maximum number of stacks is 3, with each stack lasting for 9s (each stack's duration is counted independently).
Elevation: Special DMG Boost effect. It is calculated independently of other DMG Boost effects.

Odette Spessiva is a playable Cryo character in Genshin Impact .

As the Prima Ballerina of the Korolevskiy Troupe , she dances with a frosty demeanor and unwavering precision. Beyond the stage, she works as a member of the Fatui , and is known to be the favored candidate to inherit the Harbinger seat of her mentor, Signora .

Description Gameplay Notes For every 100 ATK Odette has over 1,000, her Stellar Glimmer DMG is additionally increased by 1.5% of the original DMG. She can deal up to 30% more additional DMG in this way. The DMG increase increases the Base DMG Multiplier directly, and is not a Reaction Base DMG Bonus . Consequently, it only applies to Stellar Glimmer DMG dealt directly by Odette, and not any indirect Stellar Glimmer reaction DMG she contributes to.

Odette will enter the Radiance: Stellar-Conduct state when she is inside a Polestar Field , or the Radiance: Stellar Swirl state for 8s after a nearby party member triggers a Stellar Swirl reaction. When a party member triggers a Superconduct or Cryo Swirl reaction, it becomes a Stellar-Conduct or Stellar Swirl reaction instead, and the Base DMG of said reaction is also increased by 0.7% for every 100 points of Odette's ATK. A maximum increase of 14% can be obtained in this way.

Description Gameplay Notes Preview Shows the locations of Snezhnaya's Local Specialties on the mini-map . Practicing dance in one's spare time might even trigger other effects... Odette must be in the active party for Echo of Winter Daydreams to take effect, but she does not need to be alive. Only one local specialty will be shown on the mini-map at a time. The following Talent is identical to this talent: Treetop Watch ( Alyosha ) When Odette is in her dancing idle animation, her Elemental Skill is replaced by a button that can be tapped repeatedly to extend her dance. Tapping her Elemental Skill will add additional pirouettes and fouettés to her performance, extending her idle animation to a maximum of ~30s. While in Snezhnaya, during Odette's dancing idle animation, a variation of a section of Odette's Character Trailer theme plays.

rows: Odette is a Cryo character with both off-field DPS and support capabilities. She can also enable the party to trigger Stellar-Conduct and Stellar Swirl reactions. After using her Elemental Skill , Odette will summon a double of herself. This double will stay on the field and attack nearby opponents periodically. Stellar Glimmer reaction DMG dealt by party members is also increased. After Odette unleashes her Elemental Burst , she will deal more Stellar Glimmer reaction DMG for some time.

When Odette is in the party, Superconduct reactions triggered by party members will be converted to Stellar-Conduct reactions. A Starlight Prism will appear on the field, turning the surrounding area into a wondrous Polestar Field for a short period of time. All characters inside the Polestar Field receive a Cryo and Electro DMG Bonus, and when opponents within the field are hit by Cryo or Electro attacks, the field will store the dissipating elemental energies and then completely release them every 4s. This further increases the aforementioned DMG Bonus and also increases the Base Stellar-Conduct DMG coefficient for 4s. Additionally, opponents within the Polestar Field will also have their Physical RES lowered. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Odette Talent Demo 1.mp4

When Odette is in the party, Cryo Swirl reactions triggered by party members become Stellar Swirl reactions instead, dealing an instance of Anemo DMG to the opponent as well as generating a Stellar Vortex. Triggering Stellar Swirl multiple times can raise the level of the Stellar Vortex, which then explodes either after a certain time or when a certain number of Stellar Swirl reactions have been triggered. This explosion deals AoE Cryo DMG to nearby opponents. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Odette Talent Demo 2.mp4

After using her Elemental Skill , Odette will summon a double of herself. This double will stay on the field and attack nearby opponents periodically. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Odette Talent Demo 3.mp4

After Odette unleashes her Elemental Skill or Elemental Burst, her Elemental Skill will be replaced with an even more powerful Elemental Skill, and she will also deal an additional instance of Stellar Glimmer reaction DMG of the type corresponding to her Radiance state. After the dance duet ends, Odette's double will also deal an additional instance of Stellar Glimmer reaction DMG of the corresponding type when attacking opponents in its remaining time on the field. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Odette Talent Demo 4.mp4

After Odette unleashes her Elemental Burst , she will also summon her double and deal more Stellar Glimmer reaction DMG for some time. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Odette Talent Demo 5.mp4

Solo Dance Double: A psychic double of Odette's that dances a duet with her. May be summoned to the field through her Elemental Skill or Elemental Burst. Alternates between the Plume and Wing dance moves to periodically attack nearby opponents, dealing AoE Cryo DMG . A maximum of one Solo Dance Double summoned by Odette is allowed on the field at any one time. Additionally, when there is a Dance Double summoned by Odette nearby, her Elemental Skill Adagio: Phantom Night Dancers is changed to the special Elemental Skill Adagio: Coda at Dawn's Tolling.
Adagio: Coda at Dawn's Tolling: Odette's special Elemental Skill, which deals to nearby opponents AoE Cryo DMG over time. Then, when the dance duel ends, she deals another instance of AoE Cryo DMG that is considered Stellar-Conduct DMG. During the dance duet, Odette can control the direction of the dance steps. Radiance: Stellar Glimmer : The DMG dealt when the dance duet ends is changed to AoE Cryo DMG of the corresponding Stellar reaction type. Additionally, after Odette unleashes the special Elemental Skill Adagio: Coda at Dawn's Tolling, should she be in the Radiance: Stellar Glimmer state while her Dance Double is still on the field, the Dance Double's two dance move types will also deal additional AoE Cryo DMG of the corresponding Stellar Glimmer reaction type.
Marvelous Splendor: After unlocking the Ascension Talent "Spring Rite of the Chosen One," Odette will obtain a special effect when she summons her Solo Dance Double. Every stack of Marvelous Splendor active increases the character's Stellar Glimmer DMG by 15%. This lasts until her Dance Double exits the field or when she summons her Solo Dance Double again. When Odette is off-field, she loses 1 stack of Marvelous Splendor every second, while other nearby party members gain the corresponding number of Marvelous Splendor stacks at the same time.
Polestar Field: When Stellar-Conduct is triggered, the surrounding area will transform into a Polestar Field for a short period of time, and when inside a Polestar Field, certain characters will enter the Radiance: Stellar-Conduct state, which grants various skill buffs.
Radiance: Stellar Glimmer: Radiance: Stellar-Conduct and Radiance: Stellar Swirl are both considered Radiance: Stellar Glimmer states. Characters can only be affected by one Radiance state at any one time, and where more than one state can be triggered, Radiance: Stellar-Conduct shall apply first.
Elevation: Special DMG Boost effect. It is calculated independently of other DMG Boost effects.

Prune is a playable Anemo character in Genshin Impact .

A self-proclaimed "Witch Hunter" who traveled from Nod-Krai to Mondstadt to look for Alice after she "kidnapped" her imaginary friend Descartes . There, Prune meets Alice's daughter, Klee , and plasters Mondstadt with posters antagonizing Alice, which no one takes seriously.

rows: Prune is an Anemo support character who provides DMG bonuses to her teammates. After casting her Elemental Skill , Prune strikes the "Witchlure Bell," dealing Anemo DMG. If this attack triggers a Swirl reaction, then for a short duration, the element involved in that Swirl will cause the "Banehunter Oathhammer" to undergo Elemental Conversion. Prune can then tap the skill again to unleash an attack dealing DMG of the corresponding Elemental Type. After casting her Elemental Burst , the "Witchlure Bell" enters the "Hunter-Seeker" mode, periodically attacking nearby enemies. After unlocking the Ascension Talent Verdict and Punishment , if these attacks deal DMG and trigger a Swirl reaction, a "Banehunter Oathhammer" with the corresponding Elemental Conversion will be summoned before the enemy, slamming down and dealing corresponding Elemental DMG. After unlocking the Ascension Talent Tolling Synchronicity , whenever Prune deals DMG using an Elemental Converted "Banehunter Oathhammer," all nearby party members gain the "Tolling Rally" effect, increasing their DMG.

When using this special Elemental Skill, the Banehunter Oathhammer will be converted to the other Elemental Type involved in the aforementioned Swirl Reaction. After the Ascension Talent "Verdict and Punishment" is unlocked, when the Witchlure Bell in Hunter-Seeker mode triggers Swirl on an opponent, it will summon a Banehunter Oathhammer that has undergone the corresponding Elemental Conversion to attack the opponent.

Sandrone , also known by her personal name Marionette Guillotin and codename " Marionette ," is a playable Cryo character in Genshin Impact .

She is the Seventh of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers and the leader of the Adventurers' Guild . She interprets all phenomena through the prism of mathematics, and is an elegant lady who is never absent from a tea party.

Sandrone was created by Alain Guillotin in the image of his deceased sister, Mary-Ann Guillotin . Following Alain's death, she kept Pulonia , his final creation, as her constant companion. Since Pulonia's death, she has been accompanied by a new robotic companion named Fagio ( Facilitatrice Automatisee Generaliste Interactive et Omnitache ).
Upon obtaining Sandrone, the World Quest A Lady's Invitation becomes available, and completing it rewards Sandrone's Portable Tea Table .

rows: Description Gameplay Notes Advanced Properties Attribute Scaling Preview Normal Attack Generates threads that control her weapon using formulae, performing up to 3 consecutive strikes. Charged Attack Summons the Facilitatrice Automatisee Generaliste Interactive et Omnitache, or " Fagio ," and switches it to Decoding mode: Unleashes a sweeping fire attack on enemies in front, as well as periodically fires condensed beams, dealing AoE Cryo DMG . Radiance: Stellar Glimmer : The condensed beams will instead deal AoE Cryo DMG that is considered the corresponding Stellar Glimmer DMG. While in Decoding mode, Fagio's Decoding Power will continuously increase. Firing condensed beams will also further increase its Decoding Power. When Fagio's Decoding Power reaches the maximum of 100 points, it switches to Power Overdrive mode, in which it fires at opponents with longer intervals, dealing Cryo DMG . It will be unable to switch to Decoding mode at this time. When not in Decoding mode, Fagio's Decoding Power gradually decreases. When Sandrone is off-field, she will focus on maintaining Fagio, causing its Decoding Power to decrease at 300% the original rate. Fagio exits Power Overdrive mode when its Decoding Power has decreased to under 50. Plunging Attack Plunges from midair to strike the ground below, dealing DMG to opponents along their path and causing AoE DMG on landing. When Prism Shot or Charged Attack Condensed Beam hits at least one enemy , it generates 1 Elemental Particle . This particle generation has a cooldown of 2.5 seconds. Passive Effects Passive Talent 1, Eternal Speculation Engine : " Radiance: Stellar Glimmer : When using the Elemental Skill Formule Phenomenale: Differential Analysis , if Fagio's Decoding Power is greater than 50, the second Prism Shot fired by Fagio at nearby opponents will deal 400% of its original DMG as Fagio's Decoding Power is decreased. Additionally, for every 10 points of Decoding Power Fagio loses, it gains 1 stack of Refined Tactics for 60s (max 10 stacks). When Sandrone uses the Elemental Burst Formule Phenomenale: Q.E.D. while in the Radiance: Stellar-Conduct state, all stacks of Refined Tactics are cleared, causing the Convective Inhibition Ray to deal 100% + (number of stacks cleared) × 10% of its original DMG." Constellation Effects Constellation Level 1, Morrow After the Golden Dusk : "When in Decoding mode, Fagio's Decoding Power increases at a 50% lower rate, and all party members deal 30% increased Stellar Glimmer reaction DMG." Constellation Level 2, An Heiress Gazed Into the Looking-Glass : " Radiance: Stellar Glimmer : Increases CRIT DMG from Charged Attack condensed beams by 40%. Also, each time a beam is fired, CRIT DMG dealt by all condensed beams fired during this Decoding mode period will be further increased by 20%. Max 3 stacks." Constellation Level 3, Refuse the Wake of Dusk, the Moonlit Yoke : Increases this talent's level by 3, up to a maximum of 15. Constellation Level 6, Narcissus Wakes, Her Eyes Upon the Dawn : "When Fagio fires a condensed beam for the third time while in Decoding mode, the beam becomes a more powerful Condensed Cluster Beam that fires continuously. This beam will deal up to 4 additional instances of AoE Cryo DMG at 100% of Sandrone's ATK on top of any subsequent original beam fired. Radiance: Stellar Glimmer : The Condensed Cluster Beam will instead deal 4 additional instances of AoE Cryo DMG . The DMG dealt with this attack, which is considered the corresponding Stellar Glimmer reaction DMG, is equal to: Radiance: Stellar-Conduct : 80% of Sandrone's ATK. Radiance: Stellar Swirl : 120% of Sandrone's ATK. Additionally, all Stellar Glimmer reaction DMG dealt by Sandrone is elevated by 20%." Increases Sandrone's Elemental Mastery based on her ATK . Every 100 ATK will increase her Elemental Mastery by 8. The maximum increase she can gain this way is 160.

Sandrone will enter the Radiance: Stellar Conduct state when she is inside a Polestar Field , or the Radiance: Stellar Swirl state for 8s after a nearby party member triggers a Stellar Swirl reaction. When a party member triggers a Superconduct or Cryo Swirl reaction, it becomes a Stellar-Conduct or Stellar Swirl reaction instead, and the Base DMG of the aforementioned reaction is also increased by 0.7% for every 100 points of Sandrone's ATK. A maximum increase of 14% can be obtained in this way.

rows: Sandrone is a Cryo DMG dealer who enables her teammates to trigger Stellar-Conduct reactions and who deals Stellar-Conduct DMG directly with her Talents. During a Charged Attack, Sandrone will also summon the mechanism "Fagio" to bombard the opponent. During this time, Fagio's Power will rise continuously, and once it reaches its max limit, Fagio will overheat and slow down its rate of attack. When Sandrone unleashes the Elemental Skill , she will fire Prism Shots at any opponents nearby, as well as lower Fagio's Power so that it can continue to bombard the opponent. When she unleashes her Elemental Burst , Sandrone will summon a large number of Prismatic Resonance Cannons for an elegant wide-area bombardment in front of her.

When Sandrone is in the party, Superconduct reactions triggered by party members will be converted to Stellar-Conduct reactions. A Starlight Prism will appear on the field, turning the surrounding area into a wondrous Polestar Field for a short period of time. All characters inside the Polestar Field receive a Cryo and Electro DMG Bonus, and when opponents within the field are hit by Cryo or Electro attacks, the field will store the dissipating elemental energies and then completely release them every 4s. This further increases the aforementioned DMG Bonus and also increases the Base Stellar-Conduct DMG coefficient for 4s. Additionally, opponents within the Polestar Field will also have their Physical RES reduced. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Sandrone Talent Demo 1.mp4

During a Charged Attack, Sandrone will summon the mechanism "Fagio" to bombard opponents. During this time, Fagio's Power will rise continuously, and once it reaches its max limit, Fagio will overheat and slow down its rate of attack. Outside of a Charged Attack, Fagio's Power decreases slowly, and when Sandrone is off-field, she will focus on repairing Fagio, causing the latter's Power to decrease quickly. When Fagio's Power falls below 50% of the max limit, it will exit overheating and continue to bombard the opponent with the usual poise and elegance. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Sandrone Talent Demo 2.mp4

When Sandrone unleashes the Elemental Skill , she will board her Tea Party Tactical Assault Hovermech and elegantly hover forward for some time, as well as fire Prism Shots at any opponents nearby. During this time, Sandrone will also quietly repair Fagio on the side, causing its Power to decrease quickly. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Sandrone Talent Demo 3.mp4

When she unleashes her Elemental Burst , Sandrone will summon a large number of Prismatic Resonance Cannons for an elegant wide-area bombardment in front of her. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Sandrone Talent Demo 4.mp4

Decoding: Fagio will switch to this mode when using a Charged Attack. When in this mode, Fagio will engage any opponents ahead with a sweeping fire attack, as well as fire condensed beams at intervals, dealing AoE Cryo DMG . Radiance: Stellar Glimmer : The condensed beams will instead deal AoE Cryo DMG that is considered the corresponding Stellar Glimmer DMG.
Radiance: Stellar Glimmer: Radiance: Stellar-Conduct and Radiance: Stellar Swirl are both considered Radiance: Stellar Glimmer states. Characters can only be affected by one Radiance state at any one time, and where more than one state can be triggered, Radiance: Stellar-Conduct shall apply first.
Decoding Power: When in Decoding mode, Fagio's Decoding Power will continuously increase. When its Decoding Power reaches the maximum, Fagio will be unable to maintain or re-enter Decoding mode.
Elevation: Special DMG Boost effect. It is calculated independently of other DMG Boost effects.
Polestar Field: When Stellar-Conduct is triggered, the surounding area will transform into a Polestar Field for a short period of time, and when inside a Polestar Field, certain characters will enter the Radiance: Stellar-Conduct state, when grants various skill buffs.

He is the Eleventh of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers . Wherever he goes, danger follows, and Childe is always eager for a challenge, making him extremely dangerous despite being the youngest member.

rows: Description Gameplay Notes Advanced Properties Attribute Scaling Preview Normal Attack Performs up to 6 consecutive shots with a bow. Charged Attack Performs a more precise Aimed Shot with increased DMG. While aiming, the power of Hydro will accumulate on the arrowhead. An arrow fully charged with the torrent will deal Hydro DMG and apply the Riptide status . Riptide Opponents affected by Riptide will suffer from AoE Hydro DMG effects when attacked by Tartaglia in various ways. DMG dealt in this way is considered Normal Attack DMG. Riptide Flash: A fully-charged Aimed Shot that hits an opponent affected by Riptide deals consecutive bouts of AoE DMG. Can occur once every 0.7s. Riptide Burst: Defeating an opponent affected by Riptide creates a Hydro burst that inflicts the Riptide status on nearby opponents hit. Plunging Attack Fires off a shower of arrows in mid-air before falling and striking the ground, dealing AoE DMG upon impact. When Tartaglia is in Foul Legacy: Raging Tide's Melee Stance, he cannot perform a plunging attack. When Riptide Flash hits at least one enemy , it generates 1 Elemental Particle . This particle generation has a cooldown of 3 seconds. This cooldown is shared with the Riptide Slash particle generation. Normal Attack bonuses from artifacts or weapons affect the damage of Riptide Flash and Riptide Burst. Riptide Flash is not affected by damage fall off due to being not a part of the Fully Charged Aimed Shot. If an attack that would apply Riptide (e.g., Fully Charged Aimed Shot, Riptide Burst, 4th ascension passive Swords of Torrent triggering, and Havoc: Obliteration Ranged Stance version) to an enemy who is not affected by Riptide, would deal enough damage to kill it, Riptide will still be applied, causing Riptide Burst to trigger immediately. In this Stance, Tartaglia's Normal and Charged Attacks are converted to Hydro DMG that cannot be overridden by any other elemental infusion and change as follows: Normal Attack Performs up to 6 consecutive Hydro strikes. Charged Attack Consumes a certain amount of Stamina to unleash a cross slash, dealing Hydro DMG . Riptide Slash Hitting an opponent affected by Riptide with a melee attack unleashes a Riptide Slash that deals AoE Hydro DMG . DMG dealt in this way is considered Elemental Skill DMG, and can only occur once every 1.5s. After 30s, or when the ability is unleashed again, this skill will end. Tartaglia will return to his Ranged Stance and this ability will enter CD. The longer Tartaglia stays in his Melee Stance, the longer the CD. If the return to a ranged stance occurs automatically after 30s, the CD is even longer. Melee Stance ends when Tartaglia leaves the field. The cooldown does not start until Melee Stance ends. When Riptide Slash hits at least one enemy , it generates 1 Elemental Particle . This particle generation has a cooldown of 3 seconds. This cooldown is shared with the Riptide Flash particle generation. The Riptide Slash AoE has quadratic scaling against mobs of enemies that are grouped together. That is, suppose there are n {\displaystyle n} enemies each affected by Riptide grouped close together. If Tartaglia uses his Elemental Skill to attack the n enemies in the cluster at once, it will trigger Riptide Slash for each enemy. Each Riptide Slash will do local AoE damage hitting surrounding enemies. So there will be n {\displaystyle n} Riptide Slashes, each hitting n − 1 {\displaystyle n-1} enemies. In total, there will be n + n ( n − 1 ) = n 2 {\displaystyle n + n(n-1) = n^2} instances of damage against n {\displaystyle n} enemies for each time Tartaglia procs Riptide Slash in melee stance. So for mobs grouped close together (e.g., via Crowd Control abilities of Sucrose , Kazuha , The Viridescent Hunt , etc.), Tartaglia's Riptide Slash DMG will scale quadratically with the number of enemies in the cluster. Tartaglia's Interruption Resistance is increased while in Melee Stance. In Melee stance Plunging Attacks are disabled. The stance switch animations will be skipped if this skill is used while walking or running. However, Stance Switch DMG will still be dealt when switching to Melee Stance. Charged Attack effects apply to his Ranged Stance's Aimed Shot and Melee Stance's Charged Attack. Effects that require an arrow to be fired, such as the passives of Amos' Bow and Slingshot , cannot be triggered in Melee Stance. Effects that require hitting weak spots, such as the passive of Prototype Crescent , can be triggered in Melee Stance. Elemental Skill effects apply to the initial Melee Stance change and Riptide Slash. Cooldown The cooldown is linear in the time spent (duration) in Melee Stance. Description Advanced Properties Attribute Scaling Preview Calls forth Spirit Blades passed down through generations of the Vila to deal AoE Anemo DMG , then switches to the Armed for Action mode and gains 2 stacks of Sword Essence . Armed for Action DMG dealt by Vesna with her Normal Attacks, Charged Attacks, and Plunging Attacks become Anemo DMG that cannot be overridden by another elemental infusion instead. She will also summon a wind pinion that attacks the opponent at the same time, dealing additional Anemo DMG . Each time the wind pinion is summoned, Vesna will regenerate a certain amount of Sword Essence. Vesna can consume Sword Essence to unleash the special Elemental Skill Windborne Sword , which deals to the opponent Anemo DMG . Each use of the special Elemental Skill Windborne Sword in the same instance of Armed for Action will increase the level of Windborne Sword, beginning from Lv. 1 to Lv. 3 max, for more Anemo DMG . Using Windborne Sword at Lv. 2 and Lv. 3 will also summon Spirit Blades which deal Anemo DMG . Vesna will exit the mode when its duration ends or when she has used Windborne Sword at the highest level 3 times. Exiting will clear all remaining Sword Essence she has accrued. Additionally, when in this mode, Vesna's resistance to interruption is increased. After Vesna uses the special Elemental Skill Windborne Sword or the Elemental Burst For the Tsaritsa! , she also gains 1 stack of Disciplinary Action which lasts 20s. Max 6 stacks, and the duration of each stack is independent of the others'. When she has Disciplinary Action stacks active, the Spirit Blades summoned by Vesna will deal DMG equal to (100% + 10% × Disciplinary Action stack count) of the original DMG instead. All active stacks of Disciplinary Action are cleared when Vesna uses the Elemental Skill The Art of Victory or when she leaves the field.

Radiance: Stellar Swirl: Vesna will gain the corresponding effect based on the Elemental Type of her party members: For every Cryo or Anemo character in her current party, Vesna's ATK increases by 6%; and For every character of all other Elemental Types in her current party, Vesna's Elemental Mastery increases by 25 instead.

When party members trigger Cryo Swirl, it will be changed to a Stellar Swirl reaction, and party members' Base DMG for the Stellar Swirl will be increased based on Vesna's ATK. Every 100 ATK she has increases the Base Stellar Swirl DMG by 0.7%. The maximum DMG increase that can be gained this way is 14%. After a party member triggers a Stellar Swirl reaction nearby, Vesna enters the Radiance: Stellar Swirl state for 8s.

Holding on Sprint or Jump when Vesna is not in combat will cause her to enter the Coursing state. Coursing Continuously consumes Stamina to hover in mid-air. Sprinting or tapping Jump to go higher expends additional Stamina. Including the hold on Jump that triggers Coursing, Vesna can go higher up to 3 times in each instance of the Coursing state. Additionally, in Snezhnaya (excluding Nod-Krai), when Vesna is switched onto the field while the currently active party member is in mid-air and not in combat, she will immediately enter the Coursing state and regenerate 50 Stamina. This effect can trigger once every 10s, and does not take effect in Domains, Trounce Domains, or the Spiral Abyss.

When the Elemental Skill Rechitativ: Sonorous Dawn is used, any Stellar Vortex on the field will turn into a Wandering Vortex instead. While the Song of Ages Past effect is active, nearby party members' Stellar Swirl reactions will generate Wandering Vortex instead. Generating or detonating a Wandering Vortex will also reduce nearby opponents' Anemo RES by 35% for 6s. Additionally, nearby party members who enter the Radiance: Stellar Swirl state while Song of Ages Past is in effect will have the Radiance: Stellar Swirl state extended by 4s.

When the Elemental Skill Rechitativ: Sonorous Dawn is used, Vodyanitsa will also gain 25 stacks of Lead Vocal as well as 10 stacks of Chorus . The two effects above last 30s each, and the stack count is refreshed when the Elemental Skill is used.

Holding the Elemental Skill outside of combat will cause Vodyanitsa to embody her true Water Imp form and swim for up to 10s at the cost of Stamina. Naturally, as a Water Imp, she can also move across the water's surface. Vodyanitsa will exit her Water Imp form when the Elemental Skill is used again, when the duration ends, or when all Stamina is depleted. Additionally, while Vodyanitsa can swim faster, her Stamina consumption rate is also increased.

Description Gameplay Notes As the Prima Donna of the Korolevskiy Troupe , Vodyanitsa sings in person in place of playing an instrument. If the player uses a Music Gadget with Vodyanitsa as the active character, she will sing the notes instead of playing the instrument.

rows: Vodyanitsa is a Hydro character who provides both healing and support. She can enhance the Hydro, Cryo, and Stellar Swirl DMG dealt by characters in the party.

When Vodyanitsa uses her Elemental Skill , she enters the "Song of Ages Past" state, periodically summoning the Horn of Spring's Call to attack targets alongside the active character, decreasing the Hydro and Cryo RES of enemies hit, and intermittently healing the active character. When created or when it explodes, Wandering Vortex decreases the Anemo RES of nearby enemies and allows "Lead Vocal" and "Chorus" to increase the Stellar Swirl DMG dealt by characters in the party. Hover over previews to view in higher quality. ( Preview Preferences ) Media:Vodyanitsa Talent Demo 3.mp4

If the character's HP is below 40%: The healing is increased by 50%; and If the character's HP is 40% or above: Vodyanitsa's Max HP is increased by 20% for 6s. Max 3 stacks, and each stack's duration is counted independently.

The Wanderer is a playable Anemo character in Genshin Impact .

He was once Scaramouche , the Sixth of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers , also known by his codename " The Balladeer ." After erasing his previous identities from Irminsul , he became a drifter until he willingly regained his memories. He is currently a Driyosh of the Vahumana Darshan.

During the Archon Quest As Though Morning Dew in Interlude Chapter : Act III - Inversion of Genesis , the player can change the Wanderer's name, which will then be used in some of the game's interfaces, such as Party Setup . Most characters, however, will refer to him by the name of Hat Guy , the name Nahida used upon enrolling him to Vahumana .

Description Gameplay Notes Advanced Properties Attribute Scaling Preview Concentrates the power of the winds to break free from the shackles of the earth, dealing AoE Anemo DMG before leaping into the air and entering the Windfavored state. Windfavored The Wanderer cannot perform Plunging Attacks in this state. When he uses Normal and Charged Attacks, they will be converted into Kuugo: Fushoudan and Kuugo: Toufukai respectively; the DMG they deal and their AoE will be increased, and their DMG will be considered Normal and Charged Attack DMG respectively. Kuugo: Toufukai will not consume Stamina. The Wanderer will hover persistently during this time. While this state is active, the Wanderer's movements gain the following properties: Persistently consumes Kuugoryoku Points to maintain this hovering state. When sprinting, additional Kuugoryoku Points will be consumed for the Wanderer to accelerate mid-air. Holding sprint will cause persistent Kuugoryoku Point consumption to maintain speed. This effect will replace his default sprint. Jumping expends extra Kuugoryoku Points to increase hovering height. Holding jump will cause persistent Kuugoryoku Point consumption to keep increasing hovering height. Running out of Kuugoryoku Points will end the Windfavored state. A second cast during the duration of Windfavored will also end it. The cooldown does not start until the Windfavored state ends. When a Normal or Charged Attack during the Windfavored State hits at least one enemy , it generates 1 Elemental Particle . A non-converted Normal Attack can also generate particles if the Windfavored State is activated before said attack hits an enemy. This particle generation has a cooldown of 2 seconds. If only Normal and Charged Attacks are performed in the Windfavored state, up to 5 particles can be generated. This may change if other point-consuming actions are performed or if extra Kuugoryoku Points are gained. During the casting animation of this skill, the Wanderer is immune to being Frozen . If the Wanderer falls to the ground after being Frozen mid-air, the Windfavored state will end when the Frozen state ends. If the Wanderer is staggered mid-air, the player can press sprint or jump to immediately recover. Doing so will not consume extra Kuugoryoku Points, and pressing Sprint will not trigger Gales of Reverie if it is available. During the Windfavored state, the Wanderer will be unaffected by quest steps that force the character to walk. Kuugoryoku Point consumption begins 3 frames (60FPS) after activating this skill. While in Windfavored state Plunging Attacks are disabled. title2: Specialist, Royal Energy Commission of Snezhnaya
type: Upcoming Characters
Mitya ( Russian : Митя Mitya ) is an upcoming playable Electro character in Genshin Impact .

Mitya is a scientist from the Royal Energy Commission of Snezhnaya and an expert in the field of energy research. Brilliant yet extremely sociable and outgoing, he has a tendency to dodge work and occasionally finds himself offset by his own sentient scarf whenever he goes overboard with his conversations.
Genius At Play

"Research differs from production — efficiency is not the gold standard. I have worked alongside many gifted individuals, and I know well that talent and eccentricity tend to go hand in hand. But the one thing that never disappoints is the 'answers' they provide."
— Pierro , "The Jester," responding to the insinuation that Mitya holds special privileges
"I've applied for his scarf to be granted greater authority to help prevent leaks of classified information. In the vast majority of security inquiries, bystanders are considered innocent."
— Valeriy , Commander, Special Assignments Battalion

Experts tend to be remarkably efficient, capable of producing astonishing results in very little time. Yet for them, "attendance requirements" designed around the pace of the average researcher amount to a cage.
Whiling away the hours would be easy enough. But the world has so much more to offer, and wouldn't it be a shame to miss out on all that color?
And so, the energy expert who ought to be buried in important work can often be found wandering the streets of Snezhnograd , enjoying the leisure his talent has bought him.

Sometimes he catches the Korolevskiy Troupe 's latest production, and sometimes he shares a table with a stranger at Podvorye Restaurant , and sometimes, on a fine sunny day, he gives his scarf, that dear companion of his, a wash and hangs it out to dry...
People expect a researcher to devote himself to his work, or at the very least, not neglect his duties. But he would argue: how can someone who takes no joy in life hope to do good work?

To borrow a seafaring analogy, meticulous reasoning is like drawing an accurate sea chart, while a flash of inspiration is when a new continent suddenly comes into view through a spyglass. Clearly, the latter is the greater achievement, and a far more exhilarating one.

And so he sets out everything he finds "unreasonable" in letters, proposals, and leave requests, appends them to the last page of his research reports, and submits the lot in the hope of catching his superiors' attention.

Eventually, he got his wish. His increasingly cavalier approach to his schedule, coupled with his habit of taking it upon himself to rewrite absence reports as further arguments in his own defense, earned him the assistance of a major who took time management very seriously indeed. Congratulations were in order.

title2: Commander of the Special Assignments Battalion
type: Upcoming Characters
Valeriy ( Russian : Валерий Valeriy ) is an upcoming playable Electro character in Genshin Impact .
Discipline Down to the Second

"Oh, that officer? Don't go thinking all he does is chase me around announcing the time and nagging me to get back to work. If anyone threatens the Armory Palace's projects or researchers, you'll get to witness a terrifying sight: 'a fortress going on the offensive and rolling right over people."
— Mitya

The Armory Palace is a vast research, design, and production complex within Glupov . As Snezhnaya's foremost research institution, it has developed numerous cutting-edge technologies and many of the weapons that form the backbone of the snowbound nation's military. The secrets and valuable assets in its keeping are beyond counting.

To protect the Armory Palace and its personnel, elite troops from the 1st Grenadier Regiment were reorganized into the Special Assignments Battalion, serving as the institution's dedicated guard under the command of Major Valeriy.

His service record is particularly distinguished. He has led his troops in wiping out six concentrations of monsters linked to Ley Line disturbances, crushing three vicious Volkodlak gangs, and eliminating more than eighty percent of the rampaging chimeric monsters west of Snezhnograd ...
He also schedules the entire battalion's duties with unfailing precision, day after day, year after year... all without an adjutant's assistance.
With an expert in both combat and administration commanding their guard, the Armory Palace's specialists can devote themselves to research and production with complete peace of mind.

Indeed, since the Special Assignments Battalion took up its post, Major Valeriy and his troops have neutralized more than ninety threats of every description, including surviving bandits plotting to steal the Armory Palace's secrets and outlaws attempting to abduct its researchers.

In recent years, however, military observers have noted something surprising: Major Valeriy has become a frequent visitor to the Korolevskiy Theater and Podvorye Restaurant , among other entertainment venues...
Major Valeriy declines to comment on any of the speculation. He continues to let his impeccable time management and faultless organization at work speak for themselves.

People are not machines, of course. They cannot be expected to run like clockwork, keeping to a rigid schedule every moment of the day. But sound scheduling is a safeguard. When the unexpected disrupts a plan, it provides the room to adapt and the confidence to do so.
There will always be work that calls for contingency plans, and deadlines that simply cannot be missed.
And someone must always bear the strain, keep a constant eye on the schedule, and head off delays and mishaps.

heading_path: Butter and Cats and the Law of Energy Supply
blocks.text: - The name of this constellation is likely a reference to the buttered cat paradox , a common joke based on the combination of two adages: "cats always land on their feet" and "buttered toast always lands buttered side down." The paradox arises when one considers what would happen if one attached a piece of buttered toast (butter side up) to the back of a cat, then dropped the cat from a large height.

Gravity Ripple: After unleashing Elemental Skill Eternal Tides, Columbina will summon Gravity Ripple. Gravity Ripple will follow the current active character on the field, while continuously dealing AoE Hydro DMG to surrounding opponents. Additionally, while Gravity Ripple is on the field, and nearby party members trigger Lunar reactions or inflict Lunar Reaction DMG, Columbina will gain the New Moon's Omen effect for 2s, continuously accumulating Gravity. 20 Gravity can be accumulated every 2s. You can have up to 60 Gravity, and it will be removed when the duration of Gravity Ripple ends. Once Gravity is accumulated to its limit, a special Gravity Interference will be triggered. Different effects will be triggered depending on the Lunar reaction type that has accumulated the most Gravity for Columbina. If the Lunar reaction type that has accumulated the most Gravity for Columbina is: Lunar-Charged: Gravity Interference will deal a single instance of Electro AoE DMG . This DMG is considered Lunar-Charged DMG. Lunar-Bloom: Gravity Interference will fire 5 Moondew Sigils at surrounding opponents, dealing Dendro DMG . This DMG is considered Lunar-Bloom DMG. Lunar-Crystallize: Gravity Interference will deal a single instance of Geo AoE DMG . This DMG is considered Lunar-Crystallize DMG.
Elevation: Special DMG Boost effect. It is calculated independently of other DMG Boost effects.

Shadowless Reflection: Light the lamp, dealing AoE Geo DMG , and gain Haunted Night's Oriole-Song effect for 20s. When this effect is active, Illuga gains 21 stacks of Nightingale's Song Nightingale's Song The effect gained after Illuga unleashes his Elemental Burst Shadowless Reflection It can increase the Geo DMG inflicted by current active characters. . When Normal Attacks, Charged Attacks, Plunging Attacks, Elemental Skills, and Elemental Bursts of nearby active party members deal Geo DMG to opponents, 1 stack of Nightingale's Song is consumed to increase the DMG dealt. Increase in DMG is based on Illuga's Elemental Mastery. If DMG is inflicted by Lunar-Crystallize, DMG dealt will increase further. When Geo DMG dealt in this manner hits multiple opponents, multiple stacks of Nightingale's Song will be consumed, depending on how many opponents are hit. Additionally, if there are Geo Constructs created by nearby party members on the battlefield while Illuga unleashes his Elemental Burst, or when nearby party members create Geo Constructs while Haunted Night's Oriole-Song is active, every Geo Construct on the battlefield will allow Illuga to gain 5 additional stacks of Nightingale's Song. Within 20s after unleashing his Elemental Burst, Illuga can gain a maximum of 15 additional stacks of Nightingale's Song this way. When all stacks of Nightingale's Song have been consumed, or when the state's duration ends, the Haunted Night's Oriole-Song effect will end.

Rite of Spring's Procession: After Vesna uses the special Elemental Skill Windborne Sword or the Elemental Burst For the Tsaritsa!, she also gains 1 stack of Disciplinary Action which lasts 20s. Max 6 stacks, and the duration of each stack is independent of the others'. When she has Disciplinary Action stacks active, the Spirit Blades summoned by Vesna will deal DMG equal to (100% + 10% × Disciplinary Action stack count) of the original DMG instead. All active stacks of Disciplinary Action are cleared when Vesna uses the Elemental Skill The Art of Victory or when she leaves the field.
Armed for Action: Vesna switches to this mode after using the Elemental Skill The Art of Victory. In this mode, which lasts up to 15s: Vesna's resistance to interruption is increased. DMG dealt by Vesna with her Normal Attacks, Charged Attacks, and Plunging Attacks becomes Anemo DMG that cannot be overridden by another elemental infusion instead. She will also summon a wind pinion that attacks the opponent at the same time, dealing additional Anemo DMG . Each time the wind pinion is summoned, Vesna will regenerate a certain amount of Sword Essence. Vesna can consume Sword Essence to unleash the special Elemental Skill Windborne Sword, which deals Anemo DMG to her opponents. Vesna will exit the mode when its duration ends or after she has used Windborne Sword at the highest level 3 times. Exiting will clear all remaining Sword Essence she has accrued.

Additionally, while Gravity Ripple is on the field, and nearby party members trigger Lunar reactions or inflict Lunar Reaction DMG, Columbina will gain the New Moon's Omen effect for 2s, continuously accumulating Gravity. 20 Gravity can be accumulated every 2s. You can have up to 60 Gravity, and it will be removed when the duration of Gravity Ripple ends. Once Gravity is accumulated to its limit, a special Gravity Interference will be triggered. Different effects will be triggered depending on the Lunar reaction type that has accumulated the most Gravity for Columbina. If the Lunar reaction type that has accumulated the most Gravity for Columbina is: Lunar-Charged: Gravity Interference will deal a single instance of Electro AoE DMG . This DMG is considered Lunar-Charged DMG. Lunar-Bloom: Gravity Interference will fire 5 Moondew Sigils at surrounding opponents, dealing Dendro DMG . This DMG is considered Lunar-Bloom DMG. Lunar-Crystallize: Gravity Interference will deal a single instance of Geo AoE DMG . This DMG is considered Lunar-Crystallize DMG.
Elevation: Special DMG Boost effect. It is calculated independently of other DMG Boost effects.

Purr-loined Treasure Flask: A small elemental vessel that Jahoda retrieves after casting her Elemental Skill Savvy Strategy: Splitting the Spoils. While Jahoda is in the Shadow Pursuit state, if nearby opponents are affected by Pyro , Hydro , Electro , or Cryo , the Purr-loined Treasure Flask will convert to that element and begin filling up. The order of priority that determines which element will be converted to is: Pyro , Hydro , Electro , then Cryo . After each use of her Elemental Skill, the Purr-loined Treasure Flask can undergo one such conversion. When the Purr-loined Treasure Flask is full, Jahoda immediately drains it, exiting the Shadow Pursuit state and dealing a single instance of Anemo DMG to nearby opponents. Each time the Elemental Skill is cast, Jahoda takes out a brand-new Purr-loined Treasure Flask. Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam : When the Purr-loined Treasure Flask becomes full, Jahoda will not immediately discharge it. Instead, for a short duration, she steadily consumes the stored element inside and periodically fires Fluffy Meowballs at nearby opponents, dealing DMG of the corresponding element stored in the Purr-loined Treasure Flask.

Gravity Ripple: After unleashing Elemental Skill Eternal Tides, Columbina will summon Gravity Ripple. Gravity Ripple will follow the current active character on the field, while continuously dealing AoE Hydro DMG to surrounding opponents. Additionally, while Gravity Ripple is on the field, and nearby party members trigger Lunar reactions or inflict Lunar Reaction DMG, Columbina will gain the New Moon's Omen effect for 2s, continuously accumulating Gravity. 20 Gravity can be accumulated every 2s. You can have up to 60 Gravity, and it will be removed when the duration of Gravity Ripple ends. Once Gravity is accumulated to its limit, a special Gravity Interference will be triggered. Different effects will be triggered depending on the Lunar reaction type that has accumulated the most Gravity for Columbina. If the Lunar reaction type that has accumulated the most Gravity for Columbina is: Lunar-Charged: Gravity Interference will deal a single instance of Electro AoE DMG . This DMG is considered Lunar-Charged DMG. Lunar-Bloom: Gravity Interference will fire 5 Moondew Sigils at surrounding opponents, dealing Dendro DMG . This DMG is considered Lunar-Bloom DMG. Lunar-Crystallize: Gravity Interference will deal a single instance of Geo AoE DMG . This DMG is considered Lunar-Crystallize DMG.
Elevation: Special DMG Boost effect. It is calculated independently of other DMG Boost effects.

Shadowless Reflection: Light the lamp, dealing AoE Geo DMG , and gain Haunted Night's Oriole-Song effect for 20s. When this effect is active, Illuga gains 21 stacks of Nightingale's Song Nightingale's Song The effect gained after Illuga unleashes his Elemental Burst Shadowless Reflection. It can increase the Geo DMG inflicted by current active characters. . When Normal Attacks, Charged Attacks, Plunging Attacks, Elemental Skills, and Elemental Bursts of nearby active party members deal Geo DMG to opponents, 1 stack of Nightingale's Song is consumed to increase the DMG dealt. Increase in DMG is based on Illuga's Elemental Mastery. If DMG is inflicted by Lunar-Crystallize, DMG dealt will increase further. When Geo DMG dealt in this manner hits multiple opponents, multiple stacks of Nightingale's Song will be consumed, depending on how many opponents are hit. Additionally, if there are Geo Constructs created by nearby party members on the battlefield while Illuga unleashes his Elemental Burst, or when nearby party members create Geo Constructs while Haunted Night's Oriole-Song is active, every Geo Construct on the battlefield will allow Illuga to gain 5 additional stacks of Nightingale's Song. Within 20s after unleashing his Elemental Burst, Illuga can gain a maximum of 15 additional stacks of Nightingale's Song this way. When all stacks of Nightingale's Song have been consumed, or when the state's duration ends, the Haunted Night's Oriole-Song effect will end.

Purr-loined Treasure Flask: A small elemental vessel that Jahoda retrieves after casting her Elemental Skill Savvy Strategy: Splitting the Spoils. While Jahoda is in the Shadow Pursuit state, if nearby opponents are affected by Pyro , Hydro , Electro , or Cryo , the Purr-loined Treasure Flask will convert to that element and begin filling up. The order of priority that determines which element will be converted to is: Pyro , Hydro , Electro , then Cryo . After each use of her Elemental Skill, the Purr-loined Treasure Flask can undergo one such conversion. When the Purr-loined Treasure Flask is full, Jahoda immediately drains it, exiting the Shadow Pursuit state and dealing a single instance of Anemo DMG to nearby opponents. Each time the Elemental Skill is cast, Jahoda takes out a brand-new Purr-loined Treasure Flask. Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam : When the Purr-loined Treasure Flask becomes full, Jahoda will not immediately discharge it. Instead, for a short duration, she steadily consumes the stored element inside and periodically fires Fluffy Meowballs at nearby opponents, dealing DMG of the corresponding element stored in the Purr-loined Treasure Flask.

Windborne Sword: When in the Armed for Action mode, Vesna can consume Sword Essence to use her special Elemental Skill to deal Anemo DMG . Each use of the special Elemental Skill Windborne Sword in the same instance of Armed for Action will increase the level of Windborne Sword, beginning from Lv. 1, up to Lv. 3 max. Using Windborne Sword at Lv. 2 and Lv. 3 will also summon a Spirit Blade which deals Anemo DMG .
Spirit Blade: A weapon with special power that Vesna can summon. Attacks the opponent alongside Vesna to deal Anemo DMG . Vesna can summon Spirit Blades through the following ways: By unleashing the special Elemental Skill Windborne Sword at Lv. 2 and Lv. 3; By using the Elemental Burst For the Tsaritsa!; or By using Windborne Sword·: Transpose in the Constellation Unwavering Ardor. Radiance: Stellar Swirl: DMG dealt by the Spirit Blades become Anemo DMG that is considered Stellar Swirl reaction DMG instead.
Armed for Action: Vesna switches to this mode after using the Elemental Skill The Art of Victory. In this mode, which lasts up to 15s: Vesna's resistance to interruption is increased. DMG dealt by Vesna with her Normal Attacks, Charged Attacks, and Plunging Attacks becomes Anemo DMG that cannot be overridden by another elemental infusion instead. She will also summon a wind pinion that attacks the opponent at the same time, dealing additional Anemo DMG . Each time the wind pinion is summoned, Vesna will regenerate a certain amount of Sword Essence. Vesna can consume Sword Essence to unleash the special Elemental Skill Windborne Sword, which deals Anemo DMG to her opponents. Vesna will exit the mode when its duration ends or after she has used Windborne Sword at the highest level 3 times. Exiting will clear all remaining Sword Essence she has accrued.
Elevation: Special DMG Boost effect. It is calculated independently of other DMG Boost effects.

blocks.text: Banehunter Oathhammer: A witchhunter's trusty companion! Under the right conditions, the Banehunter Oathhammer undergoes Elemental Conversion, turning all its DMG into DMG of the corresponding Elemental Type. Prune can summon the Banehunter Oathhammer that has undergone Elemental Conversion in the following ways: For a certain time after triggering a Swirl Reaction on an opponent with the Elemental Skill Ring-A-Ding-Ding! Hexhunter Chime, Prune can unleash the special Elemental Skill Clang Clang! Witch-tribution Comes!. When using this special Elemental Skill, the Banehunter Oathhammer will be converted to the other Elemental Type involved in the aforementioned Swirl Reaction. After the Ascension Talent "Verdict and Punishment" is unlocked, when the Witchlure Bell in Hunter-Seeker mode triggers Swirl on an opponent, it will summon a Banehunter Oathhammer that has undergone the corresponding Elemental Conversion to attack the opponent.

Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots: One of the gadgets that Jahoda — a former treasure hunter — carries around with her. It is deployed upon using her Elemental Burst Hidden Aces: Seven Tools of the Hunter. Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots continuously restore HP to your active character. If the healed character's HP is above 70%, they also restore HP to the nearby party member with the lowest HP. Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam : If nearby opponents are affected by Pyro , Hydro , Electro , or Cryo , Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots will convert to that element. The order of priority that determines which element will be converted to is: Pyro , Hydro , Electro , then Cryo . After each deployment, a Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robot can undergo one such conversion. After converting, the Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robot will periodically attack up to 3 nearby opponents, dealing damage of the corresponding element.

Armed for Action: Vesna switches to this mode after using the Elemental Skill The Art of Victory. In this mode, which lasts up to 15s: Vesna's resistance to interruption is increased. DMG dealt by Vesna with her Normal Attacks, Charged Attacks, and Plunging Attacks becomes Anemo DMG that cannot be overridden by another elemental infusion instead. She will also summon a wind pinion that attacks the opponent at the same time, dealing additional Anemo DMG . Each time the wind pinion is summoned, Vesna will regenerate a certain amount of Sword Essence. Vesna can consume Sword Essence to unleash the special Elemental Skill Windborne Sword, which deals Anemo DMG to her opponents. Vesna will exit the mode when its duration ends or after she has used Windborne Sword at the highest level 3 times. Exiting will clear all remaining Sword Essence she has accrued.
Windborne Sword: When in the Armed for Action mode, Vesna can consume Sword Essence to use her special Elemental Skill to deal Anemo DMG . Each use of the special Elemental Skill Windborne Sword in the same instance of Armed for Action will increase the level of Windborne Sword, beginning from Lv. 1, up to Lv. 3 max. Using Windborne Sword at Lv. 2 and Lv. 3 will also summon a Spirit Blade which deals Anemo DMG .
Sword Essence: The energy required to use the special Elemental Skill Windborne Swordwhile in the Armed for Action mode. Vesna can accumulate Sword Essence in the following ways: By performing a Normal Attack, Charged Attack, or Plunging attack while in the Armed for Action mode, or by unleashing Windborne Sword: Transpose from the Constellation Unwavering Ardor; By using the Elemental Skill The Art of Victory; or By using the Elemental Burst For the Tsaritsa!

The Art of Victory: Calls forth Spirit Blades passed down through generations of the Vila to deal AoE Anemo DMG , then switches to the Armed for Action mode and gains 2 stacks of Sword Essence mode. Vesna can accumulate Sword Essence in the following ways: By performing a Normal Attack, Charged Attack, or Plunging attack while in the Armed for Action mode, or by unleashing Windborne Sword: Transpose from the Constellation Unwavering Ardor; By using the Elemental Skill The Art of Victory; or By using the Elemental Burst For the Tsaritsa!. Armed for Action DMG dealt by Vesna with her Normal Attacks, Charged Attacks, and Plunging Attacks become Anemo DMG that cannot be overridden by another elemental infusion instead. She will also summon a wind pinion that attacks the opponent at the same time, dealing additional Anemo DMG . Each time the wind pinion is summoned, Vesna will regenerate a certain amount of Sword Essence. Vesna can consume Sword Essence to unleash the special Elemental Skill Windborne Sword, which deals to the opponent Anemo DMG . Each use of the special Elemental Skill Windborne Sword in the same instance of Armed for Action will increase the level of Windborne Sword, beginning from Lv. 1 to Lv. 3 max, for more Anemo DMG . Using Windborne Sword at Lv. 2 and Lv. 3 will also summon Spirit Blades which deal Anemo DMG . Vesna will exit the mode when its duration ends or when she has used Windborne Sword at the highest level 3 times. Exiting will clear all remaining Sword Essence she has accrued. Additionally, when in this mode, Vesna's resistance to interruption is increased. Radiance: Stellar Swirl: DMG dealt with the Spirit Blades becomes Anemo DMG that is also considered Stellar Swirl reaction DMG.

blocks.text: Banehunter Oathhammer: A witchhunter's trusty companion! Under the right conditions, the Banehunter Oathhammer undergoes Elemental Conversion, turning all its DMG into DMG of the corresponding Elemental Type. Prune can summon the Banehunter Oathhammer that has undergone Elemental Conversion in the following ways: For a certain time after triggering a Swirl Reaction on an opponent with the Elemental Skill Ring-A-Ding-Ding! When using this special Elemental Skill, the Banehunter Oathhammer will be converted to the other Elemental Type involved in the aforementioned Swirl Reaction. After the Ascension Talent "Verdict and Punishment" is unlocked, when the Witchlure Bell in Hunter-Seeker mode triggers Swirl on an opponent, it will summon a Banehunter Oathhammer that has undergone the corresponding Elemental Conversion to attack the opponent.

Name: Bloom
Type: Elemental Reactions
Bloom is the Elemental Reaction triggered by inflicting Dendro on a target that is already affected by Hydro or vice versa.

This reaction produces a Dendro Core, which stays on the field for up to 6 seconds, and has different effects based on if Pyro , Electro or neither is applied to it before its duration expires. Only 5 Dendro Cores can exist at a time, and producing more than 5 Dendro Cores will cause the oldest one to expire immediately.

If a Dendro Core's duration expires while the character who created it is in the party and alive, it will explode, dealing AoE Dendro DMG in a 5m radius to both enemies and players. Otherwise, it will disappear without the explosion.
If Pyro is inflicted upon a Dendro Core, the Burgeon reaction will be triggered, which consumes the Dendro Core, and deals increased AoE Dendro DMG in a 5m radius to both enemies and players.

If Electro is inflicted upon a Dendro Core, the Hyperbloom reaction will be triggered, which transforms the Dendro Core into a Sprawling Shot that homes in on the closest enemy (or ally, if triggered by an enemy/the environment), dealing increased AoE Dendro DMG in a 1m radius on hit to both enemies and players.
DMG dealt to players by all Bloom-related reactions are 2% of the DMG dealt to enemies, no matter which party triggers the reaction.

Burgeon and Hyperbloom can both be triggered by a party other than the one which triggered the original Bloom, including the environment, and their damage scale with the stats of the party responsible for applying Pyro or Electro.

Certain character abilities and event buffs will cause the Bloom reaction to produce Bountiful Cores instead of Dendro Cores. Bountiful Cores explode 0.4 seconds after their creation, dealing AoE Dendro DMG in a 6.5m radius to both enemies and players. DMG dealt to players is 2% of the DMG dealt to enemies.
Burgeon and Hyperbloom cannot be triggered on Bountiful Cores. Bountiful Cores share the upper limit of 5 with regular Dendro Cores.
There are 2 Talents that match the category selection:

rows: When all characters in the party are all Dendro or Hydro , and there are at least one Dendro character and one Hydro character: The completion of the third dance step of Nilou's Dance of Haftkarsvar will grant all nearby characters the Golden Chalice's Bounty for 30s. Characters under the effect of Golden Chalice's Bounty will increase the Elemental Mastery of all nearby characters by 100 for 10s whenever they are hit by Dendro attacks . Also, triggering the Bloom or Lunar-Bloom reaction will create Bountiful Cores instead of Dendro Cores. Such Cores will burst very quickly after being created, and they have larger AoEs. Bountiful Cores cannot trigger Hyperbloom or Burgeon , and they share an upper numerical limit with Dendro Cores. Bountiful Core DMG is considered DMG dealt by Dendro Cores produced by Bloom. Should the party not meet the conditions for this Ascension Talent, any existing Golden Chalice's Bounty effects will be canceled.

Every 1,000 points of Nilou's Max HP above 30,000 will cause the DMG dealt by Bountiful Cores created by characters affected by Golden Chalice's Bounty to increase by 9%. The maximum increase in Bountiful Core DMG that can be achieved this way is 400%.

Note that one target can only take 2 instances of DMG from each Bloom-related reaction per source every 0.5 seconds, as limited by the Damage Sequence . Reactions triggered by a given character will not share this limit with reactions triggered by other characters. Note that Dendro Core explosions and Bountiful Core explosions are counted separately.

Bloom DMG is calculated as 2 × Level Multiplier {\displaystyle 2 \times \text{Level Multiplier}} . Level Multipliers for every level can be found in Elemental Reaction/Level Scaling#Level Multiplier .

Bloom DMG is only affected by the level and Elemental Mastery of the character causing the reaction, and the target's Dendro RES . It ignores the target's DEF and cannot deal CRIT Hits . The Elemental Mastery DMG Bonus and the target's RES multiplier are applied multiplicatively with the Base DMG.

Burgeon/Hyperbloom DMG is calculated as 3 × Level Multiplier {\displaystyle 3 \times \text{Level Multiplier} } . Level Multipliers for every level can be found in Elemental Reaction/Level Scaling#Level Multiplier .

Burgeon/Hyperbloom DMG is only affected by the level and Elemental Mastery of the character causing the reaction, and the target's RES . It ignores the target's DEF and cannot deal CRIT Hits . The Elemental Mastery DMG Bonus and the target's RES multiplier are applied multiplicatively with the Base DMG.

Name: Elemental Reaction
Type: Combat Game Systems
Elemental Reactions are triggered by applying certain combinations of elemental effects on a target (enemies, players, or objects).

When an element is applied to a target, it will create an elemental aura that decays over time. Elemental Reactions will occur when a second element is applied onto a target with an existing elemental aura.

Triggering elemental reactions will consume the existing aura by varying amounts depending on the type of reaction triggered and the gauge units of the triggering element. This will shorten the existing aura's duration or completely remove it.
Note that many sources of elemental damage have Internal Cooldown before being able to reapply their element and therefore may not be able to trigger Elemental Reactions on every hit.
Certain more complex mechanics of elemental reactions are explained in-depth in Elemental Gauge Theory , a framework for understanding interaction of elements.

Elemental Reaction damage can be increased by the Elemental Mastery of the character causing the reaction. The in-game interface shows the damage bonus provided by the character's current elemental mastery. This bonus will be applied in different ways, depending on the type of reaction.
See also: Damage § Transformative Reaction Damage , and Elemental Reaction/Level Scaling
Transformative Reactions include Overloaded , Shattered , Electro-Charged , Superconduct , Swirl , Burning , Bloom , Hyperbloom , and Burgeon .

- These reactions deal their own instances of damage, which is separate from the attacks triggering them.
- These reactions have a Base Damage determined by the type of reaction and the level of the character triggering the reaction.
- The Base Damage is then multiplied by a percentage determined by the Elemental Mastery of the character. The percentage can be seen in-game in the Details section of the Attributes page.
- Transformative Reaction DMG cannot CRIT and is only based on level, meaning ATK, CRIT Rate and CRIT DMG have no impact.
- Transformative Reaction DMG ignores the target's DEF , but is affected by Resistance .
See also: Damage § Amplifying Reaction Damage
Amplifying Reactions include Vaporize and Melt .

- Unlike Transformative Reactions, Melt and Vaporize do not deal damage of their own. Instead, they multiply the damage of the attacks that trigger them by either 2× or 1.5× depending on which element triggers the reaction. 2× and 1.5× amplifying reactions are sometimes described as "forward" and "reverse" respectively.
- The damage is multiplied again by a percentage determined by the Elemental Mastery of the character. The percentage can be seen in-game in the Details section of the Attributes page.
- 1.5× reactions will consume less of the initial element, often preserving the aura, while 2× reactions consume more and tend to immediately remove the initial element. This is elaborated further in Elemental Gauge Theory .
