See also: Damage § Catalyze Damage Bonus
Additive Reactions (unofficial name) , or simply denoted as "Catalyze Reactions" in Miliastra Wonderland , include Spread and Aggravate .

- Additive Reactions also increase the DMG of the hit that triggers it without dealing DMG of its own. However, they provide a Additive Base DMG Bonus that adds onto base DMG in the DMG formula, instead of multiplying DMG like Amplifying Reactions.
- The Additive Base DMG Bonus provided by Spread is slightly higher than that of Aggravate.
See also: Damage § Lunar Reaction Damage
Lunar Reactions include Lunar-Charged , Lunar-Bloom , and Lunar-Crystallize .

- These reactions can be dealt either directly by a character's talent (all Lunar Reactions), or through a separate instance of damage that takes into account the stats of all contributing characters and is dealt independently of the triggering attacks (all but Lunar-Bloom ).
- In the latter case, these reactions have their Base Damage determined by the type of reaction and the level of the character triggering the reaction.
- The Base Damage is multiplied by a Base DMG Bonus provided by certain Moonsign Benediction Passives , and then again by a percentage determined by the Elemental Mastery of the character. The percentage can be seen in-game in the Details section of the Attributes page.
- Lunar Reaction DMG ignores DMG Bonus and the target's DEF , but is affected by Resistance .
See also: Damage § Stellar Glimmer Reaction Damage
Stellar Glimmer Reactions include Stellar-Conduct and Stellar Swirl .

- These reactions can be dealt either directly by a character's talent (all Stellar Glimmer Reactions), or through a separate instance of damage that takes into account the stats of all contributing characters and is dealt independently of the triggering attacks (all but Stellar-Conduct ).
- In the latter case, these reactions have their Base Damage determined by the type of reaction and the level of the character triggering the reaction.
- The Base Damage is multiplied by a Base DMG Bonus provided by Stellar Jubilee Passives , and then again by a percentage determined by the Elemental Mastery of the character. The percentage can be seen in-game in the Details section of the Attributes page.
- Stellar Glimmer Reaction DMG ignores DMG Bonus and the target's DEF , but is affected by Resistance .
The effects of Elemental Reactions scale off of the stats of the character who triggers the reaction. The stats of the character that produced the initial aura is not considered.

Name: Lunar-Bloom
Type: Elemental Reactions
Group: Lunar Reactions

Lunar-Bloom is the Lunar Reaction triggered by inflicting Dendro on a target that is already affected by Hydro or vice versa, replacing Bloom while a character with a corresponding Moonsign Benediction Passive is in the party . When Lunar-Bloom is triggered, it will grant the party a Verdant Dew in addition to spawning a Dendro Core or Bountiful Core . Verdant Dew can be consumed by certain Talents to deal Lunar-Bloom DMG.
Main article: Damage § Lunar Reaction Damage
Lunar-Bloom does no DMG on its own. Currently, the only way to deal Lunar-Bloom DMG is through character Talents and Constellations.

When Lunar-Bloom is triggered, the player will gain 1 Verdant Dew every 2.5s for 2.5s. The player can have up to 3 Verdant Dew at a time, and when Lunar-Bloom is triggered again while the player is gaining Verdant Dew, the duration will be reset. Verdant Dew lasts indefinitely and persists through party changes, teleportation between maps and Domains , daily resets, and game sessions.

Elemental Reaction: Lunar-Bloom:
- When Dendro meets Hydro , and certain other conditions are met, a special Lunar-Bloom reaction occurs. In addition to the standard Bloom reaction effects, this also provides the party with valuable "Verdant Dew." Certain characters can consume "Verdant Dew" or utilize their Talents to deal Lunar-Bloom DMG to enemies. This DMG can trigger CRIT Hits.

Verdant Dew:
- Within 2.5s after party members trigger Lunar-Bloom reactions, your party will receive 1 Verdant Dew every 2.5s. Your party can have up to 3 Verdant Dew. If you trigger another Lunar-Bloom reaction during this time, the duration of this effect will be reset. Certain characters can consume Verdant Dew to deal Lunar-Bloom DMG to enemies.

Pale Hymn: A hymn passed down by generations of Moonchanters that increases the DMG dealt by Bloom, Hyperbloom, Burgeon, and Lunar-Bloom reactions. Lauma can gain Pale Hymn stacks in the following ways: When using her Elemental Burst Runo: All Hearts Become the Beating Moon. When consuming Moon Song stacks due to using her Elemental Burst Runo: All Hearts Become the Beating Moon. When the Frostgrove Sanctuary triggers the effect of her Constellation "I Offer Blood and Tears to the Moonlight". When party members deal Bloom, Hyperbloom, Burgeon, or Lunar-Bloom DMG, 1 stack of Pale Hymn will be consumed and the DMG dealt will be increased based on Lauma's Elemental Mastery. If this DMG hits multiple opponents at once, then multiple stacks of Pale Hymn will be consumed, depending on how many opponents are hit. The duration for each stack of Pale Hymn is counted independently.
Moon Song: A melody used to weave together hymns. When an Elemental Burst is used, or for a period of time after an Elemental Burst has been used, it can be converted into Pale Hymn stacks that increase the DMG from Bloom, Hyperbloom, Burgeon, and Lunar-Bloom reactions. When Lauma consumes Verdant Dew to perform the Hold version of her Elemental Skill Runo: Dawnless Rest of Karsikko, each Verdant Dew consumed will provide Lauma with 1 stack of Moon Song.
Lunar Domain: The domain that Columbina summons after unleashing the Elemental Burst Moonlit Melancholy. When current active characters are within the Lunar Domain, Lunar Reaction DMG inflicted by all party members will increase.
Gravity Ripple: After unleashing Elemental Skill Eternal Tides, Columbina will summon Gravity Ripple . Gravity Ripple will follow the current active character on the field, while continuously dealing AoE Hydro DMG to surrounding opponents. Additionally, while Gravity Ripple is on the field, and nearby party members trigger Lunar reactions or inflict Lunar Reaction DMG, Columbina will gain the New Moon's Omen effect for 2s, continuously accumulating Gravity. 20 Gravity can be accumulated every 2s. You can have up to 60 Gravity, and it will be removed when the duration of Gravity Ripple ends. Once Gravity is accumulated to its limit, a special Gravity Interference will be triggered. Different effects will be triggered depending on the Lunar reaction type that has accumulated the most Gravity for Columbina. If the Lunar reaction type that has accumulated the most Gravity for Columbina is: Lunar-Charged: Gravity Interference will deal a single instance of Electro AoE DMG . This DMG is considered Lunar-Charged DMG. Lunar-Bloom: Gravity Interference will fire 5 Moondew Sigils at surrounding opponents, dealing Dendro DMG . This DMG is considered Lunar-Bloom DMG. Lunar-Crystallize: Gravity Interference will deal a single instance of Geo AoE DMG . This DMG is considered Lunar-Crystallize DMG.
Verdant Dew: When party members trigger Lunar-Bloom reactions, the party will receive such a resource. Your party will receive 1 Verdant Dew every 2.5s for 2.5s after triggering a Lunar-Bloom reaction. Your party can have up to 3 Verdant Dew. If you trigger another Lunar-Bloom reaction during this time, the duration of this effect will be reset.
Frostgrove Sanctuary: A magical array that protects the Moonchanters and can be summoned by using the Elemental Skill Runo: Dawnless Rest of Karsikko. The Frostgrove Sanctuary will follow the active character, dealing a single instance of AoE Dendro DMG to opponents within the array every 2s. This DMG is considered Elemental Skill DMG.
Shadow Dance: After using the Elemental Skill Senet Strategy: Dance of a Thousand Nights, Nefer will enter this state. While in the Shadow Dance state, if you have at least 1 Verdant Dew, Nefer's Charged Attacks will be replaced with the special Charged Attack Phantasm Performance. Nefer will exit the Shadow Dance state when she unleashes 3 Phantasm Performance(s) or the state's duration ends.
Phantasm Performance: When in the Shadow Dance state caused by her Elemental Skill Senet Strategy: Dance of a Thousand Nights, if you have at least 1 Verdant Dew, Nefer's Charged Attacks will be replaced with the special Charged Attack Phantasm Performance, which will not consume Stamina. Nefer summons shades of herself to perform Coordinated Attacks against enemies. Nefer and the shades will deal 2 and 3 stages of AoE Dendro DMG respectively. DMG dealt by the shades is considered Lunar-Bloom DMG. 1 Verdant Dew will be consumed the first time shades are summoned after every Phantasm Performance.
Elevation: Special DMG Boost effect. It is calculated independently of other DMG Boost effects.

Name: Lunar-Charged
Type: Elemental Reactions
Group: Lunar Reactions

Lunar-Charged is the Lunar Reaction triggered by inflicting Electro on a target that is already affected by Hydro or vice versa, replacing Electro-Charged while a character with a corresponding Moonsign Benediction Passive is in the party . After triggering a Lunar-Charged reaction, a thundercloud will appear that continuously deals Electro DMG to nearby enemies that are affected by both Hydro and Electro .
Main article: Damage § Lunar Reaction Damage

Once created, thunderclouds will deal Electro DMG to all Wet opponents affected by Electro within 5m [ verification needed ] simultaneously every 2s. If the target has not taken Lunar-Charged DMG in the last 2s and is affected by Wet or Electro , the thundercloud will immediately deal DMG to them as soon as the other aura applied to them.

When a thunderclouds deals DMG to opponents, it will consume 0.4 GU of both the Wet and Electro auras simultaneously. Lunar-Charged shares all other properties of Electro-Charged, including damaging the wards of Fatui Skirmisher - Hydrogunner Legionnaires at an increased rate.

Thunderclouds will try to position themselves between active targets and the triggering party. After being created by a Lunar-Charged reaction, they will last for 6s before disappearing. If another Lunar-Charged reaction is triggered, their duration is reset. Only one thundercloud can exist on the field at a time; if a Lunar-Charged reaction is triggered outside of a thundercloud's range, a new thundercloud will appear at the target location while the previous thundercloud will disappear.

This DMG can trigger CRIT Hits, and the DMG dealt is based on all characters who have applied elements during the reaction.

Lunar Domain: The domain that Columbina summons after unleashing the Elemental Burst Moonlit Melancholy. When current active characters are within the Lunar Domain, Lunar Reaction DMG inflicted by all party members will increase.
Heaven and Earth Made Manifest: Summoning a shadow of her former powers, she switches to the Lunar Phase Shift mode. Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam While in the Lunar Phase Shift mode, when Zibai performs Normal Attacks, the fourth attack will deal an additional instance of Geo DMG , which is considered Lunar-Crystallize Reaction DMG.
Lumi: Strike Forms: Lumi has three different Strike Forms. Super Power Form Lumi will use Pound-Pound Pummeler to attack nearby opponents continuously. Every attack will deal 2 instances of AoE Geo DMG . If there are Moondrifts nearby, Lumi will alternate between Pound-Pound Pummeler and Heavy Overdrive Hammer to continuously attack nearby opponents . Heavy Overdrive Hammer will deal AoE Geo DMG which will be considered Lunar-Crystallize Reaction DMG. Ultimate Power Form Lumi will use the ultimate Million Ton Crush, dealing an especially powerful instance of AoE Geo DMG that is considered Lunar-Crystallize Reaction DMG, switching to Standard Power Form. Standard Power Form It might not be as flashy as the other forms, but it still packs a serious punch. Lumi will use Pound-Pound Pummeler at longer intervals to attack nearby opponents continuously. Every attack will deal 2 instances of AoE Geo DMG .
Gravity Ripple: After unleashing Elemental Skill Eternal Tides, Columbina will summon Gravity Ripple . Gravity Ripple will follow the current active character on the field, while continuously dealing AoE Hydro DMG to surrounding opponents. Additionally, while Gravity Ripple is on the field, and nearby party members trigger Lunar reactions or inflict Lunar Reaction DMG, Columbina will gain the New Moon's Omen effect for 2s, continuously accumulating Gravity. 20 Gravity can be accumulated every 2s. You can have up to 60 Gravity, and it will be removed when the duration of Gravity Ripple ends. Once Gravity is accumulated to its limit, a special Gravity Interference will be triggered. Different effects will be triggered depending on the Lunar reaction type that has accumulated the most Gravity for Columbina. If the Lunar reaction type that has accumulated the most Gravity for Columbina is: Lunar-Charged: Gravity Interference will deal a single instance of Electro AoE DMG . This DMG is considered Lunar-Charged DMG. Lunar-Bloom: Gravity Interference will fire 5 Moondew Sigils at surrounding opponents, dealing Dendro DMG . This DMG is considered Lunar-Bloom DMG. Lunar-Crystallize: Gravity Interference will deal a single instance of Geo AoE DMG . This DMG is considered Lunar-Crystallize DMG.
Lunar Phase Shift: After using the Elemental Skill Heaven and Earth Made Manifest, Zibai will change to this mode. This mode lasts at most 15s and has the following properties: Normal and Charged Attacks are converted into Geo DMG that cannot be overridden by other infusions. The Elemental Skill Heaven and Earth Made Manifest will also be converted to the Elemental Skill Spirit Steed's Stride: When Zibai has at least 70 Phase Shift Radiance, she can consume 70 Phase Shift Radiance to unleash Spirit Steed's Stride and cause two instances of Geo DMG. The second instance will be considered Lunar-Crystallize Reaction DMG. A maximum of 100 Phase Shift Radiance points can be accrued, and Zibai can accumulate them in the following ways: She gains 10 points every second she is in the Lunar Phase Shift mode. She gains 5 points when hitting an opponent with her Normal Attacks. She can gain Phase Shift Radiance points in this way once every 0.5s. Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam When nearby party members trigger Lunar-Crystallize, they will also accrue 35 Phase Shift Radiance points for Zibai. Points can be gained this way once every 4s. Unleashing the special elemental skill Spirit Steed's Stride will reset the CD for Phase Shift Radiance gained this way. Zibai will leave this mode after unleashing Spirit Steed's Stride 4 times, or when the skill's duration ends.
The Selenic Adeptus Ascends: When casting the Elemental Skill Heaven and Earth Made Manifest, or when triggering Moondrift Harmony, Zibai gains the Moonfall effect for 4s: The DMG dealt by the 2nd hit of Spirit Steed's Stride is increased by 60% of Zibai's DEF.

The moon-blessed land located in the northwestern regions of Teyvat. Follow the silver thread spun by the new moon, traverse biting gales and desolate tundras as the snow-kissed lakes, fractured like mirrors, reflect their ageless, glacial radiance. The days are bitterly short, and the night stretches on like a dark, yawning maw. But even then, the light and song of the Welkin Moon will dance gently across the faces of visiting travelers. Up at ye towers, and let your lanterns blaze into the darkness! Until the day comes... when true moonlight bathes this land once more.
Genshin Impact Official Website

Nod-Krai , also known as the borderlands and formerly as Nephilheim , is an autonomous region located on the edge of Teyvat in the southernmost part of Snezhnaya , and one of the major regions in Genshin Impact . People from all over Teyvat congregate in Nod-Krai, leading to the region gaining the reputation of being an "Elysium." Nod-Krai has a deep connection to the Three Moons that once existed above Teyvat, and the Frostmoon Scions , the indigenous people of Nod-Krai, worship the Moon Goddess Kuutar , also known as the former Fatui Harbinger Columbina.
The Archon Quest Song of the Welkin Moon takes place in this region.

Nod-Krai was formed from remnant material that was left over after the creation of the Three Moons . It is especially hostile due to the harsh environment and lack of protective and regulative forces aside from the Voynich Guild , and Liben warns the Traveler to be wary if they go there. Those that are suspected to hold a large amount of Mora are also painted as a target by others.

Nod-Krai includes locations such as Nasha Town where the "Speranza" restaurant operates, the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop that produces many different inventions, as well as Hiisi Island that is home to the Frostmoon Scions . According to Helka , the Frostmoon Scions are a strange group that lives in the wilds and forests surrounding Nod-Krai, and people do not generally look into or approach them. They also made several Statues of the New Moon dedicated to Columbina and spread them all across Nod-Krai.

Some of the inhabitants of Nod-Krai are able to use kuuvahki , a special power that originates from the Three Moons and predates the seven elements of Teyvat. A Fatui stronghold operates in Nod-Krai, led by Il Dottore . Before, the area was considered "dangerous yet lively," but in recent times, it has been more dangerous than usual. At some point, large-scale development had been planned for the area, but no traces of it exist to the current day, unless one counts the many scraps lying around. There is also a type of crab species residing in the area far different from those found in Fontaine . At some point after Helka left to explore monsters from the other nations, the Fatui had returned and moved plenty of construction supplies in as part of their "Palestar Edict," with rumors swirling that one or several Fatui Harbingers were present too. There were also "bad" situations to the north regarding Abyss influence.

Ever since the cataclysm , Nod-Krai has been plagued by attacks from a group of Abyssal entities known as The Wild Hunt . The Wild Hunt is controlled by Rerir , one of the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah , and he has been using the Wild Hunt to regain his power and reassemble his body after it was torn apart. In response to the Wild Hunt's threat, the Lightkeepers were established to fight it off, and have been doing so for centuries. Follow Rerir's banishment through the Moon Gate, the Wild Hunt has fell into control by infamous figures of legend like Rotwang and Roland .

After learning new information during their expedition, the Knights of Favonius headed to Nod-Krai with Varka . There, Varka noticed that the situation in Nod-Krai was incredibly tense, warning the Traveler through a letter that they had best be prepared before arriving.

Nod-Krai features many unique mechanics and environmental hazards:

Kuuvahki is an energy similar to Natlan 's Phlogiston and Fontaine 's Arkhe , and is used in a wide variety of mechanics in Nod-Krai. In many places in Nod-Krai, this energy is polarized, shown as blue or red. Certain "unipolar" objects are infused with one polarity of kuuvahki or the other, which are attracted to other unipolar objects of the opposite polarity, and repel objects of the same polarity. In certain situations, the player can enter an empowered state that infuses them with one polarity or the other, enabling them to remotely push or pull kuuvahki infused objects of the appropriate polarity. Some "bipolar" objects can be manipulated by either polarity of kuuvahki. Kuuvahki energy can be used in the following ways:

- Harvest Mora Chests , Portable Bearings , Rainbowdrop Crystals , and kuuvahki-infused Icy Pebbles
- Remotely manipulate and carry ID cards (to deactivate Barrier Generators), Kuuvahki Dewdrops , kuuvahki-infused rocks, and Kuuvahki Relay Mechanisms (though carrying these can attract lightning)
- Arrange Assembly Modules while controlling Bobik
- Destroy Unipolar Crystonite , Recon Bots , and kuuvahki-infused debris
- Disarm the Fatui Oprichniki of their weaponry (or, in the case of higher-ranked Oprichniki officers, stagger them)
- Temporarily disable Landcruisers ( Cutting Edge Fire Support Ground Effect Landcruiser and Force Recon Ground Effect Landcruiser only, ground-based Landcruisers are simply staggered)
- Cause objects emitting Unipolar Fields to attract or repel one another, or leap very high when empowered and standing on a Unipolar Field of the same polarity (often used for solving Moon Mirror puzzles)
- Temporarily turn into a kuuhenki for about 8 seconds. During this time, the player is in an empowered state, and can float, traverse rapidly along the ground, enter Mysterious Mists , and leap high into the air (if near certain kuuvahki-infused plants)

Unpolarized kuuvahki is exclusive to northern Nod-Krai, where it exists in opposition to abyssal energy. Things which are susceptible to unpolarized kuuvahki exist in one of three states: blighted (infected with abyssal energy), fallow, or suffused (empowered with kuuvahki). Many also trigger additional effects when suffused. Some suffused objects can release a kuuvahki current, which charges nearby kuuvahki-susceptible objects.
Some suffused objects may be carried by the player (one at a time):

- Throwing a Glimmerfruit causes it to explode, releasing a kuuvahki current. The plant will generate a new fruit shortly after the old one explodes.
- Cores from Intricate Blooms create a link between the core and the plant when carried. The length of this link can cause certain surrounding objects to move, often creating a pathway. Dropping the core fixes the objects to their current position.
- Mandragora generate a kuuvahki current when dropped or thrown near an unsuffused object, then enter a fallowed state.
- Shattered Barrier Core fragments can be collected and reassembled to clear nearby corruption as part of the World Quest Tower of Inversion in Series Nightingale's Song : Chapter I - Prelude to the Night Vigil .
- Slothsheep seed cores can be carried to guide the Slothsheep to a desired location, or be dropped or thrown to induce it to charge, releasing a kuuvahki current on impact.
- Spirebloom fruit allow the player to deploy a shield when holding down a button. Releasing it unleashes a kuuvahki lightblade. Another button controls the orientation of the lightblade. Lightblades can be used in several ways: Suffusing objects with kuuvahki energy Damaging abyssal monsters Launching them upwards by firing them at Cottonspring Flowers Severing Abyssal Riftlines Parrying attacks from Evil Eyes of Blightseep
- Suffusing objects with kuuvahki energy
- Damaging abyssal monsters
- Launching them upwards by firing them at Cottonspring Flowers
- Severing Abyssal Riftlines
- Parrying attacks from Evil Eyes of Blightseep
Other kuuvahki or abyssal energy mechanics can be found in northern Nod-Krai:

- Abyssal Fog Barriers block access to certain objects, and can be dispelled by kuuvahki currents. Some Fog Barriers require that one or more connected Barriers be dispelled before they will go down themselves.
- Abyssal Riftlines can block passage to the player. They also appear over the heads of NPCs or enemies being manipulated by the Abyss. Sever them with Spirebloom lightblades to remove them.
- Aedon , Illuga 's nightingale familiar, can accompany the player and reveal certain invisible objects during the World Quest Series Nightingale's Song .
- Blightseep Fields continuously drain the HP of a character inside them. Eliminating abyssal entities in the area will dissipate them.
- Evil Eyes of Blightseep will lock onto the player and fire abyssal attacks, which can be blocked by the Spirebloom shield. The Spirebloom lightblade does a small amount of damage to them, but parrying their attacks when the shield flashes will fire a strong deflecting counterattack that will destroy the attacking Evil Eyes in one hit.
- The Solaris Core and Nycalyx are a pair of plants that can be connected by beams of kuuvahki energy chained through other kuuvahki susceptible objects. Connecting them will trigger a powerful blast of kuuvahki which will clear nearby abyssal corruption.
- Cottonspring Flowers can be interacted with to launch the player high into the air. They can also launch certain small objects that are thrown at them, such as Mandragora or Spirebloom lightblades.
- Lunar Conflux Barriers dissipate when they are suffused, releasing any objects trapped within and recharging nearby susceptible objects. Some barriers require multiple kuuvahki charges before they will become suffused.
- Spirit Blooms generate a kuuvahki shield upon becoming suffused. This shield blocks attacks, knocks back abyssal monsters, and suffuses objects within it. Suffused Mandragora will seek the cover of a nearby Spirit Bloom when abyssal enemies are near.
- The Wild Hunt Lurks... is a climate found in Kipumaki Cliff . While within the area affected by this climate, the party will continuously accumulate Abyssal Decay. When the Abyssal Decay gauge is full, the active character will continuously lose HP . Decay accumulation can be slowed by a higher Moonsign level. There are several objects which will continuously decrease the player's accumulated Decay by standing next to them: Suffused Oath Lanterns Suffused Spirit Blooms Teleport Waypoints Allied Lightkeeper NPCs
- Suffused Oath Lanterns
- Suffused Spirit Blooms
- Teleport Waypoints
- Allied Lightkeeper NPCs

- Amazing 'Bots are small, cubical robots found in Nod-Krai, primarily on Lempo Isle . They can be found individually or joined together. They can help the player in a variety of ways, such as displaying hints to the player on their screen "faces," emitting kuuvahki energy to permit the player to enter an empowered state, emitting unipolar fields, or following the player to allow them to be gathered together to solve a puzzle.
- Cleaning Bots can be remotely controlled from certain panels on Paha Isle . They are typically used to access areas the player cannot normally enter, and are infused with kuuvahki energy, allowing manipulation of bipolar objects or empowering the player if they're next to it.
- Deepdark Shields are a shielding mechanic employed by Fishers of Hidden Depths . The shield can only be damaged with Elemental DMG and Elemental Reactions , with Lunar Reactions being three times as effective. When any Fisher's Deepdark Shield is broken, all nearby Fishers lose their Deepdark Shields for a limited time. The Lord of the Hidden Depths: Whisperer of Nightmares also deploys a Deepdark shield. It spawns four shieldless Fishers, which damage the boss's shield when killed. Breaking the boss's shield within 30 seconds will stun and damage the boss and greatly decrease its RES, while failing to do so will unleash a huge AOE attack.
- The Lord of the Hidden Depths: Whisperer of Nightmares also deploys a Deepdark shield. It spawns four shieldless Fishers, which damage the boss's shield when killed. Breaking the boss's shield within 30 seconds will stun and damage the boss and greatly decrease its RES, while failing to do so will unleash a huge AOE attack.
- Iron Coins can be used to halt fleeing Weasel Thieves during the World Quest The Raven's Legacy in Series East of the Moon, West of the Sun . These coins may be connected to the Iron coins from the event Lost Riches .
- Kuuhenki are similar in appearance to Seelie and are also involved in puzzles. Approaching a white kuuhenki will often cause it to lead you to treasure. Blue and red kuuhenki cause the player to enter an empowered state on approach and will follow the player within a particular area. Certain kuuvahki-infused plants allow the player to turn into a kuuhenki for about 8 seconds, allowing them to float, traverse rapidly along the ground, enter patches of mist, and sometimes leap high into the air.
- Kuuhenki's Hidden Troves can be unlocked using Moon Seals which are found in Precious and Luxurious Chests in Nod-Krai. Each area requires 3 specific seals of the matching type: Evermoon , Irismoon , and Frost Moon .
- Lakeside Prisms can be found in the area of the Royal Court of the Seelie in Wavechaser Plain . They are followed in a similar manner to Seelie and can suffuse objects that they approach, helping to rebuild the Court in the World Quest Echoes of a Forsaken Song . Other similar prisms can be found within Dreadshade Mire , some of which assist the player in the World Quest To Turn Each Sin Against the Sinner .
- Lunoculi can be offered at Statue of the New Moon in Nod-Krai for rewards.
- Moonlanes are paths similar to the Spiritways of Natlan which allow you to transform into a kuuhenki and quickly traverse terrain or go places that are otherwise difficult to reach. Some have the player transform into a blue or red kuuhenki, which allows them to manipulate objects in or near their path using attraction and repulsion mechanics.
- Rippleweeds are flytrap-like plants that can be opened by throwing Kuuvahki Dewdrops at them, releasing whatever is inside. The ones around Blue Amber Lake contain Stellafruit , which are used in World Quest The Tale-Telling Heart in Series East of the Moon, West of the Sun .
- Rocks enveloped in kuuvahki can be thrown to break certain objects in the "Post-Apocalyptic Elysium" bunker during the World Quest Return to Sender in Series East of the Moon, West of the Sun .
- Sniffer Moles can help the player find Unipolar Fields that may not be visible in exchange for Kuuvahki Relay Mechanisms. Others in northern Nod-Krai may offer the player Glimmerfruit, or occasionally harmless exploding fruit that temporarily obscure the player's vision.
- The Wasteland Wild Hunt is an Enemy Family in Nod-Krai that are members of The Wild Hunt faction. Completely draining a Wild Hunt enemy's HP or using skills enhanced by Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam causes them to enter a "Grief-Stricken state" for a brief time. In this state, the enemy is immobilized and damage reduces their maximum HP. After about 10 seconds, their HP meter refills and they resume attacking. The enemy will only be defeated when their maximum HP is reduced to zero while in the Grief-Stricken state. Fighting them charges nearby Tideseal Stones , which can be activated when fully charged to damage Wild Hunt enemies.

- Nod-Krai is the first area in which specific characters will have unique interactions in the region: Aino and Ineffa can speak to Knuckle Duckle for a unique cosmetic to their Elemental Burst and Skill respectively when their Friendship Level hits 6 or higher. Frostmoon Scions and Nod-Krai wildlife will react positively to Lauma and Columbina . Flins and Illuga can interact with several Tideseal Stones , understand the speech of the Wasteland Wild Hunt , and access two exclusive Hidden Exploration Objectives . Nefer and Jahoda can gather intel on the people of Nasha Town and exchange them at the Adventurers' Guild to unlock Intel Quests . All Nod-Krai natives additionally have unique conversations with various people across the region. All of them have unique dialogue with Liouba (when completing her challenges) and Hunajatta (when purchasing her candies). Columbina and Lauma have additional dialogue with some Frostmoon Scions NPCs. Nefer and Jahoda have additional dialogue with some Northern Intelligence Network NPCs. Illuga has unique dialogue with some NPCs in Piramida .

- The name "Nod-Krai" may be a composite of: The Land of Nod ( Hebrew : אֶרֶץ־נוֹד‎ – ʾereṣ-Nōḏ), a place mentioned in the Book of Genesis where Cain was exiled by God after Cain had murdered his brother Abel . Krai ( Russian : Край Kray ) is a type of federal subject of the Russian Federation , and the name of administrative units in Czechia and Slovakia ( kraj ), with the word meaning "edge," "country," or "region" in Russian, Polish, Ukrainian, Belarusian, and Bulgarian.

- Nod-Krai's historic name, "Nephilheim," may be a reference to: Niflheim , a primordial realm of ice and cold in Norse cosmology. Nephilim , a group of mysterious, powerful beings mentioned in the Bible who have been variably interpreted as giants, descendants of Seth and Cain, the offspring of angels and humans, and more. The term "Nephilim" is often confused with "Niflheim."

The nation of eternal winter in the north of Teyvat. Do not fear the bitter cold, nor shrink from the trials ahead. Face the snowstorms roaring across the sky, cross the silent and solemn frozen wastes and the cities thundering with steel, and press on into a winter untouched by the mercy of the gods. There, raise your eyes to the unblemished Pale Star. Though the extreme cold has long extinguished the warmth of bygone days, stand with those whose hearts still blaze with desire and sorrow, and bear witness as the old world burns upon the ice.
Genshin Impact Official Website

Snezhnaya ( Russian : Снежная Snezhnaya , "Snowy" ) is one of the seven nations of Teyvat and one of the major regions in Genshin Impact . It is the nation that worships the Tsaritsa , the Cryo Archon and God of Love. The Fatui , a military force under her control, is particularly notorious for their unwavering devotion and unscrupulous methods in enacting her will. The autonomous region Nod-Krai is located at the southernmost part of Snezhnaya.
Archon Quest Chapter VII takes place in this region.

Access to Snezhnaya is unlocked after completing the Archon Quest Prologue : Act III - Song of the Dragon and Freedom , but only a small part of Volkodlak Tundra is available. A Teleport Waypoint in Volkodlak Tundra is automatically unlocked and is where Chapter VII is automatically accepted. A very small area surrounding Sretomorozsk is available once players start Archon Quest Gunfire in the Silent Lands in Chapter VII : Act I - Everwinter Without Mercy , and the entire nation becomes accessible once said quest is completed. Players will be quickly overwhelmed by the sheer cold if they attempt to progress without meeting the requirements, as the borders of the restricted area behave like a Subzero Zone .

Snezhnaya is a region of perpetual winter storms; Nadia states that blizzards can last for a month straight and despite being in the midst of danger, its people look up to the sky and are just happy to be alive. Tartaglia claims that people would literally freeze to death if they didn't keep moving outside. At night, the Snezhnayan sky can see a beautiful aurora of dancing light. Each settlement within Snezhnaya contains a Kresnik's Torch , which are fueled by Kresnik Kristall .

Technologically, Snezhnaya is much more advanced than the other regions on Teyvat. Venti states that the Fatui are the strongest out of the seven regions' military, which is supported by the fact that all of their known fighting members utilize elemental attacks. The description for Agent's Sacrificial Knife calls it a "weapon made with superior Snezhnayan technology." The Fatui Skirmishers wear mechanical suits of varying degrees, and some of its members use guns and cannons in battle. Alice , who has visited Snezhnaya, recalls seeing massive factories, which she wrote down in her Teyvat Travel Guide , and Il Dottore built a factory in Liyue to conduct Ruin Guard research which is fully automated.
Snezhnaya is stated to be considered the same status as Mondstadt , as an independent and not belonging to any other nation, according to Jean .

The Adventurers' Guild originates from Snezhnaya; while this fact doesn't seem to be a secret, few people comment on it and the Guild doesn't face the same apprehension that people regard the Fatui with. It was also hinted that Katheryne , the receptionist(s) for the Adventurers' Guild, are a series of androids created for the role: the Katherynes in all regions so far are identical, and have "Error..." and "Rebooting..." idle quotes. This is further emphasized by the Katheryne stationed in Liyue, as she side-steps the Traveler questioning about her identity. Katheryne's identity as a "bionic Snezhnayan puppet" was confirmed by Nahida .

- Chill Zones - Some areas of Snezhnaya are far colder than others, and the intensity of the cold determines how fast Sheer Cold is accumulated. Players must keep themselves warm by finding kristall, either through outcrops or particular wildlife. Unlike the sheer cold system in Dragonspine, Snezhnaya's sheer cold affects all party members and deals more damage.
- The Shadow Realm - a corrupted region which are entered through rifts in the area. Players will enter a third-person shooter perspective and eliminate the corrupted entities inside the realm. They can enhance their guns by exploring more of Snezhnaya.
- Rail System - Players can utilize their train to travel across various stations situated across Snezhnaya. The train additionally has features such as a Crafting Bench , remote access to the Adventurers' Guild and a shooting range for practice.
- Prime Ice - players can harvest Prime Ice to create various contraptions and other items to aid them on their journey across Snezhnaya. Utilizing Stellar-Conduct reactions to create a Polestar Field near the construct will enhance its capabilities. Launching Platform: Launches the player upwards. Single-Use Construct Blueprints: Some areas may have a special item that can only be temporarily made in the area. Snowball Launcher: Transforms the player into a snowball for quick access across high elevated areas or down slopes. Link Mechanism: Can be used for quickly navigating across large and/or high elevation areas. Basic Heat Source: A simple heat source that will allow the player to remain warm without relying on Kresnik energy. The flame can be dragged a short distance away and can also be used to melt specific blocks of ice. Grappling Gun: Can be used to pull items or destroy weak walls with grappling hooks on them. Cubes: Can be used as stepping stones or to open/close obstacles.

- In the trailer Teyvat Chapter Storyline Preview: Travail , under the title of the quest Everwinter Without Mercy , the line written in Teyvat's Latin script reads " Ducam regina mea gloria haud pluribus impar ," which roughly means "I, nigh unmatched Queen by my glory, shall be guide." The last part of the sentence is likely modified from nec pluribus impar , a Latin motto adopted by Louis XIV of France. The motto and its meaning are obscure and almost untranslatable. While Snezhnaya's Archon Quest Chapter was originally designated as Act VI in Travail , it was renumbered to Chapter VII following the addition of Song of the Welkin Moon , even though Song of the Welkin Moon was never officially designated Chapter VI.

- "Snezhnaya" ( Russian : Снежная Snezhnaya , "Snowy" ) is a Russian adjective for "snowy," expecting a feminine noun to follow (most likely Страна Strana or Земля Zemlya — Russian words for "country" or "land" respectively, both of which are feminine and are permitted to be omitted for a synecdoche in such a context). The game's voiceover places the accent on the second syllable (Snezh- na -ya); however, in the original word, it's on the first ( Snezh -na-ya). During the first Closed Beta Test, Snezhnaya was instead named "Prekrasnaya" ( Прекрасная Prekrasnaya , "Beautiful" ). Snezhnaya's Chinese name, 至冬 Zhìdōng , is an anagram of the Chinese term for winter solstice ( 冬至 Dōngzhì ).

- Snezhnaya's Chinese name, 至冬 Zhìdōng , is an anagram of the Chinese term for winter solstice ( 冬至 Dōngzhì ).
- "Zapolyarny" ( Russian : Заполярный Zapolyarnyy , "Beyond the Arctic Circle" ) roughly translates to "beyond the Arctic Circle" or "inside the Polar region."
- "Morepesok" ( Russian : Морепесок Morepesok , "Sea-Sand" ) is a compound of the words for море more , "sea" and песок pesok , "sand," itself referring to a beach or coastline as a sort of kenning.
- "Snezhnograd" ( Russian : Снежноград Snezhnograd , "Snowy City" ) uses the Russian root - град -grad , "city," which was traditionally used when establishing cities in Russia.
- The name "Novokitezhgrad" ( Russian : Новокитежград Novokitezhgrad , "New Kitezh City" ) contains the name Kitezh , a legendary city in central Russia that sank into a lake, similar to Atlantis in Greek mythology.
- "Tsaritsa" ( Russian : Царица Tsaritsa , "Tsarina" ), used to refer to their Archon, is the feminine form of Tsar , which ultimately derives from Caesar, a title of Roman emperors. So far, no one has called her by her true name; Snezhnayans call her by her title, while Venti and Zhongli call her "the Cryo Archon."

- Snezhnaya is primarily inspired by by a mix of Medieval, Tsarist and Soviet Russia (primarily Russian Arctic and Siberia in regards to landscape), and often uses Russian words for names. However, it also draws from other European nations as well, such as using Italian commedia dell'arte stock characters' names for the Harbingers.
- Snezhnaya's affiliation with brutal winters parallels Russia's climate, which has famously contributed to the failures of the many military campaigns made against it.
- Tartaglia addresses the Traveler as "comrade" in his voice-overs , the usual translation of "tovarishch" ( Russian : товарищ tovarishch ) used in Soviet/Bolshevik Russia. In the Japanese version of Childe's Character Miscellany, he starts off his letter ("Dearest sister...") in Russian.

- Fire-Water ( Russian : огненная вода ognennaya voda , "fiery water" ), which Angel's Share bartender Charles deems the strongest wine he knows of, originates from Snezhnaya. It is a reference to the liquor vodka , a drink commonly associated with Russia. In real life, Russian Vodka is normally 45-55% Ethanol, and some Vodkas are more than 80% Ethanol, making Vodka one of the most alcoholic drinks in the world.

Name: Team Bonus
Type: Combat Game Systems
Team Bonuses are additional effects corresponding to the attributes of Characters present in a Party .
Elemental Resonance redirects here. For other uses, see Resonance .
Current Party Elemental Types
When you have a full party, you will receive Elemental Resonance effects that correspond to the Elemental Types present in the party.
Elemental Resonance effects depend on the elements of the first four party members, apply in Co-Op Mode , and do not require all party members to be alive.

Except for Protective Canopy, each Resonance requires two or more characters of the same element among the first four party slots. Having more than two characters of the same element does not further enhance the corresponding Resonance.

In Co-Op Mode, if part of the party is inside a Domain , the resonance will only be determined by the characters that are in the Domain, and only characters in the Domain will benefit from the bonuses.

Moonsign

When Moonsign characters are in the party, the party will attain a Moonsign Level corresponding to the number of such characters. When the party reaches "Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam," Moonsign characters will be enhanced. Non-Moonsign characters can also provide buffs to the party.
Aino; Columbina; Flins; Illuga; Ineffa; Jahoda; Lauma; Linnea; Nefer; Zibai;

rows: All characters in the party will gain the "Moonsign: Nascent Gleam" effect.

All characters in the party will gain the "Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam" effect, enhancing certain Talents and Skills of Moonsign characters. Unless otherwise stated, when Moonsign Level reaches Ascendant Gleam, the effects of Nascent Gleam will also apply. In addition, for 20s after a non-Moonsign character casts an Elemental Skill or Elemental Burst , they will increase the Lunar Reaction DMG dealt by all nearby characters based on their own Elemental Type , up to a maximum of 36%. This effect cannot stack. If the character's Elemental Type is: Pyro , Electro , or Cryo : Increases this DMG by 0.9% for every 100 ATK . Hydro : Increases this DMG by 0.6% for every 1,000 Max HP . Geo : Increases this DMG by 1% for every 100 DEF . Anemo or Dendro : Increases this DMG by 2.25% for every 100 Elemental Mastery .

Main article: Nightsoul's Blessing § Nightsoul Burst

When there is at least one Natlanese character in the party, a Nightsoul Burst can be triggered at set intervals. For every Natlanese characters in the party, the interval between Nightsoul Bursts will decrease: 18 seconds for 1 character, 12 seconds for 2 characters, and 9 seconds for 3 or more characters. Characters like Bennett or a Pyro-aligned Traveler do not count toward enabling Nightsoul Burst or decreasing its cooldown, even if they are canonically from Natlan or are able to enter the Nightsoul's Blessing state, respectively.

Wish feature has been unlocked. Wish upon the sky filled with a blanket of stars, and pray that they would peek down at earth and grant you various characters and weapons.
Wishes are the gacha system in Genshin Impact . There are two main types of Wishes: the permanent Standard Wish, Wanderlust Invocation , and limited-time Event Wishes for Characters and Weapons .
Players can unlock wishes after completing the Archon Quest Knights of Favonius in Prologue : Act I - The Outlander Who Caught the Wind , which players can reach at around Adventure Rank 5.

- Character Event Wish
- Character Event Wish-2
- Weapon Event Wish
- Chronicled Wish
- Lightrace Wish
- Novice Wish
- Standard Wish
Acquaint Fate

The "Standard Wish," Wanderlust Invocation , is always available and requires Acquaint Fate to wish from it. The Beginners' Wish is available indefinitely until all 20 wishes are made, has a 20% discount on the Acquaint Fate required to wish, and guarantees the player receives Noelle and one other 4- or 5-star character within the 20 wishes.
Intertwined Fate

Limited-time Event Wishes are split into two wishes, one for characters and one for weapons, and as the name implies, they are only available for a limited time. Event Wishes require Intertwined Fates instead of Acquaint Fates.

Character Event Wishes have one promotional 5★ character and three featured 4★ characters. Weapon Event Wishes will have two promotional 5★ weapons and five 4★ featured weapons. Both the promotional 5★ and featured 4★ items will have an increased probability for players to wish them when compared to the basic rates when the guarantees are factored in.

Players can buy either of the Fates for 160 Primogems each in the Wishes menu or through Paimon's Bargains . There are also in-game methods of obtaining Fates; see their respective pages for more information.

- 4★ drop guarantee: If a player does not obtain any 4★ (or above) item within 9 wishes in a row, the 10th wish is guaranteed to be a 4★ (or higher) item. (On guarantee, the probability of getting a 4★ item is 99.4%, and the probability of getting a 5★ item is 0.6%.) This counter will reset if the player obtains any 4★ item.

- Featured 4★ character guarantee: Every time a player obtains a 4★ item, there is a 50% chance it will be one of the featured 4★ characters. If the 4★ item obtained is not one of the featured characters, then the next 4★ item obtained is guaranteed to be one of the featured characters. Thus it requires a maximum of 20 wishes to obtain one of the featured 4★ characters.

( On average , a greater proportion of 5★ items are dropped between 74 and 90 pity.) This counter will reset if the player obtains any 5★ item. Character Event Wishes do not contain 5★ weapons in their item pool, as such each 5★ drop will be a character.

Thus it requires a maximum of 180 wishes to guarantee obtaining the promotional 5★ character.

The initial maximum number of stacks is 3, with each stack lasting for 9s (each stack's duration is counted independently).

Solo Dance Double: A psychic double of Odette's that dances a duet with her. May be summoned to the field through her Elemental Skill or Elemental Burst. Alternates between the Plume and Wing dance moves to periodically attack nearby opponents, dealing AoE Cryo DMG . A maximum of one Solo Dance Double summoned by Odette is allowed on the field at any one time. Additionally, when there is a Dance Double summoned by Odette nearby, her Elemental Skill Adagio: Phantom Night Dancers is changed to the special Elemental Skill Adagio: Coda at Dawn's Tolling.
Adagio: Coda at Dawn's Tolling: Odette's special Elemental Skill, which deals to nearby opponents AoE Cryo DMG over time. Then, when the dance duel ends, she deals another instance of AoE Cryo DMG that is considered Stellar-Conduct DMG. During the dance duet, Odette can control the direction of the dance steps. Radiance: Stellar Glimmer : The DMG dealt when the dance duet ends is changed to AoE Cryo DMG of the corresponding Stellar reaction type. Additionally, after Odette unleashes the special Elemental Skill Adagio: Coda at Dawn's Tolling, should she be in the Radiance: Stellar Glimmer state while her Dance Double is still on the field, the Dance Double's two dance move types will also deal additional AoE Cryo DMG of the corresponding Stellar Glimmer reaction type.

As she sees it, not every grain of wheat that falls upon the earth will grow into an ear, while those who obstruct her, once burned to ashes, can certainly be used to nourish flowers.
All Is Ash is Arlecchino 's Elemental Skill .

- When this skill hits at least one enemy , it generates 5 Elemental Particles .
- Blood-Debt Directive DMG does not snapshot and will be affected by changes in Arlecchino's stats after the ability is cast.
- Arlecchino obtains Invincibility Frames during this skill for the duration that she disappears.
- To absorb nearby Blood-Debt Directives, Arlecchino only needs to initiate a Charged Attack. The Charged Attack does not need to hit and may be canceled, such as by dashing.
- Arlecchino cannot absorb Blood-Debt Directives from Stormterror Dvalin .
Passive Effects:

- Passive Talent 1, Agony Alone May Be Repaid : " Blood-Debt Directives have the following characteristics: Arlecchino will be granted a Bond of Life worth 130% of her Max HP when an opponent to which she herself applied a Directive is defeated. 5s after a Directive is applied, it will be upgraded to a Blood-Debt Due. When absorbed, it will instead grant Arlecchino a Bond of Life worth 130%. A Bond of Life created in the aforementioned ways cannot exceed the original limit on the value of Bonds of Life obtained through All Is Ash ."
- Arlecchino will be granted a Bond of Life worth 130% of her Max HP when an opponent to which she herself applied a Directive is defeated.
- 5s after a Directive is applied, it will be upgraded to a Blood-Debt Due. When absorbed, it will instead grant Arlecchino a Bond of Life worth 130%.
Constellation Effects:

- Constellation Level 2, "All Rewards and Retribution, Mine to Bestow..." : " Blood-Debt Directives are now already Blood-Debt Due when first applied. When Arlecchino absorbs such a Due, she unleashes Balemoon Bloodfire in front of her, dealing 900% of her ATK as AoE Pyro DMG and increasing her All Elemental RES and Physical RES by 20% for 15s. This effect can trigger once every 10s. You must first unlock the Ascension Talent 'Agony Alone May Be Repaid.'"

utility1: Utility Expedition Nod-Krai Expedition Length Reduction
Backstreet Guile is Jahoda 's Utility Passive .

- This passive grants Jahoda access to the Intel Hunt feature, which is only available to members of the Curatorium of Secrets . When Jahoda is near certain NPCs , her Elemental Skill will be replaced with a special intel-gathering skill. Using it on these NPCs will reveal additional information about them and potentially unlock exclusive dialogue and/or quests . For each NPC, gathering intel from them for the first time will reward Recorded Intel ×1 . Recorded Intel can be exchanged with Katheryne to unlock Intel Quests . The intel-gathering skill has a fixed cooldown of 8.5 seconds, but uses Jahoda's standard Elemental Skill animation. Curatorium members can gather intel from a combined total of 6 new NPCs per Weekly Reset . It is commonly believed throughout Teyvat that moon phases other than the full moon are mere metaphors of ill-omen, used only by those who practice alchemy and astrology. She saw this crimson moon in her dreams many times. Were those portents of disaster? Indeed they were, but the destined catastrophes belonged to those who enraged her.
Balemoon Rising is Arlecchino 's Elemental Burst .

- As Balemoon Rising does not remove Arlecchino's Bond of Life the healing granted by Balemoon Rising is absorbed by Bond of Life bringing the talent's effective healing to 50% of her Bond of Life and 150% of her ATK, excluding any healing bonuses.
Constellation Effects:

- Constellation Level 4, "You Shall Love and Protect Each Other Henceforth..." : "When Arlecchino successfully absorbs a Blood-Debt Directive, Balemoon Rising's CD will decrease by 2s and 15 Elemental Energy will be restored to her. This effect can occur once every 10s."
- Constellation Level 5, "For Alone, We Are as Good as Dead..." : Increases this talent's level by 3, up to a maximum of 15.
- Constellation Level 6, "From This Day On, We Shall Delight in New Life Together." : "The DMG of Balemoon Rising is increased by Arlecchino's ATK multiplied by 700% of Arlecchino's current Bond of Life percentage. For 20s after Arlecchino uses All Is Ash, both her Normal Attacks and Elemental Burst gain 10% increased CRIT Rate and 70% increased CRIT DMG. This effect can be triggered up to once every 15s."

Lumi: Strike Forms: Lumi has three different Strike Forms. Super Power Form Lumi will use Pound-Pound Pummeler to attack nearby opponents continuously. Every attack will deal 2 instances of AoE Geo DMG . If there are Moondrifts nearby, Lumi will alternate between Pound-Pound Pummeler and Heavy Overdrive Hammer to continuously attack nearby opponents . Heavy Overdrive Hammer will deal AoE Geo DMG which will be considered Lunar-Crystallize Reaction DMG. Ultimate Power Form Lumi will use the ultimate Million Ton Crush, dealing an especially powerful instance of AoE Geo DMG that is considered Lunar-Crystallize Reaction DMG, switching to Standard Power Form. Standard Power Form It might not be as flashy as the other forms, but it still packs a serious punch. Lumi will use Pound-Pound Pummeler at longer intervals to attack nearby opponents continuously. Every attack will deal 2 instances of AoE Geo DMG .
Elevation: Special DMG Boost effect. It is calculated independently of other DMG Boost effects.

Riptide Flash: A fully-charged Aimed Shot that hits an opponent affected by Riptide deals consecutive bouts of AoE DMG. Can occur once every 0.7s. Riptide Burst: Defeating an opponent affected by Riptide creates a Hydro burst that inflicts the Riptide status on nearby opponents hit. Plunging Attack Fires off a shower of arrows in mid-air before falling and striking the ground, dealing AoE DMG upon impact. When Tartaglia is in Foul Legacy: Raging Tide's Melee Stance, he cannot perform a plunging attack.

Verdant Dew: When party members trigger Lunar-Bloom reactions, the party will receive such a resource. Your party will receive 1 Verdant Dew every 2.5s for 2.5s after triggering a Lunar-Bloom reaction. Your party can have up to 3 Verdant Dew. If you trigger another Lunar-Bloom reaction during this time, the duration of this effect will be reset.

Dawnbearing Songbird: Summons the trusty messenger bird, 'Aedon.' Different effects are produced depending on whether the skill is Tapped or Held. Tap Aedon dashes towards enemies in front, dealing Geo DMG to enemies it comes into contact with. Hold Enter aiming mode, and command Aedon to dash towards opponents being aimed at, dealing Geo DMG to opponents it comes into contact with.
Shadowless Reflection: Light the lamp, dealing AoE Geo DMG , and gain Haunted Night's Oriole-Song effect for 20s. When this effect is active, Illuga gains 21 stacks of Nightingale's Song. It can increase the Geo DMG inflicted by current active characters. When Normal Attacks, Charged Attacks, Plunging Attacks, Elemental Skills, and Elemental Bursts of nearby active party members deal Geo DMG to opponents, 1 stack of Nightingale’s Song is consumed to increase the DMG dealt. Increase in DMG is based on Illuga’s Elemental Mastery. If DMG is inflicted by Lunar-Crystallize, DMG dealt will increase further. When Geo DMG dealt in this manner hits multiple opponents, multiple stacks of Nightingale's Song will be consumed, depending on how many opponents are hit. Additionally, if there are Geo Constructs created by nearby party members on the battlefield while Illuga unleashes his Elemental Burst, or when nearby party members create Geo Constructs while Haunted Night's Oriole-Song is active, every Geo Construct on the battlefield will allow Illuga to gain 5 additional stacks of Nightingale's Song. Within 20s after unleashing his Elemental Burst, Illuga can gain a maximum of 15 additional stacks of Nightingale’s Song this way. When all stacks of Nightingale's Song have been consumed, or when the state's duration ends, the Haunted Night's Oriole-Song effect will end.

If this aforementioned DMG is inflicted by a Lunar-Crystallize reaction, increase in DMG is equal to 48%/96%/160% of Illuga's Elemental Mastery.

The Eternal Moon's orbit guides the rise and fall of the tides. With a languid motion, the goddess lets her hand fall, drawing forth a ripple across the Primordial Sea, the great ocean, and numberless crowds.
Eternal Tides is Columbina 's Elemental Skill .

- When this skill hits at least one enemy , it generates 1.3333333 Elemental Particles .
- Gravity Ripple attacks once every 2 seconds.
- Gravity Interference can be triggered a maximum of once every 6 seconds.
Passive Effects:
- Passive Talent 1, Lunacy's Lure : "When triggering Gravity Interference , Columbina gains the Lunacy effect, increasing her CRIT Rate by 5% for 10s. This effect can be stacked up to 3 times."

- Constellation Level 1, Radiance Over Blossoms and Peaks : "Unleashing her Elemental Skill Eternal Tides will immediately trigger an effect equivalent to the effect of Gravity Interference . This effect can be triggered once every 15s. Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam When Gravity Interference is triggered, if the Lunar reaction type that has accumulated the most Gravity for Columbina is: Lunar-Charged : Your current active character will recover 6 Energy . Lunar-Bloom : Your active character's interruption resistance will be increased for 8s. Lunar-Crystallize : Summons a Rainsea Shield . The Rainsea Shield's DMG absorption is based on 12% of Columbina's Max HP , and it will absorb Hydro DMG with 250% effectiveness for 8s. All nearby party members' Lunar Reaction DMG is elevated by 1.5%."

When Gravity Interference is triggered, Columbina will receive the Lunar Brilliance effect, which increases her Max HP by 40% for 8s. Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam : When Lunar Brilliance is active, if, during the current trigger of Gravity Interference , the Lunar reaction type that has accumulated the most Gravity for Columbina is: Lunar-Charged : ATK of your current active character increases. This effect can be triggered at most once every 15s. All nearby party members' Lunar Reaction DMG is elevated by 1.5%."

Gravity Ripple: After unleashing Elemental Skill Eternal Tides, Columbina will summon Gravity Ripple . Gravity Ripple will follow the current active character on the field, while continuously dealing AoE Hydro DMG to surrounding opponents. Additionally, while Gravity Ripple is on the field, and nearby party members trigger Lunar reactions or inflict Lunar Reaction DMG, Columbina will gain the New Moon's Omen effect for 2s, continuously accumulating Gravity. 20 Gravity can be accumulated every 2s. You can have up to 60 Gravity, and it will be removed when the duration of Gravity Ripple ends. Once Gravity is accumulated to its limit, a special Gravity Interference will be triggered. Different effects will be triggered depending on the Lunar reaction type that has accumulated the most Gravity for Columbina. If the Lunar reaction type that has accumulated the most Gravity for Columbina is: Lunar-Charged: Gravity Interference will deal a single instance of Electro AoE DMG . This DMG is considered Lunar-Charged DMG. Lunar-Bloom: Gravity Interference will fire 5 Moondew Sigils at surrounding opponents, dealing Dendro DMG . This DMG is considered Lunar-Bloom DMG. Lunar-Crystallize: Gravity Interference will deal a single instance of Geo AoE DMG . This DMG is considered Lunar-Crystallize DMG.
Elevation: Special DMG Boost effect. It is calculated independently of other DMG Boost effects.

Spirit Blade: A weapon with special power that Vesna can summon. Attacks the opponent alongside Vesna to deal Anemo DMG . Vesna can summon Spirit Blades through the following ways: By unleashing the special Elemental Skill Windborne Sword at Lv. 2 and Lv. 3; By using the Elemental Burst For the Tsaritsa!; or By using Windborne Sword·: Transpose in the Constellation Unwavering Ardor. Radiance: Stellar Swirl: DMG dealt by the Spirit Blades become Anemo DMG that is considered Stellar Swirl reaction DMG instead.

pairs: Normal Attack Generates threads that control her weapon using formulae, performing up to 3 consecutive strikes. Charged Attack Summons the Facilitatrice Automatisee Generaliste Interactive et Omnitache, or " Fagio ," and switches it to Decoding mode: Unleashes a sweeping fire attack on enemies in front, as well as periodically fires condensed beams, dealing AoE Cryo DMG . Radiance: Stellar Glimmer : The condensed beams will instead deal AoE Cryo DMG that is considered the corresponding Stellar Glimmer DMG. While in Decoding mode, Fagio's Decoding Power will continuously increase. Firing condensed beams will also further increase its Decoding Power. When Fagio's Decoding Power reaches the maximum of 100 points, it switches to Power Overdrive mode, in which it fires at opponents with longer intervals, dealing Cryo DMG . It will be unable to switch to Decoding mode at this time. When not in Decoding mode, Fagio's Decoding Power gradually decreases. When Sandrone is off-field, she will focus on maintaining Fagio, causing its Decoding Power to decrease at 300% the original rate. Fagio exits Power Overdrive mode when its Decoding Power has decreased to under 50. Plunging Attack Plunges from midair to strike the ground below, dealing DMG to opponents along their path and causing AoE DMG on landing.

While in Decoding mode, Fagio's Decoding Power will continuously increase. Firing condensed beams will also further increase its Decoding Power. When Fagio's Decoding Power reaches the maximum of 100 points, it switches to Power Overdrive mode, in which it fires at opponents with longer intervals, dealing Cryo DMG . It will be unable to switch to Decoding mode at this time. When not in Decoding mode, Fagio's Decoding Power gradually decreases. When Sandrone is off-field, she will focus on maintaining Fagio, causing its Decoding Power to decrease at 300% the original rate. Fagio exits Power Overdrive mode when its Decoding Power has decreased to under 50. Plunging Attack Plunges from midair to strike the ground below, dealing DMG to opponents along their path and causing AoE DMG on landing.

Foul Legacy: Raging Tide is Tartaglia 's Elemental Skill .

- Melee Stance ends when Tartaglia leaves the field.
- The cooldown does not start until Melee Stance ends.
- When Riptide Slash hits at least one enemy , it generates 1 Elemental Particle . This particle generation has a cooldown of 3 seconds. This cooldown is shared with the Riptide Flash particle generation.
- This particle generation has a cooldown of 3 seconds. This cooldown is shared with the Riptide Flash particle generation.
- The Riptide Slash AoE has quadratic scaling against mobs of enemies that are grouped together. That is, suppose there are n {\displaystyle n} enemies each affected by Riptide grouped close together. If Tartaglia uses his Elemental Skill to attack the n enemies in the cluster at once, it will trigger Riptide Slash for each enemy. Each Riptide Slash will do local AoE damage hitting surrounding enemies. So there will be n {\displaystyle n} Riptide Slashes, each hitting n − 1 {\displaystyle n-1} enemies. In total, there will be n + n ( n − 1 ) = n 2 {\displaystyle n + n(n-1) = n^2} instances of damage against n {\displaystyle n} enemies for each time Tartaglia procs Riptide Slash in melee stance. So for mobs grouped close together (e.g., via Crowd Control abilities of Sucrose , Kazuha , The Viridescent Hunt , etc.), Tartaglia's Riptide Slash DMG will scale quadratically with the number of enemies in the cluster.

- Tartaglia's Interruption Resistance is increased while in Melee Stance.
- In Melee stance Plunging Attacks are disabled.
- The stance switch animations will be skipped if this skill is used while walking or running. However, Stance Switch DMG will still be dealt when switching to Melee Stance.

- Passive Talent 2, Sword of Torrents : "When Tartaglia is in Foul Legacy: Raging Tide 's Melee stance, on dealing a CRIT hit , Normal and Charged Attacks apply the Riptide status effects to opponents."
Artifacts and Weapons Interactions:

- Normal Attack effects apply to Ranged Stance and Melee Stance. Also affects the damage of Riptide Flash and Riptide Burst.
- Charged Attack effects apply to his Ranged Stance's Aimed Shot and Melee Stance's Charged Attack.
- Effects that require an arrow to be fired, such as the passives of Amos' Bow and Slingshot , cannot be triggered in Melee Stance.
- Effects that require hitting weak spots, such as the passive of Prototype Crescent , can be triggered in Melee Stance.
- Elemental Skill effects apply to the initial Melee Stance change and Riptide Slash.

Riptide Slashes and Riptide Flashes triggered by this Constellation effect are not subject to the time intervals that would typically apply to these two Riptide effects, nor do they have any effect on those time intervals."

pairs: Concentrates the power of the winds to break free from the shackles of the earth, dealing AoE Anemo DMG before leaping into the air and entering the Windfavored state. Windfavored The Wanderer cannot perform Plunging Attacks in this state. When he uses Normal and Charged Attacks, they will be converted into Kuugo: Fushoudan and Kuugo: Toufukai respectively; the DMG they deal and their AoE will be increased, and their DMG will be considered Normal and Charged Attack DMG respectively. Kuugo: Toufukai will not consume Stamina. The Wanderer will hover persistently during this time. While this state is active, the Wanderer's movements gain the following properties: Persistently consumes Kuugoryoku Points to maintain this hovering state. When sprinting, additional Kuugoryoku Points will be consumed for the Wanderer to accelerate mid-air. Holding sprint will cause persistent Kuugoryoku Point consumption to maintain speed. This effect will replace his default sprint. Jumping expends extra Kuugoryoku Points to increase hovering height. Holding jump will cause persistent Kuugoryoku Point consumption to keep increasing hovering height. Running out of Kuugoryoku Points will end the Windfavored state. A second cast during the duration of Windfavored will also end it.

Hanega: Song of the Wind is Wanderer 's Elemental Skill .

- The cooldown does not start until the Windfavored state ends.
- When a Normal or Charged Attack during the Windfavored State hits at least one enemy , it generates 1 Elemental Particle . A non-converted Normal Attack can also generate particles if the Windfavored State is activated before said attack hits an enemy. This particle generation has a cooldown of 2 seconds. If only Normal and Charged Attacks are performed in the Windfavored state, up to 5 particles can be generated. This may change if other point-consuming actions are performed or if extra Kuugoryoku Points are gained.
- A non-converted Normal Attack can also generate particles if the Windfavored State is activated before said attack hits an enemy.
- This particle generation has a cooldown of 2 seconds.
- If only Normal and Charged Attacks are performed in the Windfavored state, up to 5 particles can be generated. This may change if other point-consuming actions are performed or if extra Kuugoryoku Points are gained.
- During the casting animation of this skill, the Wanderer is immune to being Frozen .
- If the Wanderer falls to the ground after being Frozen mid-air, the Windfavored state will end when the Frozen state ends.
- If the Wanderer is staggered mid-air, the player can press sprint or jump to immediately recover. Doing so will not consume extra Kuugoryoku Points, and pressing Sprint will not trigger Gales of Reverie if it is available.
- During the Windfavored state, the Wanderer will be unaffected by quest steps that force the character to walk.
- Kuugoryoku Point consumption begins 3 frames (60FPS) after activating this skill.
- While in Windfavored state Plunging Attacks are disabled.

Rushing waters are rarely seen in his snowy homeland . Perhaps his ability to command water is due to his understanding of just how precious it is.
Havoc: Obliteration is Tartaglia 's Elemental Burst .

- The Melee Stance version of this Elemental Burst drains energy later than most others.
- For more information on Riptide, see Cutting Torrent .
- If an enemy would die in one hit from the Range Stance version, Riptide Burst will still trigger, even if the enemy did not have Riptide applied to them before using the Elemental Burst.
- If an enemy with Riptide dies from the first hit of the Melee Stance version, both Riptide Blast and Riptide Burst will trigger.
- If an enemy dies to the Riptide Blast effect of this Elemental Burst, it will not trigger Riptide Burst from Cutting Torrent , as the Riptide status is consumed first to apply the damage of Riptide Blast.
- After the Melee Stance Elemental Burst hits an enemy with Riptide, there is a 0.8s delay before Riptide Blast occurs and the removal of Riptide. If Riptide naturally expires during this delay, Riptide Blast will still trigger.
Constellation Effects:

- Constellation Level 5, Havoc: Formless Blade : Increases this talent's level by 3, up to a maximum of 15.
- Constellation Level 6, Havoc: Annihilation : "When Havoc: Obliteration is cast in Melee Stance, the CD of Foul Legacy: Raging Tide is reset. This effect will only take place once Tartaglia returns to his Ranged Stance."

heading_path: Hidden Aces: Seven Tools of the Hunter
blocks.text:
- Passive Talent 1, Plan to Get Paid : "When your team has at least one Pyro , Hydro , Electro , or Cryo character, the Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots from the Elemental Burst Hidden Aces: Seven Tools of the Hunter will be enhanced based on the number of characters of each corresponding element. Jahoda secretly keeps track of these characters. Among them, the element with the highest number of characters determines the enhancement effect: Pyro : Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots deal 130% of their original DMG. Hydro : Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots heal for 120% of their original healing amount. Electro : The number of Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots increases by one. Cryo : The attack interval of Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots is reduced by 10%. If there's a tie between elements, the order of priority that determines which enhancement takes effect is: Pyro , Hydro , Electro , then Cryo . Only one elemental effect can initially be triggered."
- Pyro : Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots deal 130% of their original DMG.
- Hydro : Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots heal for 120% of their original healing amount.
- Electro : The number of Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots increases by one.
- Cryo : The attack interval of Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots is reduced by 10%.
- Passive Talent 2, Sweet Berry Bounty : "When a Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robot from the Elemental Burst Hidden Aces: Seven Tools of the Hunter triggers healing on an active team member, if that character's HP is above 70%, their Elemental Mastery will be increased by 100 for 6s."

blocks.text: Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots: One of the gadgets that Jahoda — a former treasure hunter — carries around with her. It is deployed upon using her Elemental Burst Hidden Aces: Seven Tools of the Hunter. Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots continuously restore HP to your active character. If the healed character's HP is above 70%, they also restore HP to the nearby party member with the lowest HP. Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam : If nearby opponents are affected by Pyro , Hydro , Electro , or Cryo , Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots will convert to that element. The order of priority that determines which element will be converted to is: Pyro , Hydro , Electro , then Cryo . After each deployment, a Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robot can undergo one such conversion. After converting, the Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robot will periodically attack up to 3 nearby opponents, dealing damage of the corresponding element.

Invitation to a Beheading is Arlecchino 's Normal Attack .

- Unlike all other Polearm users, Arlecchino's Charged Attack is not preceded by a Normal Attack.
- The third hit of Arlecchino's Normal Attack will pull enemies towards her.
- If Arlecchino wields any other polearm other than Crimson Moon's Semblance , her polearm will have a yellow scythe blade starting from the second hit of her Normal Attack combo.
- While holding her Charged Attack and during her high speed movement, she will sprout a red wing and be able to fly over the surface of water .
- Her Normal Attack AoE is increased during her "Masque of the Red Death" state.
- Arlecchino remains in the "Masque of the Red Death" state even if she is swapped off field and swapped back in, so long as her Bond of Life is greater than 30% Max HP.
- During the "Masque of the Red Death" state, the base damage of Normal Attacks is calculated as: ATK × ( Talent Multiplier + Masque of the Red Death Increase × Bond of Life Max HP ) {\displaystyle {\text{ATK}}\times ({\text{Talent Multiplier}}+{\text{Masque of the Red Death Increase}}\times {\frac {\text{Bond of Life}}{\text{Max HP}}})}
- The on-hit 7.5% Bond of Life consumption during the "Masque of the Red Death" state is multiplicative.
Constellation Effects:

- Constellation Level 1, "All Reprisals and Arrears, Mine to Bear..." : "Masque of the Red Death is further enhanced, the value of the increase is 100%. Additionally, Arlecchino's interruption resistance is increased when she performs Normal or Charged Attacks while affected by the Masque of the Red Death."
- Constellation Level 3, "You Shall Become a New Member of Our Family..." : Increases this talent's level by 3, up to a maximum of 15.

- If Columbina is the active character and is incapacitated while this passive is not on cooldown, she will revive herself.
- If a party member is incapacitated while this passive is on cooldown or unavailable, the revival will not activate even after this passive is available again.
- Like with Lauma 's utility passive , certain wildlife will behave differently if Columbina is in the party. This only applies in Nod-Krai, and will not work on the same creatures in other regions . blocks.text: Lumi: Strike Forms: Lumi has three different Strike Forms. Super Power Form Lumi will use Pound-Pound Pummeler to attack nearby opponents continuously. Every attack will deal 2 instances of AoE Geo DMG . If there are Moondrifts nearby, Lumi will alternate between Pound-Pound Pummeler and Heavy Overdrive Hammer to continuously attack nearby opponents . Heavy Overdrive Hammer will deal AoE Geo DMG which will be considered Lunar-Crystallize Reaction DMG. Ultimate Power Form Lumi will use the ultimate Million Ton Crush, dealing an especially powerful instance of AoE Geo DMG that is considered Lunar-Crystallize Reaction DMG, switching to Standard Power Form. Standard Power Form It might not be as flashy as the other forms, but it still packs a serious punch. Lumi will use Pound-Pound Pummeler at longer intervals to attack nearby opponents continuously. Every attack will deal 2 instances of AoE Geo DMG .

Verdant Dew: When party members trigger Lunar-Bloom reactions, the party will receive such a resource. Your party will receive 1 Verdant Dew every 2.5s for 2.5s after triggering a Lunar-Bloom reaction. Your party can have up to 3 Verdant Dew. If you trigger another Lunar-Bloom reaction during this time, the duration of this effect will be reset.
Moonridge Dew: A special Verdant Dew resource provided by Columbina's Passive Talent, Law of the New Moon. Its maximum capacity and duration are calculated separately from Verdant Dew. When the party's Verdant Dew is expended, Moonridge Dew will be consumed instead. Your party can have up to 3 Moonridge Dew.

Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots: One of the gadgets that Jahoda — a former treasure hunter — carries around with her. It is deployed upon using her Elemental Burst Hidden Aces: Seven Tools of the Hunter. Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots continuously restore HP to your active character. If the healed character's HP is above 70%, they also restore HP to the nearby party member with the lowest HP. Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam : If nearby opponents are affected by Pyro , Hydro , Electro , or Cryo , Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots will convert to that element. The order of priority that determines which element will be converted to is: Pyro , Hydro , Electro , then Cryo . - She does not need to be alive to locate local specialties, but does need to be alive to enable the passive's wildlife-related effects.
- Only one local specialty will be shown on the mini-map at a time.
- Certain wildlife will behave differently if Lauma is in the party. This only applies in Nod-Krai, and will not work on the same creatures in other regions . Some creatures will have special interactions. A glowing symbol will briefly appear above them when approached. Blunthorn Rhino - These mine and retrieve nearby Rainbowdrop Crystals . Chic Badger - These dig up Fowl and Raw Meat (amount varies). Puffin - These follow the party around. Rimehorn Deer - These heal the party and fully fill their Energy meters. However, they will do so if the player enters combat or stays near them for more than a few minutes.
