Once upon a time, the mother of roses and lilies graced the girl 's silken swaddling with a violet perfume, to ensure that an endless stream of joyous dreams might ward off death's bitter gloom. The beautiful songstress , who once plucked elegant melodies, also bathed her wings in the warm, gentle waters of compassion, for the precious newborn was never meant to be touched by the music of the world's mundane strings. This was a time when the chains of eternity had yet to be shattered, and when carefree refrains could still be heard before the throne of the heavens . It was a time when the days beneath the silver-white tree were as sweet as honey, and glorious messengers thronged the primordial paradise. In a rich, golden dream steeped in the warmth of the spring sun, the innocent child basked in the doting love of all her sisters. In their cradle of tender Azurelight , they shared laughter with the morning dew and new-blown buds; and by the black stone that had yet to fall, they sang soft tunes to the fading sunset and quiet evening breeze. Their bright eyes had never witnessed the spilled crimson in the world below, nor had their slender hands ever touched the sad pain of injustice. Then, starlight from beyond put an end to that bucolic idyll, and the bonfire of disobedience was kindled by misguided desire. The eldest daughter who dared overstep met her end, plummeting from the mountain peak, while the armored emissaries who swore to strike down the Lord of Hosts perished one after another. All this time, the youngest child, the most beloved of them all, was hidden far away, in a palace deep within the wilds, sequestered from the storm of violence and the relentless rain of blood. "I shall overthrow the throne of the Most High, to set the oppressed free, and to avenge the afflicted." "But as for our sister, who is young and tender, we shall not harden her heart to make war against the false lord." "Whether we prevail or fall, it is not right that her wings should bear the heavy yoke which we ourselves ought to bear." While no one knew the capricious ruler's desire, their righteous rule still afforded one the chance to choose one's path. And choose the youngest did, to cast off the divinity and her former powers. Then, miraculously, this child was allowed to retain human form. Thus did she step into the world of the mortals, with nothing more than her broken wings and a fragile body of flesh and bone. In this utterly vulnerable form, she wandered alone through a land filled with sorrow and tears, tainting her once pristine feet with muck and mire. This went on for thousands of years, in which countless towers turned to sand, and songs of lament dissipated into the night breeze. The envoy who wandered, the envoy who met the witch , the envoy who at last was relieved of the past... Through the journey and memories that belonged to her alone, she found her crown irreplaceable at last. The world she had never once deigned to behold was now etched forever in her eyes, the eyes of one who can no longer sing. And so the solitary guide now stands, her crown wrought from the countless joys and sorrows of men, and the grand adventures of mortal heroes. "What a beautiful world this is!"

By the time the little witch arrived at the Day King's palace, twilight had already taken hold. Had she come any later, the kingdom would have already passed beyond the Day King's rule. Before the night curtain descended, the Day King received her in what remained of his fleeting hours. "O witch who has traversed the vast cosmos, kindler of time's eternal flame... what brings you to this lonely planet?" "I did not come of my own accord. It was the planet's cry that found me through the void. Answering its call, I crossed the gate of stars forgotten by time." "In a universe nearing its quiet end, every world that yet glimmers is a treasure beyond compare..." "Who would have thought that in a region long considered dark and inhospitable, a living world would still endure?" But this was not the whole story. In truth, the little witch had caught wind of whispers from this dark expanse — whispers that had flown to her on the eve of the Night Carnival. Under ordinary circumstances, she would likely have dismissed such strange signals as just another error from the scryglass. But as the message reached her, she was fretting over the next day's festivities, desperately trying to find a way to avoid her nemesis, who would also be there. So she seized the opportunity to hide away in her workshop — spending considerable effort deciphering this distant missive. "Hmm... So this peculiar message means that some unknown planet has been feeling unwell?" "No matter what, the righteous Kingdom of Day would never do anything to harm the planet," the Day King said solemnly. "Perhaps you should ask the wicked Night King. This very morning I sent my army to vanquish him, alas..." But before he could finish, the last rays of the setting sun vanished into night, and the king's apparition melted away like cream. With the curtain of darkness descending, the court itself vanished too. The ground boiled like a raging sea, and black smoke rose from the earth. The entire planet became a vast black ocean. Fortunately, the little witch had remembered her broom — otherwise, she may well have plunged into the water. Riding her broom beneath the blood-red moon, she traveled far before finally spying a lonely castle, glowing with firelight. "Vanquish the Night King? That's the easy part. What we have to do is far more important." The castle seemed to have been built by the Day King's army. For unknown reasons, it had escaped dissolution by the sea of mist. The leading warrior, carrying a sword on his back, was not at all surprised by the little witch's arrival. Instead, he met her with an invitation. "Even if we defeat the Night King, it changes nothing. As soon as the sun sets anew, the dark tides will swallow the land once more." "To break this endless cycle, we built this castle. From here, we can search for a solution." At his invitation, the little witch descended to the deepest level of the castle, where — beyond its fragile boundaries — stretched a sea of pure darkness. Sustaining this boundary was a massive mechanism that spat out an endless stream of smoke. Countless pipes were continuously drawing thick seawater into its core. "This is the perpetual motion machine, or you may call it the Holy Grail. By burning the seawater, it generates light and heat." "Since all tangible things on this planet are merely shadows cast by light, so long as we can create a fire that never goes out..." "But doing this will only make the planet burn out even faster..." the little witch sighed. "Once the sea's been drained, this place will be finished. There's nothing 'holy' about this so-called grail..." "Now I know why the planet's been feeling unwell." Before the warrior could react, the little witch drew the sword from his back and hurled it into the "perpetual motion machine." The warrior reached out to retrieve it, but the moment the blade touched the black sea mist, both he and the fading light vanished into nothingness. The entire planet was once again swallowed by darkness. When daylight finally returned, it was as if everything from the previous night had been nothing more than a deep and distant dream. "I suppose that's a temporary fix, at least," the little witch murmured, glancing back one last time before leaving the planet on her broom. In the morning light, the warrior — his shadow trailing long behind him — took up the sword bestowed by the Day King and set out on his journey once more. "This cycle may go on for a long, long time... until the day you too become nothing but an empty shell." "But no matter what, you must keep going. At least... you must live until we meet again."

In the days before she lost her last name, the world had known her as "eldest daughter of the Strivozhas ." The Grand Duke Photius had passed away after a sudden stroke, leaving the counselor who had served him faithfully to inherit his title, While the grand rebellion he had intended to lead with the Druzhna was laid to rest in the grave alongside the mead he had drunk. Though the winds over the frozen earth were as fickle as ever, the house of the Vila princess remained at the very pinnacle of power. Against the wishes of the forebear, the Silver Court of Veneter once again fell into the hands of a Strivozha, Adding yet another tale of loyalty to the lore of that name, as was the case in the court of the Pale Star. "Oh, great princess, are you really so naive as to believe that the newly crowned Tsaritsa would elect to trust your house?" "The glory of the court of the Pale Star hangs above her head like a sharp blade. She will eventually succumb to the flattery of humankind." " Your mother ... she, The Pure One, was once so devoted to Tsar Monomakh . How could you have forgotten that oath?" "Your Highness, O noble Gluvasha Strivozha , let us join hands and cast down that usurper who dared lay claim to the throne!" The rebels sought to win her over to their cause, urging her to rebel against the new sovereign of the snowy wastes, knowing of her mother's unwavering loyalty to the old Tsar. The eldest daughter of the Strivozhas agreed without hesitation, her emerald eyes gleaming with the same noble compassion that had once shone in her mother's eyes. "If, as you say, my friend, that contemptible false sovereign must be overthrown for the future of our clan, Then I shall swear upon the honor of Saint Strivozha: the Vila will stand steadfastly at your side." Then, just as the rebels had hoped, in the months that followed, the Vila princess would regularly denounce the Tsaritsa's actions in public. First came the expulsion of the palace-appointed observer from her lands; then came the raising of a following without royal sanction. Unsurprisingly, the eldest daughter of the Strivozhas had always proven to be every bit as loyal and dependable as her mother, who had been honored as The Pure One. As such, though wary and distrustful of one another, the rebels of the various fae clans were always willing to entrust their secrets to the Vila, leaving her to devise their plans. That is, until the rebels were caught in one fell swoop. It was only then that they learned that the ally they had counted on had long since taken her place at the Tsaritsa's side. The rebels, angered by her betrayal and, in panic, began to rail against her for besmirching her mother's good name. However, they were coolly and swiftly dismissed. "Ah, did you not previously praise the loyalty of the Strivozhas and, on that very account, seek an alliance with us? As I said, if Her Majesty ought indeed to be overthrown, the Vila will naturally stand shoulder to shoulder with you in battle. Except... if the wind has ever carried word to you, then you ought to know that Anastasya alone is our sovereign. You are not my lieges, and nor am I your vassal. Why, then, are you even accusing me of betraying your rebellion?" And thus it came to pass that, beneath the benevolent light that shone upon the frozen earth, the rebellion was brought to a complete end. The Strivozhas were never the enemy of any, and as the histories would record, they upheld their honor and loyalty to the very end. Here, the tale so finely rendered comes to a close. However, the Vila princess's account of what followed remains little known... "My Tsaritsa. A noble name is no more than a chain; and the most precious gift to me now is that of freedom. Since the Vila has already been blessed by Your Majesty's boundless grace, I beseech you to grant me release from this very chain. Further, my raising of a force without sanction, even if it was done to deceive the rebels, remains an unforgivable act of treason. I beg Your Majesty to reclaim my fief, strip me of my last name and title, and appoint another in my stead." And so, a solemn decree descended from the throne on high, its mercy like a distant, ethereal sigh... "Gluvasha. From this day forth, let none remember you by your last name. In the histories of days to come, your title shall be no more. May your gravestone, in the end, bear witness to the convictions you held so true."

If power were a majestic edifice, how many bricks are needed to build it? Bricks alone do not make a building. So, who decides which bricks will form the foundation, and which will become the spire? Beneath the facade of strict order lies the truth: sheer chance alone arbitrarily decides the fate of every brick. A towering building can be brought down by a single crucial brick, one that will not obey this false order. "The Godfather 's secret treasure lies deep within the black market." The feast meant to shatter the old order had begun, and hungry thieves were now gathering for the prize. This was a battle of all against all. The most mortal threat came not from the Godfather's guards, but one's fellow ruthless thieves. A fae was the first to enter the treasure vault. The world had taught him to seek out gain, shun personal harm, and keep a distance from the schemes of others. He was cunning beyond measure, able to read people's minds like maps and navigate the safest paths through the most tangled of intrigues. The next to make an attempt was a young lady for whom winning against the fae mattered more than the Godfather's riddles. With her blade , she adroitly cut through every lock, outwitting the supposedly intricate mechanisms with the simplest of solutions. The last to face the challenge was a hunter, who saw the maze not as a riddle, but as a hunting ground more cruel than one wrapped in frigid winter, demanding every last drop of caution. Patience is a poisoned trap, and sharpness a bloodthirsty blade. Guided by his raw, primal methods, the hunter met the challenge head-on. Yet all were defeated by the vault — the fae, the young lady, and the hunter alike. A butler in black bound the three and led them, one by one, into an inner chamber. "Esteemed Godfather, your guests have been seated and now await your command." Zaytun Peach in hand, the Godfather chewed leisurely, saying to each of the guests brought in by the butler thus: "You have shown no regard for the world's order and dared to take what was not yours. And for that, I intend to reward you." "Order, as it is known, exists only to serve its architects. I find this unacceptable, which is why I shall need your assistance." "What this world calls order is naught but the rich getting richer and the poor being left with less. I have concluded that thievery, then, is the only way to restore balance." "Should you choose to uphold the thief's code from this day forward, eat this fruit in the presence of the master thief's remains." Having longed since childhood to escape the hollow luxury of noble life, the fae was moved by the Godfather's words and ate the Bulle Fruit , accepting his offer. The young lady, who had never bowed to the arrogance of those above her in station, swallowed the Wolfhook without hesitation, for her philosophy was fully in line with that of the Godfather. The last to swallow the fruit, the Valberry , was the hunter, who had once retreated into the cold forest precisely out of refusal to live in compromise with a corrupt world. "Excellent. The pact is sealed. From this day forward, you are the backbone of the resistance against injustice." After watching his guests leave one by one, the Godfather gently ran a hand along the vault's bare walls, lost in reflection. He had removed the most crucial brick from the edifice of order, yet he could not foresee an unexpected turn of events: Watching the Godfather clutch his pained abdomen with a frown, the butler beside him give an elegant smile. With utmost calm, she took up the master thief's black spine bone, leaving the Calla Lily behind to be used as an antidote as she swiftly exited. "What you just said to the gathered thieves illuminated the master thief's ideals to them. For that reason, I shall spare your life." "But true justice lies not in order itself, but in the fact that no single person can ever impose it on others."

"Were one to commit a sin that even they know in their heart cannot be forgiven," "Is he still worthy of seeking forgiveness and redemption from others?" The silent warrior would ask himself this, Wordlessly interrogating himself each time he swung his heavy greatsword. The beastman who had yet to become a warrior, once believed in the blueprint sketched out by the wise one, that joy might be brought to all who live. "Forged in its purity and glory, all shall come to love one another in the new land beneath the dawn." "Believe in the ideals of Cirnareka, follow the one named the Burner of Cities , and eternal redemption shall surely descend." Neither destruction nor slaughter would cause the warrior to show mercy, for his calling was noble: A promised homeland that would be pure and flawless, upon which a new order would be established. Even when the blood flowed endlessly, even when songs of joy no longer echoed above the earth, He only heard the voice of that wise one, whose voice was as enchanting as it was at first: "Well done, warrior. By your hand the rot has been cut off. Never have you betrayed our hopes." "Always remember, mercy to one's foes shall bring forth only a future of dissolution." How should he speak of the wound on his face, which had never truly healed? How should he speak of his unchanging silence and self-imposed exile? How to relate his betrayal, to come clean to the people? His blade was now aimed toward his old master. The valiant warrior also knew fear. The crowd had only asked him questions in passing, but the goodwill they thus showed left him at a loss. He had abandoned his past and slaughtered no more, and he followed the guiding one to atone for his past sins. Yet the innocent souls lingered in his memories, and thus did the accursed warrior taste of life and death, brought about for no rhyme or reason. Sometimes, a shadow of the wise one would visit him, and in dreams mock his follies and falsehoods in that same mesmerizing tone. Despite accepting a new greatsword and swearing an inscrutable oath, the embers of destruction still seared his heart. He resolved to let time cleanse him of confusion. Before then, solitude was the wage he chose for his sin. Even when sacrifices had to be exchanged for the delivery of a secret message, even when the guiding one had to die to defeat the certitude of destruction, The taciturn warrior stood guard in the rear, protecting his wounded comrades, locked in endless battle with old compatriots. He could not bear to kill, and so slowly lost the initiatve, allowing that wise one who had inflamed peoples' hearts to flee, And the wolf fae, drunk on the wine of ruin, spoke mockery-filled words as he stood before his former comrade. "Hah! If it isn't the traitorous warrior. Siding with humans hasn't just dulled your blade, you know. They've stuffed a soft heart in your chest, too." "Come! Welcome your end, just like that crookbacked friend of yours, that Domovoy who refused to kneel before Cirnareka." Before he could finish, the wolf fae realized that his heart had been rent by the greatsword. In his final moments, he heard the warrior's hoarse, vengeful whisper: "My name is Rafalovich. Once I was a blade for brigands, the sword of the Burner of Cities." "I have stored up for myself evil and catastrophe — redemption is but an extravagant hope for my sins of deception and violence..." "...But I still have the right to pay you back, blood for blood."

A folk tale from the northern lands tells of two brothers: the King of Midsommar Oak, who once brought warmth to the world, and his elder brother, the King of Winter Icelea , who loved him dearly. But a sudden, tragic quarrel led to the elder accidentally slaying the younger, and ever since, the world has been ruled by unrelenting winter. Perhaps it would be impossible for people to explain why their benevolent king is forever shrouded in wind and snow, if such a tragedy were not involved. But only the long-lived fae know that the unmelting permafrost has endured far longer than the reign of the Tsar. The White Emperor, who ruled the fae from the lofty throne of the Pale Star, had been silent since returning from the ruins of the far north . He lingered in the birch forest, deep in thought, before finally opening the door to the humans he had once turned away. A labyrinthine palace rose at the edge of the frozen earth, built alongside the giant furnaces of Snezhnograd . To this place were summoned the wisest of humans and fae, and here, the first seeds of a grand delusion were sown. For countless days and nights, the Tsar's most loyal and valiant retainers stood guard over this court of audacious transgression. Among them were fae who had followed their ruler from the beginning, as well as mortals from a lineage that had proven its unwavering loyalty to the Tsar. The two brothers belonged to the clan's younger generation. The elder , having inherited the nightingale's emblem, took up the duty of guarding the sacred chariot. The younger son , who had always admired his elder brother, had no choice but to forsake his family name and resign himself to a life of obscurity on the frontier. Then, a calamity, born of selfishness, shattered their ideals and changed their destiny forever... The loyal guard was consumed by " beasts ," creature of pure darkness bereft of intellect, for the crime of glimpsing the secret of the philosophers . His younger brother, who had left to quell distant unrest, returned to a world already covered in deep snow. But instead of its customary silver-white feathers, the spear he found now wore the black stain of noble blood. Years later, the general who had inherited the family name forsook his homeland, journeying into the wild borderlands on a quest for vengeance. Every time his fingers traced the spear, he was transported back to that long, snowy night outside the ancient palace gates. The memory was one that was soaked in sorrow, the words of his old friend — words spoken as he stood before the guillotine — echoing in his mind. Beneath the sublunary sphere, the world lay shackled by tragic fate, its lost citizens wandering aimlessly through the lands they once called home. The Torchforger , bathed in the moon's eternal light, lit the everlasting flame and began his watch.

In the years before the holy torch of the Pale Star was lit, the Silver Court of Veneter had been a haven of renown equal to Kitezhgrad . Fae from various clans praised the Lady of the Vila merciful ways [ sic ], hailing her a saint who had banished the bitter cold and soothed their pain. Indeed, though war raged and blood stained the frozen rivers, Vaselisa von Strivozha was never the enemy of any. Pure, benevolent, and true. So countless songs of later ages would praise her, as gentle and warm as the soft breeze of spring. And so it was that, on a bitter night cold as frost and snow, a noble with nowhere left to turn came knocking at the splendid gates of Veneter. He was a war hero who had served the Blood-Devourer , a renowned commander who had routed the armies of the Pale Star in battle time and again. Yet, for speaking plainly against his brutal liege, for urging him not to slaughter the Water Imps who were still his allies, he had been stripped of every title and office. His wife and children had been subjected to the ultimate penalty of the Blood Eagle, while the people who paid him tribute were brutally plundered and murdered by his liege's own guards, leaving the fields strewn with corpses. He had come knocking at the gates of Veneter, asking only that the merciful saint pave the way and grant him an audience with the young Tsar so he might submit himself to the latter. The saint of Veneter listened quietly to his tale, and soon tears of pity glimmered in her jade-green eyes. " Alrekr Jarizleivich , my good man, my gallant hero... How could I not weep for those who have died unjustly? Bring the surviving people under your care, the weary and impoverished with nowhere else to go, those who have suffered so grievously, all to my lands. My estate shall always keep its gates open to every soul battered by hardship, and you... may you find rest here as well." The beauteous saint, famed for her mastery of perfumery, personally filled a cup with fragrant warming mead for her weary guest, then knelt to remove the old commander's boots... ...And as the golden drink caught in his throat the metal of his blood, she calmly drew the sorrow from her eyes. Before dawn had even broken, a secret powerful enough to turn the tides of war had already been carried by the wind to the table of the king of the Volkodlak . Days later, a coffin draped in red and white silk was placed upon a sled and escorted by attendants to the royal court of the Pale Star . The saint of Veneter walked beside it herself, then fell before the young Emperor Monomakh , weeping inconsolably. Grief had left her without words. No lament was sung; only tears fell like pearls, soaking her white robes. Gluvasha , who was at the time still a maidservant, bowed her head in mourning before the Tsar. Her voice trembled as she recounted the Volkodlak's savagery. "Though my mistress had taken the survivors into her care, she could not prevent the Blood-Devourer's spies from poisoning the valiant general... Now, only Your Majesty's mercy can save the countless weeping souls upon this cold and desolate land." Through the veil of her tears, she saw in the youth's sky-blue eyes a hatred both righteous and compassionate. Indeed. Let the noblest of angers surge like a great wave, let order clash against order, steel against steel, While the wind remains forever the wind: gentle, elusive, and free, formless and ever-changing, never bound by delusion. ... The carriage on the journey home rolled through the deep snows that had lain unmelted since time immemorial. The saint brushed away the glistening tear at the corner of her eye, and turned her gaze upon her somber attendant. " Photius , you may as well speak plainly. There is no need to wear such a look all the time. Say what it is that displeases you." The young Vila, who had been chosen for her service for his skill in preparing elixirs, hurriedly lowered his eyes as he tried desperately to hide the thoughts that had just crossed his mind. "No... Your judgment has ever seen through what lies hidden. How could one as foolish and lowly as I dare show the slightest disrespect toward your wisdom..." Her words were greeted by a tinkling laugh. "There you go again, Photius. You place such faith in those you deem wise that you would sooner persuade yourself to stop thinking. You worry that the Pale Star King will learn the truth, and you question what I have done. These are all perfectly good questions. But he will suspect nothing. Indeed, I trust in his mercy. What reason has he to doubt my tears? On the one hand, the king of the Volkodlak would have the wind become a blade that cleaves bone. On the other, the Emperor of the Pale Star would have it become a holy sword to cleanse all that is corrupt. Yet in the end, they both wish the wind to bend to their will, to follow the banners of the mighty and blow where they would have it go. But Photius, the wind belongs to no one. So long as it continues to blow, none can know where it will carry itself." The saint of Veneter let her gentle smile fade, her jade-green pupils reflecting the youth's still-innocent face. "Best you learn from Gluvasha. Pride and vanity are poisons that only bring ruin to a clan. Only the gentle wind can blow on forever."

It is said that in a faraway realm on the far side of the starry sea, or perhaps in an ancient era of which history and legend alike failed to record, there was a hidden world known to none. As with all legends, this one began with a world that was formless and void, with neither beginning nor end. Only the three gods existed, passing the time amidst the infinite void in boredom. The first god claimed the name "Valor," and he possessed unlimited power and divine might. None in the universe might best him in battle. The second god was named "Cunning," possessing unlimited wisdom and guile. Since time immemorial, no one could see through his schemes and plots. Perhaps personality differences were to blame, or perhaps they needed to pass the time, but these two gods would fight endlessly, having never stopped since the world's creation. Yet, neither intelligence nor strength had any practical meaning in a world with neither beginning nor end, and such, too, proved the contest between the two gods. Neither could achieve victory, but neither was willing to admit defeat. This, then, was when the third god, "Nature," finally spoke up with an interesting idea. "Let us create a new world, upon which we shall use dice to determine the winner." "For even gods cannot change the outcome of the dice." Though no one knew what transpired in the middle, the three gods reached an agreement in the end and put their disputes aside to partake in this grand plan. The God of Valor smoothed the lands and turned them into a square chessboard, and he made mountains and rivers in imitation of the past world. The God of Cunning then carved chess pieces of various forms. Angels, humans, Jinn, monsters. He made the dragons and magical beasts also, those impelled by the God of Nature. Thus were the heavens and earth opened, and thus did things come to pass. Thousands of days and nights flew by. Countless adventures and legends took place in their turn upon this tiny, newly built world. One thing, however, remained consistent — only the dice in the gods' hands could decide the fate of the world. Even a seasoned Hero, though he could crush city halls of refined gold in but a single casual swing, Was undone by the Dark Lord despite a valiant struggle, thanks to the vagaries of horrendous dice throws. "Blast! Well, at least I came prepared for this eventuality. Valor's Hero comes equipped with divinely bestowed armor that has a mortal save. I shall revive the Hero and roll again..." "Yes, but you'll have to pass a check before that. With the Hero in a weakened state, he is vulnerable to a spiritual attack from the magical sword that contains the soul of the previous Dark Lord..." "Excuse me? Where is that coming from? I've never seen it in the rules, ever!" "The Tome of Universal Laws, Page 83. You must have failed to read the updated version, I see." "Damn you, Ibis , and your godforsaken, backstabbing ways!" "Oh, come now, what are you saying? Deception is part of war... If you must lay blame anywhere, blame your failure to upgrade the Soul Barrier ability. Alright then. The Hero is now a piece on my side, and I'd quite like him to turn on his companions and..." "Hold. The Hero is under the control of the previous Dark Lord's will. As such, he should technically not belong to the current Dark Lord's forces. Rather, he should be a monster under Nature's command..." "What? What is this nonsense!?" "Aha, you see? Now that the shoe's on the other foot, you've flown into a panic, too." "With the Hero being seized by the previous Dark Lord, even the current Dark Lord was not his match. The ancient demons thus regained control of the world... The adventure ends here. Neither of you achieved victory, alas." "That said, not all is lost. Let us create a new batch of adventurers and start another round... We have endless days and countless nights ahead of us, and shall naturally need adventures unnumbered to pass the time."
- BP Bounty ( Battle Pass ' Gnostic Hymn )

"The law shall uphold all the land under my jurisdiction, and thus shall it be blessed with peace." "These laws shall sanction all who commit acts of terror and disrupt order." "We shall conquer humanity's weaknesses and bring peace to these long borders." "We shall forsake useless emotions and keep our frozen hearts beating." One who wishes to lead the Transportation Bureau and maintain law and order within Snezhnaya must heed the admonitions of centuries past, And lend one's ear to the tale of the leader who ultimately forsook emotion and kindness, pointing a bow at those they once called friends. It was a contest between order and chaos, a battle between defense and destruction, and after that, a showdown between old friends. In those days, the young human was not the head of the Transport Bureau, and the pale fae served not yet at the Burner of Cities ' side. Both lamented the world's injustice and mourned its futile struggles, and because they shared ideals and evenly matched strength, They found kindred spirits in each other — an enviable thing in a time when humans and fae could not see eye to eye in the least. "Chaos can breed hope, and new buildings can be fashioned atop ruins. Destruction is not utterly without cause, but is meant to bring about golden rebirth." "Yet brutality has left this nation wounded and scarred. Those who live within its bounds need a new order and new laws." Thus, the two diverged over the moral path this land should take. Human and fae, in the end, should struggle to share the same ideals. And though they had parted ways with no desire to meet again, the justice of order cannot by its nature coexist with the brutality of destruction. The clash, therefore, was a foregone conclusion. The human led the Chicota , becoming the guardian of law and order, standing guard amidst snow and frost, While the fae became "the wise one," using the name of old royalty to incite the masses who longed for destruction, all in the name of rebirth. This went on till white dew had condensed into frost, and that frost had turned into dew, the metal bells ringing thrice, then thrice again. As the train passed the white birches, and both sharp sword and bright pearl fell, the long and drawn-out conflict would finally come to an end. The fae fled, covered by brigands, but could not deceive the chief of the Chicota. The bow was raised, the arrow nocked, and he locked onto his target without pause, until the fae, as if realizing something, turned and looked upon him. The human could not help but ask himself: When had this ever-beating heart grown as frigid as the frost and snow? But he could still see the guiding one's fall as if it were still before his eyes. He knew all too well how dangerous his friend of old was. The words that had come along with the bow rang in his ears still: "This bow is not given unto Eprokin , but rather to the guardian of order." One ought to harbor sorrow and compassion as a person, but the leader of the Chicota must judge in accordance with the law that governs all living beings. Many humans in years past would dedicate their lives to the moving trains, consigning themselves to the endless blizzards. And the promise he made when he received the bow and arrows became the oath that generation after generation of Chicota heads would swear upon taking the seat. "We shall conquer humanity's weaknesses and bring peace to these long borders." "We shall forsake useless emotions and keep our frozen hearts beating." "Let me exercise humility in my authority, and keep my conscience as I fulfill my duty." "Let cowardice and arrogance be far from me, that I may never betray this oath."

"Always remember, Avrelian , my dear child — the one precious gift that fate has granted me." "A thousand-year-old curse runs through your veins, and my only wish is for you to live a life of peace and joy." "No matter what happens, you must never set foot in Nod-Krai , and you must never be taken in by that fool's dream of 'Elysium.'" "No earthly paradise under the moon has ever been built for mortals. All that the Lord of the Sky has created has its boundaries." On a snowy evening gently veiled in the aurora's light, the woman once worshipped as the Maiden had another glimpse of the dream foretelling the fate of her homeland . It had been many years since she bade farewell to that place. Yet, like the creeping frost, those deliberately forgotten whispers always found their way into her warm, quiet dreams, nonetheless. Perhaps it was the new life growing within her that stirred the long-dormant visions, and now, those haunting, twisting phantoms grew ever clearer... At first, they came to her as ceaseless nightmares, countless dreams that came and went endlessly in stifling, unyielding cycles. The seeds of life, born not of natural evolution, fell from silver branches into the ruins of the desolate city. Where featherless creatures, walking upright, enjoyed untold wisdom and the blessings it bestowed. Then came endless greed and selfish desire, masked behind noble-sounding names. And from these followed hatred, curses, betrayal, strife, plunder, slaughter, and kin turning against kin. The cities scattered across the land pursued their own paths of good and evil while the divine envoys stood by in silence, watching all unfold. Until the kings of the lands dared test the eternal heavens . And only then did the great towers fall in flame, burying the cries of the slaves. Like a fleeting shadow vanishing in a single breath, a dreamless dream stretched across a thousand years and then a thousand more. A mountain of crowns in a secret place, beneath a withered tree , forgotten by all. But sometimes even the divine plan falters, and the golden city that rose from the earth... Could not satiate the hearts of mortals, aflame with desire. Hearts swollen with ambition, drawn to the vacant throne of the world , longing to shatter the boundaries between man and god. But like all tragic illusions, that boundless Elysium would crumble. The draconic kings of flame plunged into the dark abyss , and the tides swallowed the white-stone empire whole. The dying world was moving toward its end, with only the shadows of the past lingering in its halls. Countless dreams steeped in blood, tears, and sin... Countless dreams, forever out of reach... Years of division and hatred, carried across generations, cycling endlessly beneath the starless night. And then, a voice unheard, yet more familiar than any she had known... Whispered to her on the bitter end of darkness, with compassion soft and luminous as light. "I shall bring an end to the warriors of this land and raise a boundless Elysium in their place." "I do this not to be king, but so that no other can ever claim that role." Her dream would always shatter just as it reached the moment of promise, and she would be pulled back to the shores of reality. Accompanied by the pale morning light and the faint stirring of the life within her. The young mother let out a quiet sigh as her fingers brushed against the silvery-white talisman resting against her chest. Gazing upon the face of the one she loved beside her, the woman gently placed a hand over her belly and asked... "My child, my dear child... why do you stir so?" "Is it because you sense your mother's heart — are you afraid?"

In the moonless city of snow , the outlander warrior mourned a realm shattered, never to return. There, amidst the frost, he lay to rest in the ground a hope that would no longer bear fruit. Leaving his unspoken longings alongside that lonely final mural, he began to wander the frozen plains, solitary and unmoored. He believed that by casting his old greatsword into the deathly frost, he would be able to forget the weakness of days gone by, throw himself into endless battle, and thus find solace and joy in the tang of iron and blood. Yet, the warrior abandoned the hollow lie of his own despair at the very first moonfall after he left the great hall of that mountain country . It was a fleeting moment of confusion and folly. All he wanted, by pure instinct, was to save the maiden under attack. He never again wished to see a head of silver hair, or a face as bright as the moon, buried under all that ice and snow. This was a man who believed he had long broken the oath of a warrior, and who wished to spill his blood in conflict merely as a means of diversion. He launched the astral silver lance, yet untainted by crimson, into the black tide of beasts with all his might. in a strike that generations of scholars and bards thereafter would grant the appellation "dolorous." Ancient songs tell of an outlander who roamed the frozen plains and brought calamity to a land of peace. They sing of the man who, for the sheer joy of conflict, drove a cold tip of astral silver through the wind and snow and shattered the snow-covered mountains, and in so doing, leveled three thriving kingdoms and consigned vast lands to utter desolation, leaving multitudes to wander the wastes. The cries of the innocent, mourning the calamity wrought by that single blow, could be heard everywhere. But the song is but a song. Before the bloodbath around him could even become legend, the outlander stood dazed amidst the ruins, seeing nothing but fragmented glimpses of wind and snow. His wayward spear had pierced the stone that held up the earth, And the maiden that he meant to protect, too, had perished in the billowing darkness. The survivors of the ruined lands saw the man named Imunlaukr as the sworn enemy of their fallen peoples, hunting him without end. For the warrior who claimed a craving to entertain the gods with strains of strife and blood, The warrior who sank into despair but refused to accept his fate and sought redemption, yet ended up bringing on even more grief and sorrow... This was the very moment he finally ceased longing for salvation and turned away from the life of a warrior forever.

Domovoy born with statures considered small even amongst their people struggle to find a place to belong, no matter where they go. The beasts would mock their hunched forms, and humans were wary of their strange appearances. Must they be forced to bear the sin of betrayal from birth on account of their kin who had pledged loyalty to humans? Was there no other way to carve out a place for oneself beyond becoming a jester to be made sport of, thus ingratiating oneself with the powerful? "Know this, my lost kin: the realm that the Tsaritsa has created has no place in it for us." "Seek vengeance against humanity, for their sowing of discord and their preposterous plays at power. We fae were the original masters of ice and snow." The hunchbacked Domovoy was thus accepted by the Burner of Cities and her servants, and he served beneath the banner of old royalty. Alongside the brutal wolf-fae, he listened to the sublime edicts of the wise one, and from then on followed the banner of destruction and emptiness. This spy by the Burner of Cities' side was one day discovered, and they subjected him to alternating rounds of torture and persuasion. "You ingrate! We accepted an outsider such as you, only to be rewarded with treachery." "Yet a lost lamb may still be forgiven and granted blessed protection, so long as they speak truth from now." Yet for all the rattling of the chains or all the honey poured on, silence was the answer the executioners received. Humiliated and infuriated, the brigands moved to execute the Domovoy cruelly, all the better to warn others of a traitor's fate. Faced with the axe and eternal slumber, the figure that once stooped now unveiled his commanding height. "Ideals that conceal selfishness and hatred should not be allowed to deceive the world. The scheme to destroy the Torches must be stopped for justice to be done." "The Domovoy serve not humanity, but the future of all life. Away with all this ostentation! Death shall taste sweet to me." Through echoes in the relics he left behind, he was able to bring a secret report to his companions, along with the bright future he would not live to see. This then was the tale of the Domovoy, a fleeting existence in transient time, whose steadfastness earned not a single chronicler's plaudit. Only the guiding one resolved to settle his grudge, for the sake of their friendship, for his long years of persistence, For the oath of loyalty he had made and not forgotten, for he had never once lost his way amidst the long, cold nights. "To bow and scrape is not my way. One day, the world shall know," "That even at the last, Varenukha did not bend."

"Many long years ago, a member of fae royalty was worshipped in the shadows," "Until a cleansing hand came forth and slew them, leaving behind an ancient family name and forgotten remains." Many such glorious epics are destined to be forgotten by time, the vanquished in the great game of survival. The defeated young man laughed playfully, and swapped the honorifics and titles this way and that in his cryptic verse: "O Pearl of the land of ashes, eminent lords and ladies of noble name, and esteemed worthies," "No grudge there is between you and I. This is a mere contest of strength, a dispute that breaks no boundaries." "Though the outcome has been decided, I deem it best that we shake hands and make peace. Let us together cleanse this long road of filth and dust." "Thus shall we earn the praise of the people who dwell amidst ashes, and those falsely beneficent lords shall hear of our deed and quail." The young woman, lovely as a pearl, spoke forth with prideful face and menacing voice: "Listen ye, soot-worms of Kitezhgrad , humans whose sole trade is thievery." "Remember this your loss, and depart according to your wager, before this lady's patience runs dry." "Remember also this name, for it shall reclaim all that has been lost," "A day shall come when no one shall address the princess's descendants by their sacred name." The young man paid the loss no heed, and indeed still saw fighting against injustice as a game. He grew ever more revered, and he lit the way towards equity. The young woman, however, was nourished by brutality. She took for her title " Burner of Cities ," and they propped her up as a ruler of destruction and emptiness. At their next confrontation, what was once a petty squabble was now a battle for the safety of the citizenry, And the tables were turned. Facing a rival with whom he shared mutual respect, the guiding one's compassion grew within him, And where once he might have drawn upon old cunning or donned an irreverent look, he sought then to earnestly persuade: "Your noble name has been woven by those with ulterior motives into a hollow banner, and they have led you to lose all." "But people even now shall forgive you, in the name of the ashes, of Kitezhgrad, and indeed, of Snezhnaya ." But though she was beaten by one she had once vanquished, the young woman, yet beautiful as pearls, wore an arrogant look, her head yet held high. "The Burner of Cities and her followers shall not submit to Snezhnaya, nor shall the land of ashes be the abode of those of royal descent." "Base purveyors of false beneficence, opportunists of history... You are not fit to speak of conciliation and absolution." A premediated third encounter became their final reunion. The beating heart of destruction had turned into gunpowder, yearning to glimpse the end of all living beings via the train speeding toward the blast furnace. The Burner of Cities and her followers plotted to destroy the Kresnik's Torches , to have Snezhnaya play pallbearer to her ancient family name. The guide, sharp as blade, the ancestor who founded the Luchkin , led the people once more in thwarting the devices of those thugs. As to that final contest, it has been interpreted countless different ways in the tales passed from generation to generation, But only because the guide's followers continued to relive and recite the past over the centuries. "Alas for his mercy, that instead aroused her rage. Alas for his benevolence, that failed to inspire repentence in those brigands." "The battle at a stalemate, the two leapt upon the furnace, and together fell into the flames, and they perished, the good and the wicked both." The gloom that had blanketed the tundra dissipated amidst the new dawn caused by that fall. As to who had won or lost their previous encounters, the sharp blade and bright pearl of the land of ashes would tell not, for they now slumbered. Darkness now covered their eyes. Fortunately, the prized sword that fell to the earth was rescued from the thin snow. "O sword that keeps vigil over the people, let the path you guided us upon also be law that those who come after shall follow."

Beyond the ruins of the ancient palace and on the edge of the wasteland stands the tranquil sacred forest of Lake Amsvartnir . Legend has it that whoever breaks the golden branch in the forest will find the royal court of the Seelie , which is concealed from mortal eyes during the day. A kingdom of the past, it lies forgotten by both time and space, hidden in shadow where no heavenly light can touch it. Its owner has long departed, leaving behind nothing but a neglected courtyard and a hall stripped bare. Yet, within the palace that should have been abandoned, a young woman's silent lament echoes across its walls. "Once upon a time, the titan craftsman of the skies once wove the destinies of all living beings, the golden harp their instrument of fate." "That was the divine plan of the heavens. If it were followed, the entire world would usher happiness in." "Yet even the ignorant can dream, and in her dream, a new future revealed itself." "She saw men raise a tower to the heavens, and from its heights, the tower's apostle waging war against the sky..." "She saw roaring beasts, each larger than a mountain, breaking free from the bonds of the earth..." "She saw three moons casting their light upon the sea, a sight soon eclipsed by an ancient dragon rising like a tide." "All that vanished the moment she awoke, as if it had never happened." "All that remained was the indescribable glance from those star-like eyes." "Was that love? Perhaps it was just delusion woven from hope, ambition, and a longing for death." "But that matters not now, for their story has ended, and it became Elysium's finale." "The chirping of insects on a long-gone autumn night is the chorus of exiles, singing mankind's most ancient song as they live out their plight..." "They had lost the place of their bodies and souls, with nothing left but songs and memories of the homeland they once knew." The last singers, the first Seelie , they played their final tune in the hall of angels . The wolf who once broke into this place had long since departed. Only unfulfilled dreams remain, and continue to chase phantoms.

A longsword that once shone with the light of the very stars. In the voyager's hand, it becomes a brand-new light that has nothing to do with any past era.
Exaiphanes Blade is a 5-Star Sword obtained during Archon Quest Chapter VII : Act I - Everwinter Without Mercy . It is powered up by each Statue of The Seven unlocked in Snezhnaya .
The Exaiphanes Blade requires no Weapon Enhancement Materials , Weapon Ascension Materials , or Mora to level up, ascend, or refine.

After completing Step 23 of Archon Quest Great Deeds on the Tundra in Chapter VII : Act I - Everwinter Without Mercy , the player can improve the Exaiphanes Blade by applying Cryo to a Statue of The Seven in Snezhnaya , interacting with it, and selecting Enhance Exaiphanes Blade . This will increase its Ascension Phase, Refinement Rank, affixes, and/or passive effects. Unlike Traveler's resonance , the party does not need to have the Traveler nor the sword equipped to upgrade it.

Each Statue of The Seven can only be used to upgrade the Exaiphanes Blade by one stage. If this feature is available at a given Statue, the following message will appear under its map description: Can enhance the Exaiphanes Blade at this Statue of The Seven . If it is not available at a given Statue, the dialogue option will change to View Exaiphanes Blade.

Function Details Within a unique domain, you have obtained a special weapon "Exaiphanes Blade." This extraordinary blade seems to react whenever you get close to a Statue of the Seven in Snezhnaya. Furthermore, it can only be enhanced at these very Statues. Enhancement Rules You can enhance your Exaiphanes Blade after using Cryo to awaken and connect to the Statues of The Seven in Snezhnaya. Each Statue of The Seven in Snezhnaya can bless the Exaiphanes Blade once, enhancing its power.

In silent corridors made from white stone, the sacred law of eternal harmony held leisurely sway between the musicians' fingers. The golden-haired bosom friend caressed the magnificent purple robe, then bent to whisper in the musician 's ear. "My friend. My brother. Lift your head and look at those benighted slaves." Though the voice was sweet as honey and gentle as a song, it was filled with unmistakable pride. "The foolishness of this rabble, to take the grueling toil we bear for decadent lives of luxury." "A shame, a shame indeed... that this beautiful solo should fall upon mortal sod." The musician stopped playing and spoke no refutation, simply sighing. Indeed, though it could cause the very bones of the earth to shake and make miracles mortals could not fathom, The duty known as attunement, of cleansing the bitter sorrow of all waters, was essentially to burn one's soul like firewood. The sorrow, the pain, and the resentment that flowed through the high canals had to be harmonized and purified by them, Such that the God King in his golden palace could fulfill his great, tragic wish to save all souls. "Do not let pride and arrogance blind you, my friend, my brother." "We were elevated to guide and rescue those foolish slaves you speak of." "How shall we play the Sebastos' perfect melody, if we despise them so?" His golden-haired friend snorted coldly and rebuked him bitterly for his weakness. Then, he sat down beside him and began playing on the strings of his lyre. His thought should have been perfected, and yet, as the strings echoed, what he saw were afterimages of his past. Once, he too was a foolish person of bygone times, holding onto what he now knew to be weak expectation, Yet, the watery moonlight and tender, lingering whispers ultimately faded amidst the clamoring bugles, leaving behind only solemn vows unfulfilled. Perhaps he should not have become a Harmost, he thought, for he had never possessed such lofty delusions, But instead, continued to imagine, even as he had in the past, that the descendants of those who dwelled on the high sea might suffer less. " She never believed in the gods, for those who believe in gods would never commit atrocities in their name." That was how his female companion , kind and loving as an elder sister, had once lamented the untrustworthiness of the barbarian tribes. Yes, he thought, of course she would not believe in the gods. But had he not been the same way regarding the Sebastos of the golden palace? Had she been the one to ascend, she too would have bowed before the Sebastos. If he had been the one determined to take revenge, he would surely have falsely claimed to come in a god's name. The musician, the proud musician, the musician who claimed humility, always believed that. He believed that just as he could read her thoughts, he could also read the unspoken sorrows within the people's hearts. Thus did much time pass, until that rebellious fantasy dissipated in the light, Until the grievances of the past were utterly erased, when countless scattered wills finally gained restful slumber within the waterways, Until, at the final moment, when he gazed upon the golden-haired traveler — only then did the musician understand... That none can claim to understand another's heart until the final hour arrives. It was not just her. His dear friend's fanaticism, his female companion's compassion, his God King's grand design... He could not say that he had fully understood a single one of them. Perhaps all the musical passages in this world were but fragments that could never play together, And those who float or sink upon the high sea did nothing in the end but echo within their solitude. But that was no longer important. It was all water under the bridge. All dreams, noble, despicable, pure, filthy, They all converged into the waters like lightly falling raindrops, Like the tears she had shed while embracing his broken body, Silently disappearing into the shadows of the symphony of night and day.
- BP Bounty ( Battle Pass ' Gnostic Hymn )

"If you're asking about stronger spears... They exist, of course." Monomakh once asked his master about this matter in a break between bouts of training so harsh that even a fae could scarcely imagine them. Then, the young man was lean as a white-barked birch, and also akin to the dim ashes of a stove that had lost the last of its lingering warmth. He gasped for air on the ice, but his clear eyes gleamed coldly with a yearning to attain the highest levels of martial prowess. Looking upon his young, frail yet stubborn form, the crimson princess of the snow bent down in silence, And strangely, there was a trace of nostalgia in those frigid eyes, which had survived the ruins of the golden city . "Once, in the lost golden city, I beheld a spear that could even shoot Lord of the Sky down..." "I... don't think I can do that?" The innocent and earnest youth asked tentatively, his voice low. "Of course you can't. You can't even defeat me," the princess replied. "You asked if there were stronger spears in this world, not whether you could or could not learn them." "I, too, once saw a spear strike a blow that could pierce the boundless frosty plains and smash tidal waves of demons into dust." "Like a arrow shot from a bow, it transfixed countless rivers and mountains in but an instant." "I'd like to learn that!" The guileless, honest youth stood up excitedly despite his exhaustion. "That way, I can protect more— Gwahck!" "Start by firming up your stance, kid." The crimson princess of snow sighed, and spoke no more about a past now rendered futile. The years would pass, freezing the warmth of the teachings of yesteryear, and the fires of war would set the far northern wilds ablaze. Amidst a bloody sea of strife, Monomakh, who had sworn to become king, would continue to hone his skills with the spear. Further, further, furtheer still— Until his thrown spear would fall like a silver star, Obliterating all foes who would stand in compassion's way. Let it pierce the Water Imp hidden deep in the frozen lake! Let it pierce the bull stalking the thick forest glades! Let it pierce even the giant beast , mighty as a mountain! This then was the supreme art of the spear, taught to him by the Knyazhna of Blood who had slaughtered countless fae in a previous age. There were some divergences between this and the art she had personally mentored him in, yes, but that was unimportant. Holy, holy, holy! Holy is our Emperor Monomakh, unconquered conqueror of countless winters, most majestic and merciful father! Fae and mortal humans alike yielded prostrate before the Pale Star's throne, and together they sang praises to the king who had unified the vast northern realms, Yet the heart of the god who ruled them all in the name of love grew ever more perplexed. His martial prowess was unequaled, and he had strength enough to tear through glaciers and raging seas, But he could never recreate what his master had spoken of, the spear that had transfixed vast snowfields beyond count in an instant. Even with all his might, hurling his polearm as a bow fires an arrow, he could only traverse half of Snezhnaya... Surely, Monomakh thought, this is because I am not yet strong enough. Master would never lie. Thousands of winters passed, and the snow-blanketed realm had welcomed in roaring gears and molten steel. The valiant and sagacious old emperor paid a personal visit to a blazing-hot workshop, observing the newly-minted mass production of armaments most wondrous. Looking upon the creations forged of steel and Prime Ice which the artisans had named "muskets," His Majesty, the Emperor Monomakh, most severe, most merciful, most wise, fell into a long silence... Ah. That's true. Master never said that the "spears" of the golden city were thrown , did she?
- BP Bounty ( Battle Pass ' Gnostic Hymn )

Tales praising knights' martial feats have been passed down since ancient times in the land of poetry and wine. Amongst these resplendent verses, stories of the "wolf" are always the most beloved. After all, compared to the stately "lion," the free-roaming wolf better suits a poet's heart. Such tales often begin like this: A wandering knight arrives from the northern lands, traveling with a companion named Andrius , and together they visit a city freshly freed . The untamed wolf hunts alongside the knight. They slay the beasts that plague the countryside, and drive back the great serpent that threatens the coast. In time, the homesick lone wolf leaves its spirit behind in the emerald wilds, and the knight, too, departs quietly, tracing the steps of his companion. In the end, none ever learned the ranger-knight's name. And yet, his deeds were never lost to history. Romantic poets, ever eager to read meaning into legend, would have it that the nameless knight always strode onto the battlefield after drinking deep of the snowlands' searing spirits. Yet few know that the knight had come to bear witness to the wolf's fate, and that his homeland was never that merciless land of driving snow. Before he ever became the heart of a tale, the knight lived as he pleased, utterly devoid of a hero's airs. Aside from the Grand Master , who never gave up trying to recruit him, the tavern's guests saw him as nothing more than an ordinary drinker. The sole exception was a boy named Ravenwood , the son of the city's blacksmith. During the few short years the nameless knight remained in Mondstadt, the boy almost made himself his sidekick. They met when the knight first arrived in the city and commissioned the boy's father to forge him a sword. As payment, he offered a handful of coins, each stamped with a mark no one recognized. The blacksmith, who had once forged blades exclusively for the nobles, chose to simply gift the knight that heavy slab of iron . "In the new Mondstadt, everyone should take up arms to defend our freedom." From then on, the boy followed the nameless knight wherever he went, most often standing in silence as he watched the knight practice his sword. At times, when exhaustion set in, the knight would fall to rambling as the sun set, telling stories of a foreign land long forgotten. It was a place where flowers never withered, where rivers ran with mead, and along their banks once stood a warrior kingdom that had since vanished from the world. There, warriors who aforetime sang of devotion and honor bent the knee before power and gold, willingly offering their blades to a greedy tyrant. Thus, the law was abolished, and high virtue crumbled into ruin, until those who had enslaved others were made slaves themselves. The night wind stirred the nameless knight's tattered cloak, and his finely wrought armor with intricate patterns gleamed under the moonlight. Wandering and freedom were to be the final fate of the knight without a homeland, for beneath the moon, there was nothing left for him to defend. Many years later, the tale of Andrius became a legend, and the chain-breaking hero was nowhere to be found. It is said that freedom is born of great sacrifice, yet the comfort that follows often leads back to servitude. The Knights' code still echoed in memory, but former comrades had already broken their oaths, seeking refuge once again in the embrace of the old aristocracy. In such uncertain times, the blacksmith's son picked up a newly forged longsword and set out into the wilds. "Once lost, neither freedom nor the courage to die for it can be reclaimed. Cherish your virtue while it still endures." Days later, a knight draped in a tattered cloak appeared before the gates of the fortress. Wielding his heavy, fearsome sword, he danced with his foes as if guided by the hand of a god. An old man recognized his techniques as those once used by the knight who called himself "Andrius." "It's Andrius! Andrius has returned!" Amid the crowd's roaring cheers, Ravenwood closed his eyes... Charge! For freedom, and chivalry indomitable!

In an age long forgotten, idyll and blossom ruled a land without sorrow. Even the fiercest winds and snows would falter before the towering oakwoods. Hunger was unknown there, and barrenness unheard of — only a paradise whose people sang in the light of the heavens' favor. Thus did the Arcadians , exalted by the thousand winds , believe their holy city's glory would endure for all time, untouched by the world beyond. Yet even such a place could not escape calamity's grasp. Life ebbed away, warmth gave way to stillness, and the ancient nation's spring was laid to rest in a deathly chill that would not stir. With Arcadia now lost, with but the forlorn hope of its salvation to carry, the Knight of the Golden Bough turned from what remained and stepped alone into the endless frost and shadow. "O Gunnhildr , hero named in prophecy, scion of the hallowed line, last light of our people..." "Only when the Golden Bough, pure and untainted, is severed shall the withered wood be stirred to life again..." "Only when the Golden Bough, pure and untainted, is severed shall our sealed paradise endure through all the years yet to come..." At the end of a long and bitter wandering, the knight who trod the frozen wastes came at last upon another sacred grove spared from ruin. No priests, however, remained to tend the white tree. In their place, something else had taken root — something that named itself king , and watched from the high boughs left behind by a vanished envoy. It was no rightful lord, but a warden bound to an old and fading command, a Jack Frost that delighted in riddles, in mockery, in leading the lost astray. The knight pleaded, enduring its capricious trials, each more impossible than the last. Yet the fae king, towering as a mountain, gave answers that were not answers, barring the knight from the grove's heart. And so, for the Golden Bough that might defy calamity, for the fallen capital sealed within its deathbound tomb, A duel bereft of words unfolded across the frost-bound wastes. Steel met frost, and their clash stirred a bitter wind through the desolation, Until the knight's blade rose in a final arc and struck the crown from the fae king's brow. Once more, the champion asked to be bestowed the Golden Bough, for the sake of a homeland already lost. But when the storm fell still, and the drifting snow at last gave way to silence, the truth that stood revealed was colder than any winter. The Golden Bough, once spoken of as imperishable, had been claimed by the frenzied aurora long before any could come to seek it. And with each passing tide of the Light Realm , the last vestiges of mortal reason and the quiet breath of plant life were stripped away, Until only a pallid and withered remnant remained, suspended upon the branch, too frail to bear the longing for paradise reborn. The frostbound creature did not comprehend this loss, that the holy tree was no more, its blessings having departed just as its former lord's dream had ended. And so it remained, oath-bound, guarding the grave it yet believed was hallowed ground. Beneath the withered holy tree was the knight's longsword hurled down, as a soundless laugh came to the hero's lips. A paradise sealed against all change could never endure without end, just as even the gods could find no refuge from their unmaking. With that, any resolve to restore what was lost loosened its hold, and the knight turned toward the storm-swept south, setting out upon a homeward road unknown. In the years that followed, this hero would gather those Arcadian remnants willing to leave their ruined capitol behind, Leading them onward to the high tower where once the wicked dragon had been cast down, to stand before its lord and seek shelter. The chortling Jack Frost King knew naught of this, naturally. It received its defeat unperturbed, And placed the Golden Bough, now emptied of its former divine grace, into the traveler's hands. It gave the frail, fleeting mortal's desire to seek a new dawn its blessing, And held to the hope that the one who had set the Jack Frost here might also, one day, find a path that leads home...-

When the newly-born flames yet boiled over with steam, and were by them lifted through the seared and pockmarked rocky strata, After he had dismissed the attendants, and none but he remained in the royal hall, he ceased half-kneeling before the empty throne and stood up. The sword he drew from the leather scabbard had gone unused for so long that its edge had lost the keenness it once possessed. However, its owner had taken good care of it, allowing not a speck of dust to sully it across these decades. In truth, he was no swordsman, for the half of his blood that he hated had conferred upon him strength too far beyond the common clay. All knew that he had mastered the golden language and could command the rainbow light to a nigh-magical degree, but none knew that he could fight a dragon with his bare hands. The timing of his coming into possession of this weapon, too, was a tad strange. After the many heroes had swept through a certain stronghold of draconic descendants, Everyone lit a bonfire amidst the bones and broken mechanisms, and within a few cups had lost any sense of proportion in their speech. "Everyone knows the best weapon to use against giant beasts is a large two-handed sword! Just watch the creature's movements and BAM! One good hit, and even the hardest skull would be ringing like a bell for half a day." "Hah. If my venom-tipped arrows hadn't sunk deep into their hides and bones, you couldn't ever have gone for their dumb heads. You can barely put your right foot in front of your left most days!" "This one proposes that Ixquieh did the most work, luring them into our trap as she did using Phlogiston . Their automaton soldiers had their weaknesses exposed to us for a good while on her account." "Nah, you did good too, elder brother . Dodging those claw-swipes, swirling and cutting in mid-air one-handed, and all that. Why, you even got onboard one of those dragons and crashed its head into the cliff face, didn't you?" "Help. Help! Someone get me ticket out of hearing these siblings blow each others' horns! I'd rather hear Maghan play the flute." "If you think me a poor player, Uenuku , why don't you cover your ears, hmm? It's not as if I can control your arms." "You know what? We need a judge! That's what we need! Someone to pick the best weapon!" Thus did the raucous crowd turn their eyes toward the red-haired man carrying the meat. Sealing the mouths of the noisy drunkards shut with the grilled meat, he looked at the one who stood in the shadows. "The best weapon, huh..." The man who could use all weapons, naturally, could not give everyone a satisfactory answer, but when the man with the flaming hair turned his gaze upon him, Ah, he thought to himself, so that was it. Indeed, surely it could only be so. He was himself the other's most perfect weapon. How could it be otherwise? "By the way, you've gone without weapons all this time, right? So, what do you want to use? Whatever you pick... We'll take that to be the best weapon!" It was only later that he discovered that this was one of that man's aggravating habits — throwing ridiculous questions at bystanders. At any rate, he made his decision... His answer likely only pleased Ahpub and that man who now did not need to answer a troublesome question. The latter fulfilled said promise, and it was a deed rich with meaning indeed — fire was brought forth to smelt the works of the ancient dragons, and from them a sharp blade was made for him. "It's standard practice to make weapons of war from materials we gather from our hunts." "Give it a try. The material and center of gravity have all been tuned to your proportions." A weapon gifted by that man could never perform poorly. Many times would he use himself as bait, and use this blade to cut off the bewildered foe's heads. He swore to use this blade to hunt down all the inhuman heretics, to create a realm belonging only to humans for the one who had given him this sword. But it had been too long since he had last wielded this sword in battle, and he was never very good at it anyway. The crimson-eyed young man 's face, yet-immature but wrathful, flashed before him with a might not unlike a god 's, And the sword that once slew heretics was wrenched from his hand, and then was thrust into his breast even as he teetered on the brink, about to fall into the mud. He watched the other party as his body sank into the pitch-black mire. "Hah... That's right. I see now. It... could only be thus." Before he closed his eyes, he looked upon the red-eyed young man's flames for moment, And lo, he took it for the shadow of the cunning crimson fox, face filled with sorrow, flashing across the corner of the collapsing palace.

The Water Imp who sings alone has always kept close this fairytale heard in her youth: Once upon a time, a very, very long time ago, a child was born of the breaking waves. This child was more noble than the daughters of the sea, and fairer than all living things upon the earth. But sweeter than her face was her voice in song; whenever she sang the ancient hymns, Sailing mariners would allow themselves to sink into the whirlpools, and even the frozen seas thawed before her melodies. Then, as tales of this sort so often go, a prince of the land entered the story. The child born of the waves, filled with love and wonder, followed the prince onto the land, Paying no heed to the warnings of her older sisters, who cried, "Our dear sister, the creatures of the land are not to be trusted." Paid she no heed either to the calls of her father: "My child, the ocean floor is the true garden for your song." And so, from that day forth, she sang only for the handsome prince, for his glory and his ambitions, bringing beauty to the royal banquets with her singing so that he might boast of his power and grandeur. In return, the prince bestowed upon her silk, golden robes, and agate, granting her leave to sleep upon cushions of velvet; he cherished her as his most precious jewel, and the splendid palace became the jewel-box. At this point in the tale, the young Water Imp interjected confidently: "And from that day on, they lived happily ever after. That is how all fairytales end." But it was not to be. The storyteller shook their head gently, and replied, "If the tale had ended so, it would not have been passed down by our people for a hundred years." And so the young Water Imp listened on, unprepared for the turn the tale would take... The child born of the waves remained at court, continuing to sing for the prince's glory. But even as the prince applauded her magnificent high notes, he could not comprehend the sorrow in her song. Over time, her skill in song grew ever more refined, yet within her alone grew a foreboding of ill to come. Her voice grew harsher day by day. Then one day, The child born of the waves found herself no longer able to sing the ancient hymns that brought tears to the eyes, or any touching melody for that matter. The prince grieved for her, only because she was like a priceless jewel that had lost its worth, While her sisters of the water rose to shore hand in hand, calling out to her, mourning her silence, "Our dear sister, find your voice once more, for that is your true soul. Find your voice once more, lest you turn into foam and perish." The sisters of the water brought a sacred artifact to their cherished sister. Their kin had sealed the deal in blood, obtaining from the fae of the wind the method to free her: "Our dear sister, your song has been imprisoned by that man's indifference and disdain. Let his heart spill its blood, and this artifact shall return you to our side." The child born of the waves returned to the palace with the artifact. Mindful of her kin's sacrifice, she raised the blade above the sleeping prince, her hands trembling, only to let the strike fade into a sigh. And so, the ancient hymns were lost forever in the twilight of that fairytale. The storyteller shook their head softly, allowing the ending to dissolve into a sigh of its own. "So, what is this story trying to tell us?" the young Water Imp asked, uncertain. "The story tells us that we, the Water Imps, should sing only for those who truly understand our song."

The precious stone known as jade is known to shine even in the darkest night. When carved into a bow, they say that the arrows fired from it would seek out and destroy all evil. The gaze of the lord of the mountains remained resolute and cold till the end, chilling and contained like the eternal glint of golden jade. In those endlessly turbulent years , the tremulous, resounding howls of the bowstring replaced comforting song. They say that that god who once had great insight into the weakness in mortal hearts was slain by this very bow. Her eyes were keen and her mind was sharp, and she excelled in dominating the wills of those who served her. "See, my child, how this dauntless hero is gnawed by fear. See how selfless rulers bow as if they lacked spines." "Behold, my child, how those lovers who swore by the sky and earth betray and torment another with lies." Surrounded by hatred and resentment, the god reclined upon her throne, savoring the fruit of joy, watching the juices flow between her fingers. And with the sound of formless, clattering chains, blood-drunk on agony and frenzy alike, the loyal bloodhound at her feet devoured "dreams." Those unbending bones resisted the piercings and floggings, though each heartbeat would bring fresh agonies. The wondrous taste of those blood-drenched dreams was matched only by their transience, and the pure hatred and revulsion they produced indeed brought the god to ecstasy. "Then tell me, child, tell me! How do those sweet dreams you have devoured taste?" "Child, know that love is but a fleeting fog. It is power that forms the stuff of sweet dreams." Pain and cruelty were but the ripple effects of power. It was shattered dreams that were the joyous, sweet wine. But the god who was herself so sharp never expected that her heart, too, would be pierced by arrows of jade stone. When her form crumbled, the unnumbered fragments of dreams would also scatter and fade into nothing... Thus did the god who pursued and chained human hearts go to her destruction, when the bow, its power like a towering mountain, pronounced retribution upon her. Such an end was to be expected, that one who delighted so in tyranny should come to a cruel end. When peace was restored and the nights were no longer filled with lamentations and mourning, the mighty bloodstained bow would be carefully sealed. There, it would patiently await the rise of another tyrant, to one day again pierce their heart with a light that no darkness can hide.
- BP Bounty ( Battle Pass ' Gnostic Hymn )
