Passing through layers of rocky ridges, the hidden spring of a forgotten tomb absent from all chronicles finally revealed itself at dusk. A whispered tale it was, that ran only among the mining tribes, speaking of an adeptus who forged swords from flowing light, an adeptus who once vanished into the watery moon beneath the depths. Seeking traces of that adeptus, the girl ventured into the shadowed gorge, landing softly among the pines on her climbing sandals. No one was around; only moonlight spilled through the narrow clefts, sketching half-formed phantoms behind bamboo curtains. "In ages past, before Mt. Tianheng rose, and the seas still knew no calm, there was a kingdom named Lang-Gan on the western coast." "With roasted millet and boars proffered, beating earthen drums on wicker stands, the people honored the gods with utmost sincerity." "Thus the Heavenly being descended, teaching them to till earth and sow grains, to spin thread and weave cloth." "And thus it was proclaimed: Fair shall be the fortune of your kingdom, long-enduring as the Heavens; vast shall be the blessings of your realm, limitless as the Earth itself..." But the mighty dragon who once stood alongside the Lord of Geo could not escape sudden ruin , trampling the flourishing lands of humanity's master. The mountain folk could only take up their ancestors' weapons and follow the Yaksha beneath that lord's banner, resisting the calamity that descended from the Heavens. Searching for the sword that would save them from calamity, the daughter of the sheer cliffs and crystal sands followed ancient songs, at last reaching the kingdom of her forebears, hidden within the caverns. Hearing now her purpose declared, the silver shadow seemed to stir with a soft laughter, rippling along with the spring under the moon. "Alas! The path of the Heavens is ever-shifting and unknowable; fortune and woe are intertwined and unpredictable." "In those days, a blazing comet fell from the East, descending upon the western frontiers. Unrest followed in its wake..." "Thereafter, the heavens toppled and the sea lay in ruin; the earth was swallowed into chasms , deep as the whale dives. The people perished, and the realm was left to woe..." "Glorious blooming flowers and splendid woven brocades are naught but reflections on water, phantoms in mirrors. Eternal prosperity — how could it ever be attained?" Perhaps the stone fortresses in the mountains would one day crumble into jade-colored ruins, becoming Glazed Sand Crystals in the hands of merchants. But to the young girl, such things were yet a hundred generations off. They were idle tales for the distant future, not for today. The shadowed figure casually pulled a wild bamboo stalk from the slanted cliff. The tip broke and fell, but the girl caught it before it touched the ground. "As the waxing moon bears its light, one might chase forms and shadows. Now, now... You've understood the true essence of the sword. Why seek its physical form, then?" It is said that the girl later trained a hundred elite warriors in sword-and-halberd combat. Alongside the Lord of Geo, they subdued the dragon and quelled evil across the land. By the time the malevolent demons were vanquished and the world was now in peace, those once-fierce warriors became shrewd merchants haggling over every coin in Shenglu Hall . Today, it is only when selling their exquisite porcelain, fired from Sand Crystals, that they speak of those ancient, fanciful tales. The mountains stand silent, while the cold moon hanging over the harbor city holds vigil, illuminating every river just as it did thousands of years ago.

No secret remains forever hidden, for even in the darkest and most of secret of rooms, negligence will always leave a crack. No matter its complexity or brilliance, a lock is vulnerable from the moment of its creation, Just as even the most meticulous plan is bound to sow the seeds of its own failure. To the young woman who claimed to be the successor of a master thief , secrets and mechanisms were but mere games. Neither the proud gentry of the north, nor the sycophantic merchants along the borderland , Could build an unpickable locks to match her skill. The more intricate a design is, the more fragile its construction. With enough pressure, no lock can hold forever. And so, as the notoriety of the "Bladebreaker" blazed across the land, Schanzkowska, the peasant's daughter, became lost to all memory in time. The girl who claimed the mantle of a fae lord pilfered countless treasures, her laughter ringing through the dim extravagance with the abandon of a genuine noble. What should have remained to be a mundane, uninspired life, untouched by any spark, changed dramatically one day when a voice suddenly rang out: "My dear young lady, oh proud and ridiculous imposter, I'm guessing you're the first person to see this news." "The Grand Duke's so-called treasure is of no interest to me. You may have it, my dear, just as you have claimed the mantle of that master thief..." "But do remember: I was the first to break this mechanism. Let my name be etched into your heart, a name you will remember forever, alongside your failure." The Grand Duke's dinner banquet had been a blatant provocation to thieves everywhere, for the secret treasure on display was impossible to steal, or so he boasted. The young lady, scoffing at the arrogance, vowed to make away with his treasure in what would be one last heist before her retirement. But someone had beaten her to the punch. The thief, who went by the "Escape Artist," had left a taunting message on the wall, and its sting left her seething with fury — as well as humiliation. What followed were countless grudging contests, each one ending in a humbling defeat. The lockpicking skills the young woman once prided herself were found constantly wanting in her rivalry with this unseen nemesis. The more she failed, the more her shame burned, and the more she hungered to meet the one who kept beating her. This went on until one day, the infuriating rival who always left her red with rage vanished without a trace. Subsequently, word reached her that this thief had been caught and executed. For reasons she could not explain, she found herself at the rambling graves, unearthing the stone coffin containing the prisoner's body. But when she dug it up and looked inside, she found that the body was gone. All that remained was a mocking sentence, etched in the cold stone. Wiping away tears she couldn't quite explain, the young woman cursed her longtime foe's cunning through clenched teeth. As always, she swore to dedicate her life to uncovering the truth behind his faked death and, once and for all, outwitting him. In the end, time claimed both the beauty she once flaunted and the final breath she held. Bereft of the strength to pick even a simple lock, the woman cursed his name one last time before resting inside the empty coffin.

"As you have always known, my Aila — my heart's child, my dearest, my most beloved," "In our blood flows the purest silver light, and we alone are worthy to receive the grace of the Frost Moon ." "You shall not wed the son of an outlander, for you are destined to bear the heir to Elysium for the people of the far north ." "The mistress of the Frost Moon has already spun every path in the world with her silver thread, and all things now move in step with the thread's silent dance." Those were the days before the pitch-black calamity swept through the borderlands, when the Archpriestess of the far north repeated her blasphemous and misguided deeds in vain. Perhaps out of excessive devotion to the gods, or because she had never believed in dead gods who had never shed their light upon the world, (There was, after all, no real difference between the two. Her grandmother, who had raised her, certainly never distinguished between them.) The young handmaiden, with unwavering faithfulness, carried out every last one of the venerable Archpriestess's commands. She never defied that kind and gentle old grandmother, no matter how dreadful the punishments cloaked by her soft words. Whether someone's thread was to be severed by a sharp silver blade, or another's singing voice must be silenced in the dead of night, All sins were borne to purify the holy blood bestowed by the moon, for only by drinking crimson water could one hone absolute flawlessness. "As you have always done, my Aila — my heart's child, my dearest, my most beloved," "Since he has put his trust in you, use your wisdom to guide him. Set his heart on the right path and lead him to the sanctuary." "The man called Solovei is nothing but a treacherous murderer, and yet, he dares to seek our protection after all the wicked deeds he has committed." "When he comes here, you will thrust your sword through his heart from behind to sever his venomous thread." The only response the Archpriestess got, as ever and always, was silence, and those accustomed to silence from their followers always wind up taking it for consent. The handmaiden's lengthy years of obedience had long convinced the Archpriestess that all that suffering brought on by impurity had never once stirred resentment in her. But of course. She was the blessed one. The one destined to bear the Sacred Heir. Of course, she understood that the sacrifices she offered up were in service of a decree a thousand years in the making. So, even as the pure silver blade pierced her back, the last Archpriestess of the far north could not comprehend the source of the betrayal. "Heh... Mr. Solovei was right. You were just lying to us, Grandma Lovia." "If that were not the case... why would you bleed dawn-light crimson, rather than moonlit silver, when your thread was cut?"

Of all the stories handed down from the ancient forest, only the bird with wings drawn close is willing to sing them before the world. Its song begins amid the splendor of spring, in an age when peace had endured for centuries and the forest had grown deep beneath a wealth of branch and leaf. Yet as the season turned, the ice began to thaw and run in streams along the riverbed, carrying with it from lands still bound in frost the distant ringing of arms. Soon, none could halt the advance of the Blood-Devourer , and across the snowy realms, every nation was brought before the same cruel choice: to bow or to perish. The treeborn , however, whose roots reached back beyond even the frozen earth, still remembered their gracious lords of old, for that memory endured in the ordering of their leaves and in the rings that traced their wood. Though the golden bough had long lain broken, though lofty dreams had fallen to ruin, and nations once resplendent as the morning stars had vanished beneath boundless fields of ice, The descendants of the forests still desired no part in strife, wishing only to remain faithful to the peace they had kept since ages immemorial. Even the Knyazhna of Blood , for all her tyranny, had never sought to exterminate their kind — much less, they believed, would the Volkodlak who bore the name of wisdom. Until the bird returned, at the season when it should have settled upon tender new boughs, only to behold the haze of battle rising in every quarter. For no greater offense than declining, with all due courtesy, the summons to pledge themselves to the Volkodlak, the holy forest left behind by the dawn-star had been consumed in flame. Thus, when the King of the Pale Star came at last with his chosen retinue, scarcely a tenth of the ancient treeborn remained alive. Unbidden tears slipped from the eyes of Vaselisa , daughter of the King of the Water Imps , as she mourned in song the countless lives so unjustly taken. While Strivozha , saint of the Vila , wept until no words would come, and beseeched the King of the Pale Star to grant the forest his protection as well. "O King Lesnik , venerable grandsire of the wilderness and of the myriad forests, I am Monomakh, heir to the Pale Star and bearer of the Pale Crown." "I have come to end the strife of this world and bring peace upon the earth. I would found a realm of mercy and forgiveness, where no living creature shall ever come to harm again." "O King Lesnik, venerable grandsire of the wilderness and of the myriad forests, I therefore come before you with a plea, though I do not ask that your kin spill their blood in my name." "I ask only for such healing herbs and leaves as you might bestow upon us, that my companions may tend the wounds borne by the earth." The great lord of the trees looked down upon the young golden-haired boy, as a Vila might look upon the Domovoy dwelling far below. The canopy murmured, and after a silence steeped in ages of ancient pride, all that long-held reserve yielded at last to a single weary sigh. Then a venerable bough broke from the ancient tree, and the bird took it gently into its beak, bore it forth, and laid it before the golden-haired youth. "Go forth, young king. See your promise fulfilled, and make of this world a peace everlasting, beyond all sorrow and unrest." "Into your keeping I give my life, and no barrier wrought of shadow shall turn aside its edge." "Mourn not the dead, for all who draw breath must in time sink back into the dust. This truth I learned long ago." "Yet though they return to dust, the forest shall remember. When spring comes again, the new-grown branches and leaves shall carry that memory onward."

"When the ' Eternal Moon ' fell, the heavens and earth were thrown into chaos." "When the ' Iridescent Moon ' shattered, the crimson shadow sank into the abyssal sea." "When the ' Frost Moon ' ceased to turn, nations faltered and fell into ruin." "The world, no longer sheltered by 'Eternity,' marches toward its final breath." "Until Elysium dawns and begins to turn the primordial wheel." Following an ancient prophecy, the descendants of the Golden City erected a lonely temple on the desolate tundra. For a thousand years, the moonlight had quietly streamed through the frosty forest. The descendants of the north still upheld their ancient rituals and faith, Forging pale ceremonial crowns from secret silver and choosing the purest Archpriestesses to guide their people. As in the days of old, they continued their prayers and chants, though their gods had long departed and the sky no longer answered. An outsider might regard these practices as the actions of the foolish, clinging to old, meaningless ways. Yet only those these prayers and sacrifices, passed down for a thousand years, could serve as emblems and signs for a people who had lost their homeland. The spindle-wheel of fate had rusted, and the silver thread had grown dim. Prophetic visions alone could not bring true hope to the people. "Who would worship a dead god, or endure such hopeless suffering for an empty dream?" Just as in ages and epochs past, now returned to the earth's depths through countless cycles, the ignorant continued to yearn for tangible guidance. Thus, those rituals had become their great isolation, a high wall keeping them unseen and unknown to the world beyond and its peoples. So it had been for a thousand years, and so it would remain for a thousand more, until the prophesied Elysium descended, Until the pure bloodline, refined through generations, produced the sacred heir who would make the world fall to its knees. And when that time came... All lies and sins would be forgiven, even praised, for they all served the pure Elysium beneath the moon. What follows is the sacred journey of the Frostmoon Scions , who have long ceased to turn outsiders away. The first Moonchanter, a saint graced by the divine and the one who witnessed the birth of a god, was once the mortal Aila . According to stories passed down by later generations, she foresaw the new moon 's birth and, moved by divine revelation, chose to abandon the old rites. "She was the chosen one. Blessed from birth, a devout soul untouched by the sublunary sphere's countless corruptions." "She saw the spinning wheel's dead silence and the silver thread's despair, for a millennium of praise had become nothing more than a hollow echo." "The faded glory never once had pity upon the desolate borderlands. Now, only the new moon, on the cusp of its birth, held the promise of true hope." "Aila's devotion earned her the admiration of even the last Archpriestess of the far north, who opened her heart to her without hesitation." "She earnestly entrusted Aila with the authority to lead the people, and granted her the honor of sealing the ancient sanctuary with her own hands." "Thus was the old glory buried, the hollow titles and meaningless past cast aside. Now, they would await the advent of the newborn god." No one would again hold the title of Archpriestess of Hyperborea. Only the Moonchanter remained standing amidst the pure light. ... Countless moons rose and fell. Those who dreamed of Elysium found only the shadow of the axe, while those who longed for salvation were swept into by the flowing light. The mad monk who reached for the heavens lost his mind. The old master of the Pale Star throne is gone. The White Emperor fell into the churning black waves of filth . At last, even the nightingales fell silent. Countless names faded from the world beneath the moon, becoming echoes that the living were left thereafter to judge. As promised to the Torchforger , the new moon's maiden spun a prayer song and laid it to rest alongside the sanctuary. And until the Whitenight erases the final witnesses of that era, only the moonlight shall remain, flowing quietly even as it did a thousand years before. "When the 'Eternal Moon' fell, the heavens and earth were thrown into chaos." "When the 'Iridescent Moon' shattered, the crimson shadow sank into the abyssal sea." "When the 'Frost Moon' ceased to turn, nations faltered and fell into ruin." "The world, no longer sheltered by 'Eternity,' marches toward its final breath." "Yet, from the ashes, the 'New Moon' rises, its ascent spinning the wheel of fate anew..." "And those who follow the tides still sing their songs and offer their prayers." "For the new moon shall come, precisely as the ancients have foretold."

"O little dove, child of the moon," "Though dust may stain your fair white feathers," "Though you lie down not in a warm embrace," "May the moon be with you in your slumber." A shattered husk falls toward the misty land that never became a moon, their blessings scattered into clear waters and mossy plains. In a prison beyond the reach of both Time and Wind, the one who traverses backward beholds the eternal slumber of three sisters . In the eternal and fleeting, unbound by start or cease, the imprisoned Moon Maiden drifts through the night, Her consciousness gently caressing the hazy, ethereal memories woven in the tapestry of yesteryear... The silvery vessel patrolled between mountains and seas at the moment when day and night intertwined. In the age when the pulse of the earth's bones had not yet yielded to the heavens, the vessel guided the souls of the untainted, Ferrying them across the corrupted mortal realm and the frigid atmosphere to rest in peace on the dark side of the moon, hidden from view. Yet, it could not draw the gaze of the three mistresses of the golden hall to meet the eyes of the children of humankind. The Lord of the Seven Calamities would not tolerate the gods showing mercy for the petty sufferings of the mortal world, For before the primordial laws, only complete submission and humble reverence could be considered true care for humanity. Even the three sisters, high in their jade-colored chambers, spinning the silver threads of fate for all living beings... When it came to ancient peoples and mortals struck down by fate, they were bound in threefold silence. Pity, compassion, admiration and longing were always separated by a gossamer veil of moonlight, spanning hundreds of thousands of miles. Whether compelled to turn against their dark, corrupted master of old , in defense of the living beings on Earth, Or being constrained to turn blind eyes each to the other, amidst internal strife, so that the ember of defiance might be kept alight, Or being driven to stain their own hearts with darkness and corruption to seek vengeance against a tyrannical usurper... Like her, they walked the mortal world. Like her, they were three moons that illuminated countless cold nights. In the end, it was their own path they could not light. At the end of all three ways lay the night of oblivion. That was the future once lamented by the vanished moons, in the era when three were still three. But, in the dark night, were there truly only three paths that they saw? In the memories that belonged to her alone, there was a golden star not of this world. It was reflected in the cold, lonely courtyard under the silver moon — that strand of starlight had always lingered in her heart... And linger it did, even across millions of years, even across countless worlds long extinguished. That star, which her gaze once had captured, would surely illuminate her journey home... In the next timeless instant of such unwavering belief, begins the era when three are no longer three. At the edge of darkness, the Lord of the Crossroads looked back at the fourth path beyond the three-way fork, Amid honeyed veils of dreamy hues, she tarried silently, waiting for the appointed meeting with her companions beneath the stars. "O little dove, child of the moon," "Let not sorrow for hardship or parting weigh upon your heart," "The flowers will bloom once more by your window," "And the moon will be with you in your slumber by night or day."

How many rains must fall upon a seed before it bears fruit? How many choices must one make in life to find the way to happiness? There are things even the gods may not know. Yet, mortals must struggle to learn them, even if it should cost them their entire lives. Such a choice lay before Soini , the son of a poor farmer, and he could not help but tighten his grip on the shovel in his hand. A secret treasure had been unearthed from the tired, hollowed-out soil. If he could sell it on the black market, he might be able to escape a life of poverty. A ragged man with treasure in his hands was bound to draw greedy eyes. And with the brutal winter closing in, he had no choice but to take a precarious step. First purchasing a Fatui uniform, the clever peasant then closed his first deal, using the disguise to intimidate any threats who might lurk. Soini was reveling in success when a dark shadow surged out at the end of the road — the very same thief who had sold him his uniform. "Hand over the treasure, or this barren patch will be your tomb!" Forced under the blade, the peasant complied. The two came to the field where the treasure lay hidden. The thief's gaze fell on a jagged piece of black spine bone, and a sudden, wild thrill ignited within him. "Surely these are the remains of the master thief ," he said, lifting the bone with trembling hands. He was unaware that in this moment, he had sealed his own fate. With a heavy thud, a farming shovel drove the thief into the earth. In that moment, Soini knew he had to leave the farm for good. The now-bloodied treasure had opened a perilous path to the very summit of the black market, a path Soini marched grimly through. He came to be named "Godfather" by the desperate criminals who flock here, lured by the charnel scent of fortune. "Oh most esteemed Godfather, your wisdom is the light we follow. The black market is honored to count you as one of our own!" Yet, no one really knows why a worn-out shovel, of all things, rests above the Godfather's throne. In those blood-soaked times, he kept the shovel as a constant reminder that for a robber, death was always a hair's breadth away. Now, countless treasures lie buried admist the border reefs. Each one is a potential chip, to be traded for loyalty and terror. He no longer wastes time agonizing over choices, for his power and wealth can correct any misstep. The world is governed by a hidden law, an unstoppable cycle in which the rich grow richer and the poor sink ever deeper into hardship. The Godfather was no wiser in mind than the poor peasant he once was, and no different in deed from the thief who once tried to kill him. "Then why? Why was it I who claimed the treasure my shovel unearthed, and another whom the shovel buried?" Was it all nothing more than chance? Did luck simply favor him more than the thief who met his end that day? A thousand choices and a lifetime of sacrifice, all made in pursuit of happiness. Yet in the end, it had all come down to chance! A wave of disgust washed over Soini at the sheer injustice of it all. "This is where all my treasures are," he uttered. Thus did he reveal his treasure map to the public. Anyone in the borderlands could now vie for the prize, armed with nothing but their own capabilities. Let them succeed or fail. Soini cared not how their stories would end either way. The Godfather, draped in finery yet still gripping a shovel, had come to understand the kind of justice Reed Miller preached: "If the laws of this world are destined to be unbalanced, let gold find its way to gold, and let earth return to earth." "This world needs a hand to balance the scales — let that hand belong to the thief."

The decaying Cinder City and the usurper 's delirious dream collapsed together into a blaze as brilliant as the sun. The scarlet-eyed hero summoned the god's fiery wrath, burning the blighted, corrupted throne to drifting ash. Decades have passed since Maghan the dragon slayer drove the old ruler from the deep valleys. In the villages that once worshiped the dragons , new generations have long since forgotten their ancestral oaths. Thus, when the young priest Wagadu fulfilled Maghan's final wish... And laid him to rest in a nameless grave, taking up his bow, and setting forth toward the mist-shrouded mountains... He had no understanding of what the old man's dying words truly meant. What was it to "renew the covenant"? What was it to "restore peace"? Wagadu had no idea. He simply believed the old priest had asked him to return his cherished bow to the perilous Night Realm ... To soothe the wrathful spirits long abandoned since the age of ancient sacrifice. He parted the veil of mist and climbed the threefold stone stair. At the ineffable border of the shadowed realm, a vast, labyrinthine hall revealed itself. Its intricate corridors glowed softly in the flowing light. Before the young priest could discern whose hand had inscribed the gilded runes, a sudden surge of fog clouded his sight. Visions rose in the mist and filled his mind. In a daze, countless shifting forms shimmered like iridescent light. He saw a maiden with eyes of turquoise, a colossal serpent draped in starlight, and a white spider weaving the sun and moon... He saw figures of black gold and white steel, a sly hare mocking a wild fox, and a coyote struggling in tar. Terrified, Wagadu fell to his knees. He begged the sacred ones of the Night Realm to forgive his intrusion. But when the mist finally lifted, the being that loomed above the hall and gazed down upon him was not the dead he had imagined. It was a mighty dragon , its wings unfurled like a rainbow cascading across the heavens. "O soulless one, whose fate is bound to the stars, do not let my form fill you with fear." "I have long comprehended your purpose, even if your own heart remains veiled in ignorant mist." "The priest who named himself dragon slayer sent you to forge a covenant for the ages to come." "The noble blood of the ancients never stained his blade, and that sincerity speaks louder than a thousand words." "It matters not. Our king has long perished, and I have grown weary of tending to my kin who dwell within dreams." "I am willing to impart all the secret rites I know, that your tribes may prosper." "To let you hear the whispers of the night without giving blood to the envoy who has fallen into the underworld." "For this, I ask but two things in return, as price for the covenant to be sealed." "First, your descendants must treat the ancient people I once protected as friends and equals." "They must heed their counsel at all times, and never allow their oaths to become mockery like the Grand Alliance ." "Second, your descendants must strike my name from every woven record and scroll." "Let no self-proclaimed sage uncover it, lest they bring ruin upon our pact through their foolish revenge." "You need not consider, only accept. The Wayob that shelters you was once my servant ." "Long before your birth, she told me of this transgressive covenant." Like one just awakening, unable to tell dream from reality, the dazed Wagadu nodded to signify acceptance. In an instant, the gilded hall and the mighty dragon dissolved like mist from a past age. Wagadu was still wondering whether the visions he had just witnessed were anything more than a fleeting dream born of fatigue... When suddenly, he felt a soft, feather-like touch at his side, cold as the night wind, that made him instinctively turn around. There, according to legend, stood the first Iktomisaurus , newly emerged from the Night Kingdom.
- Obtained during the Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey event.

After the great tower of Shah Ramshahr finally fell, like a honeyed yet poisoned dream swallowed by the blood-soaked sands... His royal power shifted between countless states as fleeting as the morning dew, until it was buried itself in yet more blood and tears. Beneath the sapphire domes, those nobles who once pledged allegiance to the tyrant broke free of his yoke... Only to follow false sages and be drawn into games of carnage and collapse amid the scorching sands once more. O, the proud people of Tulaytullah who had long forgotten the silent warnings of the sages. It was only when their ambitions faded along with Gurkan's name that they came to know the true cost of rebellion. By the time the brutal Khagans arrived on horseback, there were no more warriors guarding the Garden of Endless Pillars . And like tamed beasts, those who dwelled in gilded dreams had no choice but to lower their heads before new masters once more. Soldiers and tax collectors, driven by insatiable greed, came from distant lands to prey upon the already weary people. Though the viridian court, which had claimed such benevolence, was unrelentingly harsh to its people. There will always be those who, subjugated beneath the iron-clad hooves of foreign tribes, seek solace in a romanticized past. They whispered praise for the brief reign of King Humayun while huddled in the shade, taking shelter from the searing sun. The young noble Goudarz stepped into the sacred hall buried deep beneath the sands, determined to free his countrymen from their shackles. Legend has it that the palace belonged to the Ibis King , and the wisest of the seven sage monks — the keeper of records — who served as secret envoy to the moon and stars. But that desperate and near-hopeless assault stood little chance, for no plan could match the conqueror's forces, which blazed with the brilliance of the sun. The wise men of Tighnar had long since fled, and that magnificent sanctuary of wisdom in the desert lay buried beneath the iron-hued sea of sand. Yet, from the depths of a dried-up spring, sacred and ancient echoes rose in answer to the young man's prayers... "O reckless child, o noble one, you yearn for the power of the blazing sun and the fury of sandstorms, yet you dream the fool's dream of raising a tower from quicksand." "I can bestow upon you a power not yet witnessed by prophet or proselyte, much as one might give bitter and brackish water to a thirsty camel." "However, the lord of the flowers and oases once left three riddles for my master, King Deshret ." "But he, wise and sagacious as he was, could not answer them before he fell into that poisonous dream ." "If you can lift the fog of confusion that has long plagued me, I will grant you the power of a king." The young Goudarz answered thusly: "Then pray reveal these ancient riddles, o Holy One, of the sacred edicts, writing, medicine, and wisdom." "I shall offer my mortal answers with truest sincerity, for there is no room for the shadows of falsehood on my path." And so, the wisest of them all among the sage monks spoke thusly: "What rises and falls in endless turns, perishing at its apex before swelling once more?" "Like the moon, it waxes full, then wanes away into nothing." "Both the wise and the foolish yearn for it, in ceaseless cycles of desire." "Yet like the tides, it ebbs and flows within the hearts of men." The young Goudarz answered thusly: "What you speak of is conspiracy and treachery. The robes of those who speak idly of virtue conceal nothing but festering weakness and fatigue." "It is this very weakness that brought down the sapphire domes, and it is this very weakness that has driven the people to cry out in sorrow." The sage monk burst out in laughter, though he did not directly address the youthful noble's answer. Nonetheless, he handed him the Staff of Falsehoods. And this was how Goudarz's name became lost to history... To be replaced by the mighty title of King Saleb Dowleh. The warrior who once would brook no lies had gained kingly power through cunning. Casting the illusion of a golden age over the fading hues of twilight. ... It was not until even the most perfect lie could no longer control his insatiable thirst for power... Until King Deshret's creations could no longer fabricate the illusion of divine manifestation... Until the voice of the Ibis King rose once more to ask him that very same question... That the aged king gave his final answer amid the laments of Gurabad : "O Holy One, all I speak are lies. Even I do not trust my own words." "The only thing I can do now is fight to the death. At the very least, I shall not betray once more the trust of the brothers who have come to my rescue." "O, Holy One, whether you seek truth or falsehood, you must taste it in your own blood." His kingly power was seized by the Deys of other tribes, and on and on it went, until the various kingdoms were ground to dust by the desert winds. And, as if collecting moonlight like amber honey, the holy one had taken the king's last will as his final answer.

"O, my kind child Lovia , the purest of them all, receive this Archpriestess's staff." "Only your mercy and compassion can open the eyes of the lost lambs and bless them with serene, gentle joy." "Only you can give them the happiness known to the weak — the comfort of being led — for they are born with hearts that ache to belong." "Only you can correct the twisted falsehoods that lurk in the shadows beneath the moon, for there is no other path but the way of truth." "The mistress of the Frost Moon has already spun every path in the world with her silver thread, and all things now move in step with the thread's silent dance." The ancient blessings gradually flickered out like a dying candle in the cold night, as the young handmaiden took over the staff of the former Archpriestess. The girl was an orphan from another land — though she was unaware of this fact. She should never have been chosen, for she had never been blessed. The pale white Frost Moon no longer gazed down at them, and even the purest of saints, born of the purest bloodline, could no longer wield its radiant light. As the former faithful turned aside and whispers of doubt grew louder, the increasingly frail Archpriestess had no choice but to place her adopted daughter upon the fragile throne. She hoped that her kindness might at least unite the divided followers, despite the clear, bright moonlight having never flowed through her veins. And just as the Archpriestess had hoped, the handmaiden, compassionate and ever tender toward the weak, held true to what she believed was "right." Light and shadow, brightness and dark, good and evil, life and death... There is a "right" and "wrong" side to everything that exists in this moonlit world. As such, only by walking the path of absolute "right" can one hope to guide all beings toward true happiness. To walk the path of righteousness is to give grain to the hungry and tend the sick through the long night. To mend the wounds of suspicion with sincerity and understanding, and to soothe the troubled hearts of one's kin. The right kind of kindness will eventually become a gentle flame in the night, warming cold and indifferent hearts and devouring resentment and hate. This was the truth the girl named Lovia so stubbornly held on to, as she cast her eyes — so full of compassion — over her followers. That is, until the maiden of the purest bloodline in all the far north — a sister by bond, not blood... Fell beneath a traitor's blade. She sacrificed herself to protect her elder sister, who was still struggling to convince her flock. Then and there, in that blinding silvery-white, the girl who was unable to let out even a single cry of anguish finally came to a new realization: The path she had chosen to that day was not the "right" one after all, And the kindness of the weak was but an unforgivable delusion. If the true moon were to withhold its gift of hope, then let lies be spun into a gentle dawn. That would stir the long-awaited fervor of the weak and grant the suffering lambs a paradise where all may rest as equals. Should the ethereal new moon never rise again, then let absolute authority reign over the mortal dream. So that the straying flock might once more be made obedient and no longer grieve for gifts bestowed in vain. Indeed, that was the "right" kind of love, the only salvation left for the weeping masses. The "right" path of kindness, even for one who had never truly laid eyes on the moon's silvery threads. Those who dared defy this truth would have their wicked falsehoods washed away in blood. For the right path could suffer no defilement at the hands of the wicked until her late sister's orphan be born the sacred heir. And this was how the handmaiden — compassionate and ever tender toward the weak — who wept unceasingly for all the world's suffering... Came to don the antlered crown — pure, defiled, and illusory — as though wrapping herself in a cocoon.

Once upon a time, whispered tales spoke of a bloodthirsty spirit amidst the cold forest veiled in frost and mist. Legend told of a malevolent phantom, swift to anger, that spared no one who trespassed the deepwood's bower. Whether they be the overbearing soldiers of the northern realm, or the most raucous bandits of the tundra, All fell a-quiet at the mention of Nephilheim 's desolation. They would instinctively lower their voices, As if fearing that the low hum behind them might be the last sound they would ever hear. Very few knew that the hum came not from some vile spirit, but from the keen edge of a blade wielded by an unknown hunter . The silent hunter was an exile, one whose name appeared in no records and who had never fought for any ideal or banner. But for the children who had lost their homes in those turbulent times and fled to the frigid forest, Clutching a conch as their only token of trust, he simply killed every villain that appeared in those woods. The cold metal of the blade could never mimic the echo of the conch, just like how the past could never be reclaimed. Yet the warmth that bloomed from people's necks was enough to silence the wicked, preserving the children's peaceful dreams. From the days of the gentry and the old Tsar , and through the protracted struggle to reconstruct a new order, The wandering hunter stayed silent, his only constant the whistle that hunted in the cold nights. It was only when the frozen woods were emptied of all the children who had lost a place of refuge, And the aged guardian himself had forgotten how to speak amidst the endless pale nights, Did the hunter finally cast his blade aside. He then turned toward the deepwood and vanished, never to be seen again.

The story begins in our protagonist's youth, long before he was revered as the founder of Qimen Divination , and long before the name " Wind Reader " was known to the world. Back then, he was a mere vagabond wandering the streets, plucking talismans from the air and pouring wine to lay esoteric formations. And through endless banquets and revelry, he earned a name for unbridled boldness. He prided himself on having seen through the cold indifference of the world, viewing the ultimate truths of creation as mere playthings at his fingertips. With his peerless genius, he thought, he was meant to wander the mortal realm aloof while looking upon all its joys and sorrows from afar. So it was that the young thaumaturge drifted across the lands, answering to nothing but his own whims, untethered by notions of good and evil. He did as he pleased, whether it was stealing the bronze mirror of the Two Sages of Lianshan or striking down the bandits who terrorized the hills. This went on until one night when the shrieks of shadow phantasms shattered the peace of a certain mountain village. The young vagabond, who happened to be passing through, summoned wind and rain, thunder and lightning with a casual flick of his wrist, burning the evil spirits to ash. Thus, he slew every demon in his path, and true to his unbridled nature, he proceeded to mock and tease the very villagers he had just saved. But even before the lingering thunder could fade, a sudden flash of silver light descended. Streams of celestial radiance woven into ten thousand jade feathers spilled across the sky, And from the glow, a striking maiden as graceful as a divine swallow appeared, her clear eyes piercing his frivolity. It was the swallow adeptus , later revered as one of the Three Beasts of Tao Dou , and she lamented the youth's squandering of his gifts. Though blessed with a divine foresight capable of calculating the ultimate truths of creation, he had treated it as nothing more than a toy with which to mock the mortal realm. Never before had the arrogant youth suffered such an insult. Drawing his sword, he pointed its tip straight at the high and mighty immortal figure... "Ha! Do you truly think I fear you? Listen well: I was born proud and untamed, and I have roamed the world through ten long frosts. With neither father nor mother, bound by no ties, I have wine, I have flowers, and I have the gleam of my sword. By night, my talisman fire blazes, burning to the stars, a hundred leagues of springtime wind captured in my jar. Name Qimen no false or lesser path, nor mock my sacred vow, for I cultivate the supreme law that rules the cosmos now. Among the blooms I forge my Core, in dreams my true fire gleams. Tipsy with drink, I command the thunder gods, and tease immortal queens. Should I unleash but a fraction of my powers, the Seven Heavens and Four Holy Ones would reel in distress. With a whisper of cosmic pitch and a few paper wards drawn in water, the Jueyun Adepti would feel their very souls shatter! Fair maidens are but cauldrons for my art, and pleasure houses my sacred shrines. Deep in silk-draped chambers, I curse the fleeting dawn; my jade flute rings clear, stirring gale and tempest night. Should you dare block my path, I care not that you are an old hag with graying hair — I will rip out your souls and spirits, bound within my flame, and forge your flesh to gold inside my cauldron's furnace frame!" "Are you done talking?" Her words were quiet, like silver moonlight. Yet, behind them crashed an immortal might that could shatter clouds and split the heavens. Then came the storm of talisman and blade. For all his boast of peerless genius, the young thaumaturge eventually crumbled before the brilliant splendor of the jade feather. Pinned beneath her foot like a beast in a pit, a fire he had never known blazed up in his eyes. Yet the immortal, her silver feathers gleaming like jade, did not flare with rage as he had expected. Instead, she lifted him to his feet... "If your heart's true aim is to do good, why wallow in the squalor of the outlaws? Come, walk the wanderer's path with me. The world is far bigger, and more wondrous, than the mundane sights you have seen." "Why put on this soft act now, you old hag? I am a proud practitioner of the great way, and my hands command the lightning and the thunder, and even devour the stars and the moon! Did you really think that I would ever bow as your servant?" But for all his vicious spatting, the arrogant youth made no move to leave, Not because he had suffered another beating again for calling the immortal "old hag," But because in those cold eyes, he saw a tenderness he had not felt in a long, long time. It felt like a mother's warm embrace as told in the ancient texts, or perhaps... ... "Or perhaps...?" She asked with curious eyes, bathed in the flickering light of the silver lamp. Many years had passed since then. Given his nature, the founder of Qimen Divination should have laughed the question off with some clever, silver-tongued charm. Instead, he found his throat suddenly tight. For all the thousands of words at his command, he could not scrape together a single line of banter. The dim lamp had burned out by the time he came to. Only the untouched wine on his desk and a lingering spirit had remained to keep him company. It's that dream again, he thought. Another year had come and gone, bringing with it the full moon, yet still she had not returned. Then he would keep waiting in his dreams. He would wait on like this and one day... surely, one day...

There are few truly inescapable traps in this world, for even the densest web can be threaded with a needle. Glimmers of hope can be found between the hooks and cages of even a trap set to kill. Just as no one can fully lock away their heart, even the most cautious defenses must eventually falter. To a fae raised in the palace, falsehoods and hypocrisy are far more perilous than tricks and traps. To preserve their ill-gotten wealth, the nobles hid their treasures in countless deadly snares. They believed no one could escape alive, yet the clever fae always found a way. This is because the more complex a structure, the more flaws it contains. Seize the right moment, and all obstacles will fall away. This was how the reputation of the thief known as the Vagabond spread like wildfire. The deception was so complete that no one even suspected his true identity as the noble Nashchokin . He was both a noble, enduring the tedium of court and aristocratic society, and the infamous thief who plundered the guarded treasures of the very lords he laughed and chatted with perhaps just moments before. By right, his life should have been a calm and measured one, untouched by the influence of any other. And yet... "Hey! You sly fox — yes, I mean you. Always hiding in the shadows, huh? If you have the stones, come with me to the Grand Duke's dinner banquet!" "Let's have a contest. Whoever uncovers the duke's secret first wins the mantle of the master thief!" "And don't forget: if you lose, you have to give up the nobles' gold and silver to those who truly need it. That's the way of a true master thief." The fae had meant to avoid all trouble, this included. That changed the moment he saw a young lady at the banquet sneering at the gathered worthies. Her masterful disguise as a distinguished guest had one glaring flaw — her utter lack of pretense. So he accepted Bladebreaker's challenge, but not for the thrill of victory. All he wanted was to glimpse the true nature of a person, a thing so rarely revealed in this world. Cleverer than beating the game was to never play it, and the fae who sidestepped said game always came out ahead. Fuming with humiliation, the young lady refused to concede defeat. This time, her challenge was a personal one: to strip the noble of his greatest honor. She stole the treasure gifted by the Tsaritsa herself, then gave it to the poor children. Surely, victory was at hand. Not far off, the fae chuckled as he quietly returned the ragged children's toy to the gilded display case. The sight of the toy astonished both the young lady and the nobles at the unveiling ceremony, and it was clear who had won. Only this time, the nobles had finally tired of the provocations of the base. And so, they had laid a trap from which there could be no escape. To the problem, the fae saw a simple solution — the thief who stole the treasure and the one who placed the toy inside need not be two people. So, he calmly stepped into the trap and took the blame for them both. His influential family name spared him a public execution, and even secured him a final request. "Please prepare an empty coffin for my burial," the fae finally said after a period of silence. Surprisingly, his request was granted without hesitation. A smile touched the fae's lips, and then he plunged from the high wall into the eternal silence, stealing the final judgment of life and death from the hands of the higher powers. yet the thief known as the Vagabond could not ultimately escape the dark shadow of death. Few secrets last forever, save for those buried deep within the grave... "My dearest friend, I hope you never unravel this mystery in your lifetime."

"Oh, innocent Manechka , against whom shall you clamor tomorrow?" "Oh, high-handed Manechka, why do you smile no longer today?" "Oh, eminent Manechka, did yesterday make you sad?" "Oh, Manechka, you once garrisoned this land." The children of the ash-lands continue to sing that ancient song . They imagine as they sing, and they learn to wield their polearms as the guardian once did. At first, the young girl was a little lone wolf who knew nothing of defending others. She would falsely borrow the guiding one 's name, concealing her hunger and helplessness under haranguing hubris. "If you know this spear, then you know whose name Manechka comes in here!" "A loaf of rye bread with twice the servings of butter and jam! Go on, serve it up, quick!" She succeeded in this venture many times, until the day she encountered the very person whose name she'd falsely taken up, himself feigning a glare of displeasure. The girl apologized in a panic, dividing her spoils in two to seek forgiveness, only for the other party to laugh aloud. "O wolf cub of the snowy plains, enjoy the fruit of your hunt." "There is no need to fear, for you will receive the care you deserve from now on." Later, the young girl would follow the guiding one, casting down injustice and upholding the good with her spear in hand, Sometimes leading a wolf pack that answered her call, defending the ashes with innocent devotion. Then, the brutal acts of the Burner of Cities threatened to raze this land and destroy its people's homes. As the final battle neared, and she prepared to leave alongside the guiding one, she turned and warned the people thus: "Do no evil, and do not wield your power to oppress others. If you do anything that betrays your conscience," "And we hear of it, rest assured, you won't walk free when we get back." The girl who returned alone had to learn how to be a calm alpha wolf, for the sake of the hard-won peace, And for the sake of the guide's last command. She remembered her oath, and would shoulder the burden of defending the people alone. "Such a price she paid! A half-loaf of bread could have settled things at the start, but Manechka let herself be won over by Big Brother's care." "A good trade, that was. This story must be told so that future generations will remember the debt the guide owes." The years of her vigil passed, until the snow-covered land was no longer so full of scars. Until the children had grown up, and their children then bore the story with them as they took root in the earth. "Oh, innocent Manechka, against whom shall you clamor tomorrow?" "Oh, high-handed Manechka, why do you smile no longer today?" "Oh, eminent Manechka, did yesterday make you sad?" "Oh Manechka, the ash-lands will always be your home." They imagine as they sing, and they learn to wield their polearms as the guardian once did. The children of the ash-lands continue to sing that ancient song.

" Kreuzlied , have you ever heard the pipes call out in the dusk?" "Have you heard a voice in the wind sing: farewell, goodbye forever?" "We shall not weep for you, for the night breeze will bear our tears away." "Yes, comrade, it shall bear our tears away." They say that there was once a traveling musical troupe who conspired to assassinate the ruling house . Among them was a renegade noble scion named Kreuzlied. A tune was written for him after the plot failed. His real name was, of course, not "Kreuzlied," and has been lost to time. The word Kreuzlied itself used to mean "The Quartering Song" in the old tongue. In those days when the nights grew long and the dark hung low, quartering was a cruel punishment that left its victims begging for the release of death. Deserters, bandits, rebels, and makers of moonshine would be executed in public in this manner, while the ruling aristocracy basked in their dreadful cries. In those days when one could not see the light of dawn, "Kreuzlied" became a byword for those who rose up and failed. But in this way, it also became the rallying cry for rebellion. The Kreuzlied of the traveling troupe has had their name lost to time, yes. But it matters not, for by then, Kreuzlied had already taken on countless monikers carried on the wind in song: "The Nameless Shepherd ." " Imunlaukr ." " Midnight Rogue ." " Dawnlight ." " Gunnhildr ." " Ragnvindr ." Till at last the final Kreuzlied would awaken from a thousand-year slumber, Answering the small cry of a foreign maiden who had drifted to this land, Just as he had once been born from the wish of a certain youth ... ... The songs that told of Kreuzlied would be fashionable for a time. But in the end, they would leave the lips of men, for in the time after the darkness, there was no longer any need for this name. "Kreuzlied, have you ever seen the horizon turn white?" "Have you heard the maiden sing to the wind: farewell, goodbye forever?" "The morning sun has kissed away my tears, and told me that dawn has broken," "O my lover, the dawn, it has broken."

As the academic world has acknowledged, the script for " Black Snow Swan " is based not only on an original story but also references some folk songs, manuscripts, and other scripts preceding the creation of the Korolevskiy Troupe . The following two scripts are from the Palestar Songbook, which precedes the present day by around 300 years. Their lines, tone, rhythm, and even sentences are almost identical, and it is impossible to tell which was written first. In the second act of "Black Snow Swan," the white snow swan Tatyana's final dance is adapted from one of these passages, with the removal of a sword dance that has nothing to do with ballet (but which commonly appears in ancient fae theater). The original text is published exactly as it is, to ensure complete accuracy and authenticity. ... "White" ... Passage Summary: The Elfking tempts the young woman Tatyana, who has resolved to elope, to murder her lover. ... Tatyana: See you now, my father, the Elfking of renown? Tatyana: The beautiful Elfking, with robe and crown. Tatyana's Father: My daughter, you see naught but the futile wind. Tatyana's Father: Cold it be, but not as human hearts unkind. Tatyana: My father, my father, can you not now hear? Tatyana: The promises the fair Elfking breathes into mine ear? Tatyana's Father: My daughter, you hear the voice that snow and breeze begot. Tatyana's Father: Though cold, it bites not quite so nigh as benefits forgot. Elfking: Such is man, cold-hearted, forgetting favors received. Elfking: As you are also, lovely Tatyana, Elfking: Who for your beloved shall abandon your father. Tatyana: But not my heart, unlike you, venom'd snake, who lavish attention equally to all. Tatyana: For though you wait upon them so, in the end you shall bite their ankles. I will not heed your lies. Tatyana: Yes, I shall elope with my beloved. If you will, report me and my cause aright to my father, Tatyana: And let the rest be silence. Slay me with your sword, if it pleases you! Elfking: Wondrous imagination! Yet to feel fate's cruelty most acutely thereby is to nurse a festering wound. Elfking: You yearn for beautiful sentiment, for pure love, for you have yet to taste its fragrance. Elfking: But say I to you that this stage, though huge, is but a scene in a play. The heavens have long arranged all. Elfking: Once the oath is broken, the skies shall forever be shut. Our lot shall be to struggle and sink within this filthy sludge. Elfking: The bird that should once have belonged in the sky shall have its wings broken, and shall fall to the sullied soil. Is this what you wish for? Tatyana: And what would you know of that? Elfking: That even now, your heart wavers? Elfking: I am you. I know as a matter of course. Tatyana: And what would you have me do? Elfking: Ah, you love him, do you not? Elfking: Love is like a blade that pierces your heart. Will his promise today stand tomorrow? Elfking: See! This sword is purer than his lies. A fine blade, but alas, without a scabbard. Tatyana: You wish for me to... Elfking: Ah! Did I ever say such terrible words? And from whose mouth should I expect thanks? Elfking: I swear now upon my reputation that I meant only to present you this lovely sword, no more, no less. ...

They say the Snegovik came into being with dawn's first gleam of gold, born from the virgin frost upon which the morning star had laid its kiss. Yet their spirits were more desolate than winter itself, and only love could make their broken hearts whole again. When at last the handmaiden of the Azurelight rose from a slumber as deep as death, she still carried within her the warmth of the lord she had served in ages past. For once, there had been a land where people still dared to dream, and those who bore courage and hope within their hearts would lift their eyes to the stars . The Mother of Dawn herself had lifted the curse from her, that her kind might no longer be bound to the fate laid before them. And within that golden dream, even one as small and humble as a speck of snow might find happiness. How could she ever forget? Once, the happiness promised to her had been so very close. But the great golden city had fallen like an avalanche, and all its countless dreams had faded with it into the pale silver of death. Across the bitter frozen wastes wandered the last remnants of that lost kingdom, clinging to life by consuming one another's flesh and blood. The strong trampled the weak beneath their feet, and even the fae faded away like mayflies, to say nothing of mortals, whose lives had been fleeting from the first. "Behold those ravening beasts. Behold what has become of my mother's dream at their hands." "The great city of gold has fallen, fallen at last, until all that remains is a burial ground for things foul and loathsome." "If I alone am left to protect the descendants of my gracious lord, then let blood answer for blood." The first of the Snegovik had never known what love was, yet she purged even those of her own kind who shared her hatred of mankind, And opened her frozen domain without reserve to the mortal clans driven from their homes. Crimson and silver-white alike flowed in rivers, and the cries of the countless dead stained the skirts of her gown, Yet whenever those trembling people raised their eyes to her, she found no love there. Even the king of the Volkodlak , who ruled the shadowed depths of the forest, came himself to beg for a truce, beseeching the merciless, blood-soaked Snegurochka to spare the fae of his kind from further slaughter. He had come prepared to offer tribute and bend the knee, yet never once had he imagined that she would ask him, of all things, what love might be. "This... Surely what you have done is love, Your Grace?" But the blood-soaked mad queen did not lower the long spear in her grasp, and the Volkodlak Lord of Cirnareka could do nothing but speak on. "Love is fear. All things with blood in their veins know fear, for they dread the day when that which they cherish will be taken from them." "You bind your mortals to yourself through fear and keep them as gentle stock. We do the same. By rights, then, there is no reason for us to be enemies..." His words had scarcely left his lips when silver light flashed through the Volkodlak Lord's throat. Many an age of the fae came and went thereafter. Long afterward, a youth still young and unknowing wandered astray amid the driving snow, Until, alongside a company of exiles, he found his way into her realm. She knew his lineage at a glance and, without further ado, accepted him as her pupil. Amid the scant moments of rest his relentless training permitted, the master who had spent so long teaching him to love unexpectedly asked what he believed love to be. "Me? You... you're asking me?" "I don't know. But I think love is bearing one another's burdens and granting one another forgiveness. You taught me that yourself, didn't you, Master?" "To build a land that may once again dare to dream, we must share not only in its splendor, but in every hardship that comes with it." "In a kingdom of love, none should be left to suffer alone. Only if we carry one another's burdens and face tomorrow together can we... Gah!" His words had scarcely left his lips when silver light struck the stone beside his feet. Thus did the successor of her choosing finally depart, setting forth upon the journey that would live on in song and story for ages to come. And when at last the noise she had grown so weary of faded away, the scarlet Knyazhna of Blood found that the longing within her heart had grown fainter with it. Her Lady and Mother had stripped from her the curse that once moored her to destiny, but she had never found another bond by which to remain in the world, And a soul severed from all that bound it here was like fading snow, destined one day to dissolve without a sound into the passing wind. For the first time, the first of the Snegovik, dreaded by countless mortals and fae alike, felt a fear deeper than any she had ever known. Ahh... if no more blood is shed, will the day not come when even I forget the dream Mother once cherished? Slaughter, slaughter, slaughter there must be, in which her soul might sink ever deeper into that blood-soaked mire, lest it too grow pale and vanish with the passing wind... Thus did the remnant of a fallen kingdom, whose life endured like a winter night, cross paths with one as fleeting as the dew at dawn.

Marvelous Splendor: After unlocking the Ascension Talent "Spring Rite of the Chosen One," Odette will obtain a special effect when she summons her Solo Dance Double. Every stack of Marvelous Splendor active increases the character's Stellar Glimmer DMG by 15%. This lasts until her Dance Double exits the field or when she summons her Solo Dance Double again. When Odette is off-field, she loses 1 stack of Marvelous Splendor every second, while other nearby party members gain the corresponding number of Marvelous Splendor stacks at the same time.
Radiance: Stellar Glimmer: Radiance: Stellar-Conduct and Radiance: Stellar Swirl are both considered Radiance: Stellar Glimmer states. Characters can only be affected by one Radiance state at any one time, and where more than one state can be triggered, Radiance: Stellar-Conduct shall apply first.
Solo Dance Double: A psychic double of Odette's that dances a duet with her. May be summoned to the field through her Elemental Skill or Elemental Burst. Alternates between the Plume and Wing dance moves to periodically attack nearby opponents, dealing AoE Cryo DMG . A maximum of one Solo Dance Double summoned by Odette is allowed on the field at any one time. Additionally, when there is a Dance Double summoned by Odette nearby, her Elemental Skill Adagio: Phantom Night Dancers is changed to the special Elemental Skill Adagio: Coda at Dawn's Tolling.

When the Frostgrove Sanctuary attacks opponents, it will deal 1 additional instance of AOE Dendro DMG equal to 185% of Lauma's Elemental Mastery . This DMG is considered Lunar-Bloom DMG. This instance of DMG will not consume any Pale Hymn stacks and will provide Lauma with 2 stacks of Pale Hymn, as well as refreshing the duration of Pale Hymn stacks gained in this manner. This effect can occur up to 8 times during each Frostgrove Sanctuary. When using the Elemental Skill Runo: Dawnless Rest of Karsikko , all Pale Hymn stacks gained in this manner will be removed. Additionally, when Lauma uses a Normal Attack while she has Pale Hymn stacks, she will consume 1 stack to convert this to deal Dendro DMG equal to 150% of her Elemental Mastery. This DMG is considered Lunar-Bloom DMG. Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam : All nearby party members' Lunar-Bloom DMG is elevated by 25%.

Adagio: Coda at Dawn's Tolling: Odette's special Elemental Skill, which deals to nearby opponents AoE Cryo DMG over time. Then, when the dance duel ends, she deals another instance of AoE Cryo DMG that is considered Stellar-Conduct DMG. During the dance duet, Odette can control the direction of the dance steps. Radiance: Stellar Glimmer: The DMG dealt when the dance duet ends is changed to AoE Cryo DMG of the corresponding Stellar reaction type. Additionally, after Odette unleashes the special Elemental Skill Adagio: Coda at Dawn's Tolling, should she be in the Radiance: Stellar Glimmer state while her Dance Double is still on the field, the Dance Double's two dance move types will also deal additional AoE Cryo DMG of the corresponding Stellar Glimmer reaction type.
Solo Dance Double: A psychic double of Odette's that dances a duet with her. May be summoned to the field through her Elemental Skill or Elemental Burst. Alternates between the Plume and Wing dance moves to periodically attack nearby opponents, dealing AoE Cryo DMG . A maximum of one Solo Dance Double summoned by Odette is allowed on the field at any one time. Additionally, when there is a Dance Double summoned by Odette nearby, her Elemental Skill Adagio: Phantom Night Dancers is changed to the special Elemental Skill Adagio: Coda at Dawn's Tolling.
Marvelous Splendor: After unlocking the Ascension Talent "Spring Rite of the Chosen One," Odette will obtain a special effect when she summons her Solo Dance Double. Every stack of Marvelous Splendor active increases the character's Stellar Glimmer DMG by 15%. This lasts until her Dance Double exits the field or when she summons her Solo Dance Double again. When Odette is off-field, she loses 1 stack of Marvelous Splendor every second, while other nearby party members gain the corresponding number of Marvelous Splendor stacks at the same time.

blocks.text: Pale Hymn: A hymn passed down by generations of Moonchanters that increases the DMG dealt by Bloom, Hyperbloom, Burgeon, and Lunar-Bloom reactions. Lauma can gain Pale Hymn stacks in the following ways: When using her Elemental Burst Runo: All Hearts Become the Beating Moon. When consuming Moon Song stacks due to using her Elemental Burst Runo: All Hearts Become the Beating Moon. When the Frostgrove Sanctuary triggers the effect of her Constellation "I Offer Blood and Tears to the Moonlight". When party members deal Bloom, Hyperbloom, Burgeon, or Lunar-Bloom DMG, 1 stack of Pale Hymn will be consumed and the DMG dealt will be increased based on Lauma's Elemental Mastery. If this DMG hits multiple opponents at once, then multiple stacks of Pale Hymn will be consumed, depending on how many opponents are hit. The duration for each stack of Pale Hymn is counted independently.

Lumi: Strike Forms: Lumi has three different Strike Forms. Super Power Form Lumi will use Pound-Pound Pummeler to attack nearby opponents continuously. Every attack will deal 2 instances of AoE Geo DMG . If there are Moondrifts nearby, Lumi will alternate between Pound-Pound Pummeler and Heavy Overdrive Hammer to continuously attack nearby opponents . Heavy Overdrive Hammer will deal AoE Geo DMG which will be considered Lunar-Crystallize Reaction DMG. Ultimate Power Form Lumi will use the ultimate Million Ton Crush, dealing an especially powerful instance of AoE Geo DMG that is considered Lunar-Crystallize Reaction DMG, switching to Standard Power Form. Standard Power Form It might not be as flashy as the other forms, but it still packs a serious punch. Lumi will use Pound-Pound Pummeler at longer intervals to attack nearby opponents continuously. Every attack will deal 2 instances of AoE Geo DMG .

Name: Stellar Glimmer Reaction
Type: Combat Game Systems
Group: Elemental Reactions
Stellar Glimmer Reactions are a subset of Elemental Reactions .
In order to trigger a Stellar Glimmer Reaction , a character with a passive talent that converts specific Cryo -related elemental reactions must be present in the party .
Stellar Glimmer reactions will also interrupt a specific attack from Snowland Fae and Aberrant Chimeric Monsters .

- Stellar-Conduct
- Stellar Swirl
1 Artifact Set increase Stellar Glimmer Reaction DMG:

rows: 2-Piece: ATK increased by 18%. 4-Piece: Increases the equipping character's ATK by 12% for 12s when they trigger a Stellar Glimmer reaction or deal Stellar Glimmer reaction DMG. Also increases Stellar Glimmer reaction DMG dealt by all nearby party members by 50%. The above effects can trigger even when the equipping character is not on the field, and the DMG bonus from multiple Artifact Sets with the same name do not stack.

rows: Viper's Ballad Increases Energy Recharge by 20 ~ 40 %. When the equipping character hits the opponent with their Elemental Skill or Elemental Burst , they gain a stack of "Hymn of the Pure." This effect can trigger once every 0.03s, max 3 stacks, and at 3 stacks, all instances of "Hymn of the Pure" are cleared to give the equipping character "Thus Lied the Viper" instead. This grants nearby party members a 24 ~ 48 % Stellar Glimmer reaction DMG boost for 12s, during which no stacks of "Hymn of the Pure" can be obtained. The aforementioned effects can still trigger even when the equipping character is not on the field.

Echo of a Vow Triggering an Elemental Reaction increases the equipping character's Elemental Mastery by 60 ~ 120 for 12s, while triggering a Stellar Glimmer reaction increases their Stellar Glimmer reaction DMG dealt by 16 ~ 32 % for 12s. The aforementioned effects can trigger even when the character is not on the field.

Starfire Upon the Snowplains Triggering an Elemental Reaction increases the equipping character's ATK by 16 ~ 32 % for 12s. Triggering a Stellar Glimmer reaction increases their Stellar Glimmer reaction DMG dealt by 16 ~ 32 % for 12s. The aforementioned effects can trigger even when the character is not on the field.

Day and Night in Counterpoint Every 10s, the equipping character plays a "Harmonic Movement" of the corresponding type for a boost in the following order: + 18 ~ 36 % ATK > + 120 ~ 240 Elemental Mastery > + 28 ~ 56 % Stellar Glimmer reaction DMG. Each instance of Harmonic Movement lasts 10s. This effect can trigger even when the equipping character is not on the field. Triggering a Stellar Glimmer reaction will also grant an additional 12-second instance of "Harmonic Movement: Contrapuntal" with the same effects as the Harmonic Movement active when Stellar Glimmer is triggered. This effect stacks with the original Harmonic Movement effect, and can trigger once every 12s.

Wildgrowth When the equipping character hits the opponent with an attack within 12s after using the Elemental Skill , they gain the "Verdant" effect, which increases their ATK by 4 ~ 8 % and their Elemental Mastery by 20 ~ 40 . This effect lasts 6s and can trigger once every second. Max 3 stacks. The aforementioned effects can still trigger even when the equipping character is not on the field. Radiance: Stellar Glimmer: The effect of "Verdant" is changed to: Increases ATK by 6 ~ 12 % as well as Stellar Glimmer reaction DMG dealt by the equipping character by 8 ~ 16 %.

Secrets of Frost The equipping character gains "Silver-Tinged Blood Pact": The equipping character's Elemental Mastery is increased by 24 ~ 48 for every Cryo character present in the party. For every Electro character present in the party, the equipping character's ATK is increased by 4.8 ~ 9.6 %. Up to 4 Cryo or Electro characters can provide the above buffs. Name: Stellar Swirl
Type: Elemental Reactions
Group: Stellar Glimmer Reactions

Stellar Swirl is the Stellar Glimmer Reaction triggered by inflicting Anemo on a target that is already affected by Cryo , replacing Cryo Swirl while a character with a corresponding Stellar Jubilee Passive is in the party . This reaction deals Anemo DMG and creates a Stellar Vortex that will explode after a period of time, dealing Cryo DMG . If Stellar Swirl is triggered with a Vortex nearby, its level will raise, causing it to deal increased DMG in a larger AoE.
Main article: Damage § Stellar Glimmer Reaction Damage

When Stellar Swirl is triggered, an instance of Anemo DMG is dealt to the target opponent, and then a Lv. 1 Stellar Vortex is created that lasts for 3s . Stellar Vortices will explode after a delay, dealing AoE Cryo DMG . After triggering Stellar Swirl for the third time, the Vortex will level up to Lv. 2, after which it will deal greater DMG across a wider AoE upon bursting. If Stellar Swirl is triggered three more times, the Vortex will explode immediately.
Additionally, for 5s after a Stellar Vortex explodes, the player's next jump will have its height increased.

Elemental Reaction: Stellar Swirl:
- When Anemo meets Cryo , and certain other conditions are met, a special Stellar Swirl reaction is triggered. This deals an instance of Anemo DMG to the opponent and generates a Stellar Vortex. Triggering Stellar Swirl multiple times raises the level of the Stellar Vortex, which explodes after a certain time or after a certain number of Stellar Swirl reactions have been triggered. This deals AoE Cryo DMG to nearby opponents. The aforementioned DMG can CRIT. Up to one Stellar Vortex can exist on the field within a certain range. A Stellar Vortex on the field will level up to Lv. 2 after a certain number of Stellar Swirl reactions have been triggered. A higher-level Vortex deals more AoE Cryo DMG to opponents over a wider area when it explodes.
After a Stellar Swirl reaction is triggered, certain nearby characters will also enter the Radiance: Stellar Swirl effect for 8s, which enhances certain Talents and skill effects. Certain characters can use their Talents to deal Stellar Swirl reaction DMG to opponents. This DMG can trigger CRIT Hits. When the Stellar Vortex explodes, it will also grant nearby characters the ability to jump higher once, for a short time.

Name: Stellar-Conduct
Type: Elemental Reactions
Group: Stellar Glimmer Reactions

Stellar-Conduct is the Stellar Glimmer Reaction triggered by inflicting Cryo on a target that is already affected by Electro or vice versa, replacing Superconduct while a character with a corresponding Stellar Jubilee Passive is in the party . After triggering a Stellar-Conduct reaction, a Starlight Prism will be created, briefly transforming the surrounding area into a Polestar Field. The Polestar Field increases the base reaction coefficient of the Stellar-Conduct reaction, grants Cryo and Electro DMG Bonus to the party, and reduces the Physical RES of all enemies. Hitting enemies within the field with Cryo or Electro attacks will store the energy and grant buffs to the party.

After Stellar-Conduct is triggered, the resulting Starlight Prism lasts for 7s and will continuously sustain a Polestar Field around it. Inside the field, hits from Cryo and Electro attacks on enemies that apply an element (as limited by Internal Cooldown ) are recorded by the Prism. The initial hit that created the Prism is not included. Every 4s, the count is reset, and buffs lasting 4s are granted based on the number of hits recorded:

- If at least 1 Cryo or Electro hit is recorded, the Base Reaction Coefficient for Stellar-Conduct (which starts at 1) is increased by 40% plus an additional 5% for each recorded hit, up to a maximum of 12 hits.
- Characters inside the field have their Cryo and Electro DMG Bonus increased by 20%. If at least 1 Cryo or Electro hit is included, Cryo and Electro DMG Bonus is instead increased by 28% plus an additional 1% for each recorded hit, up to a maximum of 12 hits.
- All enemies in the field have their Physical RES reduced by 40%.
- Characters inside the field will not lose any heat or Kresnik Energy in the Snezhnayan open world. Additionally, if the character's Kresnik Energy is below 30%, it will immediately be restored to 30%.
- Prime Ice Constructs and firearms will receive certain buffs while inside a Polestar Field (see Prime Ice Construct Archive and individual firearm pages).

In the Snezhnayan open world, if a Starlight Prism exists while the player is not in combat, it will turn into a Prism Mirage after its duration expires, which the player can interact with to reactivate it. Reactivated Starlight Prisms last indefinitely and have the same properties as Prime Ice Constructs , meaning they have placement limits, can appear as co-op constructs , and can receive likes. Reactivated Starlight Prisms can be removed by interacting with them or via the "Manage Prime Ice Constructs" feature on the map .
Main article: Damage § Stellar Glimmer Reaction Damage

Stellar-Conduct does no DMG on its own. The only way to deal Stellar-Conduct DMG is through character Talents and Constellations. The DMG dealt can be either Cryo or Electro , depending on the Talent or Constellation that dealt it.

Elemental Reaction: Stellar-Conduct:
- When Cryo comes in contact with Electro , a special Stellar-Conduct reaction will be triggered if certain conditions are also met. When this happens, a Starlight Prism is generated, and the surrounding area turns into a wondrous Polestar Field for a short period of time. All characters inside the Polestar Field receive a Cryo and Electro DMG Bonus, and when opponents within the field are hit by Cryo or Electro attacks, the field will store the dissipating elemental energies and then completely release them every 4s. This further increases the aforementioned DMG Bonus and also increases the Base Stellar-Conduct DMG coefficient for 4s. Additionally, opponents within the Polestar Field will also have their Physical RES lowered. Certain characters will also gain the effects of Radiance: Stellar-Conduct when within the Polestar Field, enhancing certain Talents and skill effects. Certain characters can deal Stellar-Conduct DMG to opponents using their Talents, and this DMG can trigger CRIT Hits.

Starlight Prism:
- In certain places in Snezhnaya , a Starlight Prism will also generate a Prism Mirage that lasts for a short time at the same location when it vanishes. Approach the mirage to activate the Starlight Prism again, at which point it will remain on the field permanently. Prisms activated by such interactions have a chance to appear in other Travelers' worlds. Similarly, Prisms from other Travelers' worlds may also appear in your world. In certain places in Snezhnaya, the Polestar Field also presents with additional capabilities: · When inside a Polestar Field, the Eye of Graeae will not lose any energy. If the Eye's energy level is below 30%, it will also be immediately restored to 30%. · It also appears that Prime Ice Constructs inside a Polestar Field will gain various wondrous buffs...

"Stellar-Conduct" and Firearms...:
- When inside a Polestar Field created by the Stellar-Conduct reaction, you will also get additional buffs with certain firearms.

Polestar Field: When Stellar-Conduct is triggered, the surrounding area will transform into a Polestar Field for a short period of time, and when inside a Polestar Field, certain characters will enter the Radiance: Stellar-Conduct state, which grants various skill buffs.
Solo Dance Double: A psychic double of Odette's that dances a duet with her. May be summoned to the field through her Elemental Skill or Elemental Burst. Alternates between the Plume and Wing dance moves to periodically attack nearby opponents, dealing AoE Cryo DMG . A maximum of one Solo Dance Double summoned by Odette is allowed on the field at any one time. Additionally, when there is a Dance Double summoned by Odette nearby, her Elemental Skill Adagio: Phantom Night Dancers is changed to the special Elemental Skill Adagio: Coda at Dawn's Tolling.
Marvelous Splendor: After unlocking the Ascension Talent "Spring Rite of the Chosen One," Odette will obtain a special effect when she summons her Solo Dance Double. Every stack of Marvelous Splendor active increases the character's Stellar Glimmer DMG by 15%. This lasts until her Dance Double exits the field or when she summons her Solo Dance Double again. When Odette is off-field, she loses 1 stack of Marvelous Splendor every second, while other nearby party members gain the corresponding number of Marvelous Splendor stacks at the same time.
Adagio: Coda at Dawn's Tolling: Odette's special Elemental Skill, which deals to nearby opponents AoE Cryo DMG over time. Then, when the dance duel ends, she deals another instance of AoE Cryo DMG that is considered Stellar-Conduct DMG. During the dance duet, Odette can control the direction of the dance steps. Radiance: Stellar Glimmer : The DMG dealt when the dance duet ends is changed to AoE Cryo DMG of the corresponding Stellar reaction type. Additionally, after Odette unleashes the special Elemental Skill Adagio: Coda at Dawn's Tolling, should she be in the Radiance: Stellar Glimmer state while her Dance Double is still on the field, the Dance Double's two dance move types will also deal additional AoE Cryo DMG of the corresponding Stellar Glimmer reaction type.
Radiance: Stellar Glimmer: Radiance: Stellar-Conduct and Radiance: Stellar Swirl are both considered Radiance: Stellar Glimmer states. Characters can only be affected by one Radiance state at any one time, and where more than one state can be triggered, Radiance: Stellar-Conduct shall apply first.
Decoding Power: When in Decoding mode, Fagio's Decoding Power will continuously increase. When its Decoding Power reaches the maximum, Fagio will be unable to maintain or re-enter Decoding mode.
Decoding: Fagio will switch to this mode when using a Charged Attack. When in this mode, Fagio will engage any opponents ahead with a sweeping fire attack, as well as fire condensed beams at intervals, dealing AoE Cryo DMG . Radiance: Stellar Glimmer : The condensed beams will instead deal AoE Cryo DMG that is considered the corresponding Stellar Glimmer DMG.
